## Introduction to Cash Management
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 13*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Introduction to Cash Management 

Use the Cash Management application to manage corporate cash accounts—including checking, savings, and 

credit card accounts—from a central location. As a cloud-based application, users can work cooperatively 

regardless of their geographic location. For example, even if your headquarters are in the East, regional offices in 

other global areas can enter their own credit card transactions and reconcile them. 

With the Cash Management application, you can: 

• 
Make manual payments. Cash Management allows you to step outside the normal Accounts Payable 

workflow and make a one-time payment. You record the payment and create a corresponding A/P invoice 

all in one step, and payment can be by check, cash, credit card, or funds transfer. 

• 
Record funds transfers. Cash Management smoothly handles the transfer of funds from one cash account to 

another. You can examine the cash balance report to verify the balances of your accounts to determine if 

you need to make a transfer, or if there are sufficient funds that you can transfer. 

• 
Receive payments. Cash Management allows you to receive payments that are not tracked to customer 

invoices, even if you do not subscribe to the Accounts Receivable (A/R) application. You can also use this 

feature even if you do use the A/R application and have customers. For example, for counter sales you do 

not want to track to A/R customers, enter the source of the payment here. You have the choice of depositing 

the receipts either directly into a bank, or into your undeposited funds account for later deposit. 

• 
Make deposits. You can deposit payments that you receive in two ways: 

• 
If you have already deposited the payment, then the receipts function records both the receipt of 

payment and its deposit. 

• 
You can receive payments, accumulating them in an undeposited funds account for later deposit, at 

which point you create a “deposit slip,” which then posts the amounts of the deposits. 

• 
Record and pay off credit card charges. There are two ways to pay off a credit card: 

• 
Full A/P cycle: You can create a payment request, which is then reviewed and approved before you 

print a check. 

• 
Funds transfer: You can transfer funds from a bank account to a credit card account, which performs 

the process automatically. 

• 
Reconcile cash accounts. You can reconcile all checking, savings, and credit card accounts. Upon your first 

reconciliation, you enter initial open items, enter the statement ending balance and bank charges, and then 

select all of the items that have cleared. 

• 
Run Cash Management reports. Reports include bank, check, deposits, and credit card registers, along with 

a cash balances report. The registers allow you to navigate to the details quickly and conveniently. 

• 
Print out remittance information for your vendors or true payment copy information for your files. You 

can remove or include the “File Copy” watermark when you print remittance information, depending on the 

intended purpose of the payment copy information. Do this directly from the Print payment copies page. 

B O O K I

#### Escheatment Workbench Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

Escheatment Workbench 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Escheatment Workbench Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Escheatment Workbench`


The Escheatment workbench in Cash Management allows you to manage and report on the 

escheatment process. Use this workbench to mark uncollected payments as “aged payables” and 

escheat invoices. Marking an invoice as an aged payable will void the payment and transfer the 

amount of the payable into a G/L account to be escheated. Aged payables cannot be paid; 

however, you can revert an aged payable back to a posted or paid invoice if you need to pay it. 

When the funds for an aged payable have been transferred to the state, you can mark the invoice 

as escheated. 

The workbench contains the following components: 

a) Views: Filters the list of transactions in the workbench by the selected transaction type.  

b) Filters: Filters transactions by the selected criteria. Filter options vary by transaction type. 

c) Actions: Allows you to perform actions on selected transactions, such as marking payments 

as aged payables or escheating invoices.  

d) Transactions: Displays a list of transactions matching the selected filters. The columns and 

actions vary by transaction type. See Using Workbenches for more information. 

Under certain conditions, an invoice will not appear in the Escheatment workbench. This includes:  

• 
Multi-entity invoices 

• 
Invoices paid multiple times using different checks 

• 
Invoices with the same vendor and location paid using the Merge vendor option 

• 
Reconciled invoices

##### Filtering the Escheatment Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 28*

Escheatment Workbench 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Filtering the Escheatment Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Escheatment Workbench`


The Escheatment workbench displays four types of transactions: 

• 
Posted invoices: These are invoices that have been posted to the General Ledger. 

• 
Paid invoices: These are confirmed, printed checks. This includes top-level and entity-level 

payments, but not payments for multiple entities. 

• 
Aged payables: These are invoices that have been marked as an “aged payable”. This 

includes top-level and entity-level A/P invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices.  

• 
Escheated: These are invoices that have been marked as “escheated” and transferred to the 

state. This includes top-level and entity-level A/P invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices. 

You can apply additional filters to find and target specific invoices. The filter options are slightly 

different depending on which transaction type you select. 

You must enter a date range to populate transactions in the workbench. 

Filtering Posted Invoices 

To filter posted invoices: 

1. 
Select the Posted invoices radio button. 

2. 
Define one or more filter options: 

• 
From date / To date: Type or select a range of dates to include in the list. For posted 

invoices, this is based on the Invoice date. 

• 
Invoice no.: Type a specific invoice number. 

• 
Vendor address state: Select the U.S. state for the vendor that was paid. This is the 

state listed on the Mailing information tab of the Pay to contact record. 

The system ignores capitalization in the contact record when filtering. If the Pay to 
contact does not have a State, then the payment or invoice will not display in the 
workbench. 

• 
Property: Select a specific property. 

• 
Bank account: Select a specific bank account. 

• 
Vendor: Select a specific vendor. 

• 
Vendor type: Select the category of vendor.  

3. 
Click the Apply button to apply the filters. 

A list of posted invoices matching the filter criteria appears. 

---

##### Marking an Invoice as an Aged Payable
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 31*

Chapter 1: Escheatment Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Marking an Invoice as an Aged Payable 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Escheatment Workbench > Create Aged 
Payable`


When an invoice is marked as an “aged payable,” the funds are transferred into the escheatment 

account (Aged payable account) defined on the Configure Cash Management page. The funds 

are held in this account as unclaimed assets until it is time to transfer the funds to the state. If the 

invoice was a paid invoice, then the original payment is voided. 

To mark an invoice as an aged payable: 

1. 
Select the Posted invoices or Paid invoices radio button. 

2. 
Type or select a From date and To date to filter the invoices by a specific date range.  

The dates correspond with the Invoice date if it’s a posted invoice or the Payment date if 
it’s a paid invoice. 

3. 
Set additional filters (on page 15) as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. 

A list of invoices matching the filter criteria appears. 

5. 
Select the check box next to the invoice(s) you want to mark as an aged payable. 

6. 
In the Aged payable date field, type the date you want to post the aged payable journal 

entry to the General Ledger. By default, this field uses today’s date. 

7. 
In the Void date field, type the date you want to void the original payment. By default, this 

field uses today’s date. 

This field applies only to paid invoices. 

8. 
Type a brief Memo to record in the G/L journal entry. If you don’t enter a memo, the 

Description from the journal entry will be used instead. This includes the invoice number, 

vendor ID, and vendor name. If it’s a paid invoice, it also includes the check number and 

payment date. 

9. 
Click the Create aged payable button. 

---

The system creates a journal entry for each payment in the Aged payable (APJE) system 

journal. The Status of each invoice changes to Aged payable, and the invoice(s) will appear 

in the workbench as Aged payable transactions. If the invoice was a paid invoice, then the 

original payment is voided. 

Configuring an Escheatment Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration`


You can set up an escheatment account in Cash Management to hold the unclaimed funds of 

aged payables. The funds will remain as unclaimed assets for your company for a period of time 

before you escheat the invoice and transfer the funds to the state. 

To designate an escheatment account: 

1. 
On the Configure cash management page, find the Escheatment section.

Reverting an Aged Payable to a Posted or Paid Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Escheatment Workbench > Aged Payable > 
Reverse`


Aged payables cannot be edited, reversed, or reclassified. However, you can revert the status of 

an invoice so that it’s no longer marked as an Aged payable. Reverting the status will also reverse 

the original journal entry. 

To revert the status of an aged payable: 

1. 
Select the Aged payable radio button. 

2. 
Type or select a From date and To date to filter the transactions by a specific date range. 

For aged payables, the dates correspond with the Invoice date. 

3. 
Set additional filters (on page 15) as needed. 

4.

A list of invoices matching the filter criteria appears. 

5. 
Select the check box next to the aged payable you want to revert.

Change the Reversal date if needed.

#### Bank Accounts List

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide

Bank Accounts List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Bank Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts`


Use the Bank accounts list to view and manage your company’s bank accounts. From this list, you 

can: 

• 
Add a new bank account. 

• 
View or edit an existing bank account. 

• 
Delete a bank account. 

• 
View pending bank reconciliations. 

• 
Start the process of reconciling an account. 

• 
View a list of reconciliation events associated with an account. 

Bank Accounts in Multi-Entity Shared Companies  

Bank accounts can either be common to all entities, or exclusive to a specific entity. 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you can create bank accounts at 

both the root and entity levels. Create the bank account at the top level if you want to use it for 

inter-entity transactions. Always reconcile a bank account at the same level in which you created 

it. In addition, assign it a unique General Ledger account and a location. When you are at the top 

level, select the Include private check box to view entity-level banks. When you are at the entity 

level, both entity-level banks and top-level banks are available. 

If you do not see the Include private check box on your page, verify that you are not using a 
custom view.

Adding a Bank Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > 
 Bank Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > 
 Bank Accounts`


Adding a bank account includes entering details about the account, such as your bank name, the 

journals and other accounts you want to map to, and how you want to print checks and pay your 

vendors. 

Entering the Bank Account Details 

In the Financial institution section, fill in the required information. 

1. 
In the Account type field, select whether you want to create a checking or savings account. 

2. 
In the Account ID field, type a unique number to identify the checking account. 

3. 
In the Account number field, type the 10-digit number found at the bottom of the check. 

4. 
In the Bank name field, type the bank name. If you have more than one account at this 

bank, include a description in the name. 

5. 
In the Name on the account field, type the official name that the bank has on file for the 

checking account. 

6. 
In the Routing number field, type the 9-digit number printed at the bottom of the check if 

you are printing on blank check stock. Otherwise, leave this field blank. 

7. 
In the Branch ID field, type the number found at the top of the check, above the date field. 

8. 
In the Address 1, Address 2, City/Town, State/Territory, Zip code/Post code, and Country 

fields, type your bank’s address. 

---


<!-- Page 46 -->
Search & Find 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

9. 
In the Phone number field, type the phone number of your bank branch. 

10. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether the account is Active or Inactive. 

11. 
In the Currency field, select a default currency for the bank account. 

This field appears only in multi-currency companies. 

In the Accounting information section, fill in the required information. 

1. 
In the Default bank G/L account drop-down list, select an account from the General Ledger. 

How you assign G/L accounts determines where and how an account can be used. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 
find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

2. 
In the Bank G/L account field, click the Select link to choose alternate G/L accounts. You can 

select an unlimited number of alternate G/L accounts. Activity from these accounts appears 

in the bank reconciliation and is included in the bank balance. 

3. 
In the Default payables G/L journal drop-down list, select a journal to record payments and 

transfers out of the account. The default is the same journal used for Accounts Payable 

payments. 

4. 
In the Default receivables G/L journal drop-down list, select a journal to record deposits 

and transfers into the account. The default is the same journal used for Accounts Payable 

payments. 

5. 
In the Service charge G/L account drop-down list, select an account to post service charges 

and other fees to during reconciliation. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 
find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

6. 
In the Interest earned G/L account drop-down list, select an account to post interest to 

during reconciliation. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 
find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

7. 
In the Department ID drop-down list, select the default department for G/L posting. If your 

company does not use departments, then this field is not displayed. 

8. 
In the Location ID drop-down list, select the default location for G/L posting. Depending on 

your company, the location ID may be required to force the system to balance the 

associated journal entries. 

9. 
Select the Disable inter-entity transfers check box to exclude the account from inter-entity 

transfers, even if you have globally enabled inter-entity transfers for the entire structure.

10. 
In the bottom section, select whether to enable the bank account for specific third-party 

payment services enabled on the Configure Cash Management page. 

• 
Enable for RealPage Payments or third party payments: Select this check box to allow 

the bank account to be used for RealPage Payments or third-party payments. This 

option is available for both checking and saving accounts. 

If you enable the bank account for third-party payments, then the system displays 
the bank account in the payment options when you pay A/P invoices. 

• 
Enable for RealPage Debit Card, Virtual Refund or PC Reimbursement payments: 

Select this check box to allow the bank account to be used for RealPage Debit Card 

payments, RealPage Virtual Refunds, or petty cash (PC) reimbursements. This is 

required in order to process payments and reimbursements. 

• 
Select which Bank account type should be refunded for these types of payments 

and reimbursements. 

• 
Select the Override MID and LID check boxes if you want to use a bank account 

other than the property’s operating bank account for RealPage Debit Card 

payments, PC reimbursements, or RealPage Virtual Refunds. An implementation 

consultant will help set this up. If you choose to override MID and LID for 

RealPage Debit Card payments, then the system will not run a validation check 

with ResidentDirect. 

When RealPage Debit Card payments or PC reimbursement payments are enabled for 
a bank account, RealPage Accounting automatically validates whether the location 
associated with the bank account is set up in ResidentDirect, a bill payment service 
offered by RealPage Payments Services (RPPS). If the location is not in 
ResidentDirect, then you will receive an error message when you try to save. If this 
occurs, contact your account representative for more information.  

Setting Your Check Printing Preferences 

On the Check printing tab: 

1. 
Select a Print on option to determine how you want to print checks. 

• 
Pre-printed check stock: This option requires you to order check stock in advance, 

using separate check stock for each checking account, and printing from one checking 

account at a time. Print checks in U. S. and Canadian dollars only. 

• 
Blank check stock: This option requires MICR ink and a printer that supports the ink, 

and coordinating alignment of check details with your bank. Print checks in U. S., 

Canadian, or Mexican currency. 

• 
Disable check printing from this account: Select this option to disable check printing. 

2. 
Select the Print company address check box to print a company address on your checks.

Restricting Bank Accounts 

The ability to restrict bank accounts by entity is a configuration option that your system 
administrator can turn on in a multi-entity shared environment. See Entity Restrictions for 
more information. 

If you create a bank account at the entity level, then it is already restricted to that entity, and 
the Restrictions tab does not appear. Similarly, if you create a bank account at the entity level of 
a parent entity, it is not accessible to the parent entity ’s child entities/locations. If you want to 
apply location restrictions and allow child locations to access a bank account, you must create 
the bank account at the top level. 

1. 
Select a restriction option: 

• 
Unrestricted: This option makes the account available to the top-level company and 

all entity-level locations. This is the default. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: This option makes the account inaccessible to entity-level 

locations. 

• 
Restricted: This option makes the account accessible to locations or location groups 

that you specify. 

2. 
If you select the Restricted option, click the Select button, and then use the multi-select box 

to choose one or more locations or location groups that can access the bank account. For 

instructions using the selection box, see Using the multi-select box. 

To save this account and create another, click the More actions drop-down menu, and then select 

Save & new. 

To save this account and go back to the Checking accounts list, click the Save button. 

---

Bank Account Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Bank Accounts > Add, View, 
or Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts > Add, View, or 
Edit`


The Bank account information page allows you to add, view, or edit details about your checking 

and savings accounts and map journals and accounts to them. This page contains the following 

tabs: 

• 
Details: Use this tab to enter details about your bank account and then map G/L journal and 

accounts to it. 

• 
Check printing: Use this tab to set check printing options for checking accounts. 

• 
ACH setup or Electronic payments setup: Use this tab to set up standard ACH payments or 

foreign electronic payments to vendors. 

• 
Restrictions: Use this tab to restrict a bank account to one or more entities or locations. 

Printing Wiring Instructions for Bank Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Bank Accounts > View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts > View`


You can print instructions for wire transfers directly from a bank account record to share them 

with vendors and partners. The wiring instructions include the following information: 

• 
Internal bank ID: This is the unique identifier assigned to the bank account in RealPage 

Accounting. 

• 
Account holder name: This is the name and address of the individual or entity who owns 

the funds . 

• 
Bank account #: This is the bank account number. 

• 
Bank name: This is the name of the financial institution holding the funds. 

• 
Incoming wire ABA: This is the nine-digit ABA routing number that directs the funds to the 

correct financial institution. 

To print instructions for wire transfers: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2.

Restricting a Bank Account to One or More Entities/Locations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Bank Accounts > Edit > 
Restrictions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts > Edit > 
Restrictions`


In a shared multi-entity company, you can restrict an account to specific entities or locations to 

prevent entities from paying bills out of the wrong bank account. The ability to restrict bank 

accounts by entity is a configuration option that your system administrator can turn on in a 

multi-entity shared environment. See Entity Restrictions for more information. 

If you create a bank account at the entity level, then it is already restricted to that entity, and 
the Restrictions tab does not appear. Similarly, if you create a bank account at the entity level of 
a parent entity, it is not accessible to the parent entity ’s child entities/locations. If you want to 
apply location restrictions and allow child locations to access a bank account, you must create 
the bank account at the top level. 

Applying Entity Restrictions to a Bank Account 

To restrict a bank account: 

1. 
In the Bank accounts list, click the Edit link next to the account name.  

The Bank account information page opens. 

2. 
Click the Restrictions tab. 

3. 
Select a restriction option: 

• 
Unrestricted: This option makes the account available to the top-level company and 

all entity-level locations. This is the default. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: This option makes the account inaccessible to entity-level 

locations. 

• 
Restricted: This option makes the account accessible to locations or location groups 

that you specify. 

4. 
If you select the Restricted option, click the Select button, and then use the multi-select box 

to choose one or more locations or location groups that can access the bank account. For 

instructions using the selection box, see Using the multi-select box. 

---



##### Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 58*

Search & Find 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

You can’t remove a location restriction if the location is set as the owner location for the 
account, or if this bank account is configured as the default bank account. 

How Restricting by a Location Affects Inter-Entity Transactions 

When you restrict a bank account to a location or location group, only that location or group has 

access to that account. If another location is paying the A/P invoices for the first location, the 

location can’t use the account to pay A/P invoices, because it doesn’t own that account. If the 

locations are in different entities, the system can create an IET due-to/due-from transaction. 

For example, suppose a location for Texas receives an A/P invoice but a Corporate location pays it 

from an account owned by Corporate. In this case, an inter-entity transaction (due-to/due-from) 

will be created between the two locations or entities. You can see the IET in the following General 

Ledger report. 

In a case where a bank account is restricted by location and another location within the same 

entity pays the A/P invoice, no IET is generated because both locations are children of the entity.

Credit Card Accounts List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Credit Card`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Credit Card`


The Credit card accounts list displays the credit card accounts in your system. From this list, you 

can add, edit, or delete accounts and even start the process of reconciling an account or 

generating reconciliation reports. 

Credit Card Accounts in Multi-Entity Shared Companies  

Credit card accounts can either be common to all entities, or exclusive to a specific entity. 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you can create credit card 

accounts at both the root and entity levels. To view credit card accounts at the top level, select the 

Include private check box at the top of the Credit card accounts list. Enter all credit card 

transactions at the entity level. When you create a credit card, a location is required. 

Consequently, in credit card transactions, the system knows to use the base currency for the entity 

associated with that location. Credit card transactions do not support foreign currency. 

If you do not see the Include private check box on your page, verify that you are not using a 
custom view.

When you edit an existing account, the ID, Last 4 digits of card number, Type, and Payment 

method fields are read-only. In addition, reconciliation information is displayed, which includes 
two read-only fields (Last reconciled balance and Last reconciled date) and a Reconcile link. The 
link opens the Credit card reconciliation page. 

To add a credit card account: 

Fill In the Credit Card Details Section 

1. 
In the ID field, enter a unique identifier to distinguish the card’s purpose.  

2. 
In the Description field, enter a short description to identify the card account. 

You can differentiate credit cards versus debit cards in both the ID and Description fields 
by using abbreviations such as CC and DB. 

3. 
In the Type drop-down list, select the applicable credit card type: 

• 
Visa 

• 
Mastercard 

• 
Discover 

• 
American Express 

• 
Diners Club 

• 
Other Charge Card

4. 
In the Last 4 digits of card number field, type the last four digits of the credit card number. 

5. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select between the following items: 

• 
Credit: Credit cards must have a vendor ID and a credit card offset account. 

• 
Debit: Debit cards used to pay A/P invoices must have an associated checking account 

and vendor ID. 

6. 
In the Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip code/Post code, and Country fields, enter the 

relevant address information. 

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select one of the following options: 

• 
Active: This is the default status. 

• 
Inactive: Select this option if you are no longer using the card and do not want it to 

appear on the list. You can always see inactive cards by selecting the Include Inactive 

check box in the Credit card accounts list. 

8. 
In the Month and Year drop-down lists, select the month and year when the credit card 

expires. 

Fill In the Accounting Section 

1. 
In the Credit-card offset account drop-down list, select an account that is different from the 

default offset account for Accounts Payable. This field appears only if you select Credit as 

the payment method. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 

find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

2. 
In the Debit-card checking account drop-down list, select a checking account to associate 

with the debit card. It must be the same account for which the card was issued. This field 

only appears if you select “Debit” as the payment method. 

3. 
In the Default G/L journal (accrual & cash basis) drop-down list, select the journal into 

which you want to place a charge card transaction performed in Cash Management. The 

default journal is the same one used for A/P payments. For credit cards, all transactions 

(charges on the card and payoffs for the card) use the same journal. For debit cards, banks 

have different journals. This field appears if you did not enable dual method reporting. 

4. 
In the Default G/L journal (accrual basis) drop-down list, select an accrual journal. This field 

appears if you enabled dual method reporting and only applies to credit cards. 

5. 
In the Default G/L journal (cash basis) drop-down list, select a cash journal. This field 

appears if you enabled dual method reporting and only applies to credit cards. 

6. 
In the Finance charges account drop-down list, select an account to be used for credit card 

reconciliation. This field does not apply to debit cards.

#### Deposits
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 80*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Deposits 

When you deposit multiple payments, it’s normal to group the payments and submit them to 

your bank with one deposit slip. When you deposit payments and later receive your bank 

reconciliation statement, all you see is one entry with the total deposit amount. The Deposits 

page enables you to record all of the individual payments that constitute a deposit. 

Deposits automatically post to the General Ledger and appropriate subledgers. 

When you record a deposit, the payment must already be received against your undeposited 
funds account. 

Use the manual deposit feature to record a customer payment that isn’t made against a specific 

invoice, for example, an over-the-counter cash sale. 

Deposits, Automatic Deposits, and Manual Deposits 

Deposits in the RealPage Accounting system are different from automatic deposits and manual 

deposits. 

Method 
Description 

Deposits 
When you receive payment for A/R invoices, A/R advances, or Cash 

Management other receipts into an undeposited funds account, create a 

deposit as the next step in the workflow. This type of deposit enables 

you to record payments from multiple customers into one deposit. 

When you deposit multiple payments in a single deposit, you see only 

one entry for the total deposit amount when you receive your bank 

statement. The Deposits page enables you to record all of the individual 

payments that constitute the deposit. 

Automatic deposits 
When you receive payment for A/R invoices, A/R advances, or Cash 

Management other receipts directly to a bank account and not into an 

undeposited funds account, the system automatically posts the deposit 

to the G/L and appropriate subledgers. You do not have to take any 

further action. 

Manual deposits 
When you receive a payment and don’t have an A/R invoice to apply the 

payment to–for example, an over-the-counter cash sale–you can create 

a manual deposit. The system automatically records the payment and 

creates the matching invoice at the same time. 

You can view all these methods of deposit in the Bank Register report. You can view only 

undeposited funds for which you create a deposit on the Deposits page. 

---

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Prerequisites 

To create a deposit, you must have completed these tasks: 

•

the entity level where the transaction is recorded in the entity’s base currency. Adding deposits is 

not available for top-level companies.

#### Deposits Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 82*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Deposits Workflow 

The following diagram illustrates the deposits workflow and the posting activity in the General 

Ledger and subledgers. Remember, you can add a deposit only after you receive payments into 

an undeposited funds account. 

When you receive a payment into an undeposited funds account, the system: 

• 
Posts the payment amount to the General Ledger. 

• 
Credits the appropriate account, depending on what the payment is for and how your 

accounts are set up, and debits the undeposited funds account. 

• 
Adds the payment to the list of payments that can be deposited on the Create deposit slip 

page. 

Payment type 
Typical account that is credited 

A/R invoice 
Accounts receivable account 

A/R advance 
Customer prepayment account 

CM other receipt 
Miscellaneous or other income account 

After you add a deposit, the system: 

---


<!-- Page 83 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
Posts the amount of the deposit to the General Ledger.  

• 
Debits the bank account. 

• 
Credits the undeposited funds account that previously held the transaction. 

• 
Adds the deposit record to the Deposits list. When you run the Bank Register report, the 

deposit appears in the report. 

• 
Removes the payments that you included in the deposit from the list of payments on the 

Create deposit slip page. They are no longer available to be included in other deposit slips.

#### Undeposited Funds Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 84*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Undeposited Funds Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration`


You use an undeposited funds account to hold checks and cash payments that you are collecting 

for a future deposit. As you collect checks and cash, you can enter these payments even if you do 

not know when you will make the deposit, or to which bank you will make the deposit. 

Example 

You make your deposits on Fridays. You collect payments throughout the week and record 

them. The payments are correctly accounted for in the undeposited funds account. 

However, the deposit is not actually in the bank account until you complete the Create 

deposit slip page. At that point, the funds are transferred from the undeposited funds 

account to the bank account. 

Thus, if you received a particularly large check, but were not yet sure where you want to 

deposit it, you could record it when you receive it so that the payment is on the books and 

preserve your options with regard to which financial institution you want to deposit it. 

When you select an account for undeposited funds, you cannot select a General Ledger account 

that is associated with a bank account, even though that might seem natural. Rather, you should 

specify an account that can be used as a transfer account so that you can deposit them later. (If 

you were to choose a bank account, the funds would already be posted to that bank, even though 

you have not yet deposited them. That would defeat the whole purpose of having an undeposited 

funds feature.) Typically, you create an account such as 1500 Undeposited Funds. However, you 

can have a more granular structure of multiple undeposited funds accounts. 

You can set up a standard undeposited funds account and an undeposited funds account for 

intercompany billing. Both are configured on the Configure Accounts Receivable page. 

To set up undeposited funds accounts: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click Configuration. 

Setting up a standard undeposited funds account: 

1. 
Find the Defaults section of the Payments section. 

2. 
In the Offline payment account drop-down list, select Undeposited funds account. The 

Undeposit account drop-down list opens. 

3. 
Select the desired account for funds from standard transactions.  

4. 
Click Save. 

Setting up the intercompany billing undeposited funds account: 

---


<!-- Page 85 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click Configuration. 

3. 
Find the Intercompany billing setup section. 

4. 
In the Undeposited funds account (ICB) drop-down list, select the desired account to use 

for undeposited funds for intercompany transactions. 

Only funds from fully paid A/P Invoices are applied to the undeposited funds account. 

5. 
Click Save.

Reversing Deposits 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > Reverse`


To maintain an audit trail of cash activity, you cannot edit a deposit. However, you can reverse the 

deposit and then re-create it to make changes. For example, if you entered a deposit that is 

missing an A/R payment, you can re-create the deposit to include the payment. 

When you reverse a deposit, a new transaction appears in the Deposits list labeled “Voided 

Deposit Slip.” The reversal is a mirror image of the original deposit, but the debits and credits are 

reversed so the journal entries cancel each other out. 

You can reverse a deposit when: 

• 
You have permission to reverse. 

• 
The deposit has not been reconciled. 

• 
No items in the deposit—A/R payments or Cash Management other receipts—have been 

reversed. You can, however, reverse any of the other items in the deposit.

##### Reversing a Deposit
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 89*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

After you reverse the deposit, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can record another 

deposit to replace it. 

Reversing a Deposit 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > Reverse`


To reverse a deposit: 

1. 
In the Deposits list, click the Reverse link next to the deposit slip you want to reverse. 

The Transaction reversal date box opens. 

2. 
In the Reverse the transaction on date field, type or select the date to reverse the deposit. 

This is usually the original transaction date or a later date. You can even select a date in a 

prior closed period so that your financial statements are correct. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type a description that applies to this deposit. This text is for your 

information only. 

4. 
Click the Submit button. 

The Deposits list now displays two line items for the deposit: 

• 
The first line item, the original deposit, is now labeled Reversed. 

• 
The second line item, labeled Reversal, is the reversed deposit. 

Example 

You have a deposit for $500. After reversing, you still have the original $500 deposit, but also a 

voided deposit for -$500, resulting in a net of zero. 

The resulting journal entry debits undeposited funds and credits the bank account. A/R payments 

and other receipts that were in the original deposit are not reversed and are available to be 

redeposited.

##### Reversing a Payment in a Deposit
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 90*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Reversing a Payment in a Deposit 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > View`


A deposit includes payments for A/R invoices, A/R advances, and other receipts that are received 

into an undeposited funds account. The deposit generates the journal entry to record the transfer 

of funds from undeposited funds to the bank (debits the bank account and credits undeposited 

funds). 

After you make a deposit, even if it has been reconciled, you can reverse a payment in the 

deposit. For example, you might need to reverse a payment to correct a payment date or handle a 

bounced check. 

Reversing a payment creates a new reversing payment to offset the original. The combination of 

the original payment and the negative reversal produces a net effect of zero and serves as an 

audit trail. 

The new reversing payment has its own G/L date so that you can optionally use a different date 

for the reversing payment than the date on the original payment. The resulting journal entry 

debits Accounts receivable (or some other account if another receipt was reversed) and credits 

the bank account. 

After a payment in a deposit has been reversed, the deposit can’t be reversed. You can, however, 
reverse as many payments in the deposit as you like. Reversing all of the payments effectively 
voids the deposit. 

To reverse a payment in a deposit: 

1. 
In the Deposits list, click the View link to view details about the payments in the deposit. 

You can drill down further into each payment. 

2. 
Reverse the payment according to your payment type: 

• 
A/R invoice: Reverse the payment from either the Posted payments list or the Receipts 

Register report in Accounts Receivable. 

• 
A/R advance: Reverse the payment from either the Posted advances list or the 

Receipts Register report in Accounts Receivable. 

• 
Other receipt: Reverse the payment (deposited into undeposited funds) from the 

Other receipts list in Cash Management.

#### Deposit Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 91*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Deposit Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Daily Tasks > Enter Payments > Deposits > 
Add/View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Deposits > Add/View`


Use the Deposit page to record a deposit after you have received a payment into an undeposited 

funds account for: 

• 
A/R invoices 

• 
A/R advances 

• 
Other receipts 

The deposit ensures that your books reflect the transfer of funds from your undeposited funds 

account to your bank account when you decide to actually move the collected and held payments 

to your financial institution.

A funds transfer is a transfer of funds from one cash account to another. In Cash Management, 

you can record a transfer of funds by entering the from and to accounts and the amount of 

money that was transferred.

• 
Bank accounts 

If you want to see the balances of your accounts to determine if you need to make a transfer or if 

there are sufficient funds to be transferred, you can run a Cash Balance (on page 437) report.

##### Adding a Funds Transfer
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 97*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Adding a Funds Transfer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > 
 Funds Transfer`


After you create a funds transfer, you can’t void or edit it. However, you can reverse it and then 

enter another funds transfer with the correct information. You can’t undo a reversal after you 

submit it. 

To add a funds transfer: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, click the 
 Add button next to the Funds transfer menu 

option. 

The Funds transfer page opens with a new, blank record. 

3. 
In the From account and To account drop-down lists, select the bank accounts that you are 

transferring the funds to and from. Note the following fields: 

• 
Bank G/L account: This field appears only if you have enabled alternate G/L accounts 

for your bank accounts on the Configure Cash Management page. The drop-down list 

automatically populates with the default G/L account defined in the bank account 

record. You can select an alternate G/L account from the drop-down list as needed. 

• 
Inter-entity receivable account: This field automatically populates with the inter-entity 

receivable (IER) account that you set up on the Inter-entity account mapping page.  

• 
Inter-entity payable account: This field automatically populates with the inter-entity 

payable (IEP) account that you set up on the Inter-entity account mapping page. 

• 
Balance: This field automatically populates with the bank account’s current balance. 

• 
Currency: This field appears only if your company uses multiple currencies. It 

automatically populates with the currency defined in the bank account record. 

If you are transferring funds in a multi-entity, multi-currency system, see Transferring 
Funds Across Multiple Entities. 

4. 
Select the Generate ACH check box to automatically generate an ACH payment file for the 

transfer activity. The ACH payment file automatically appears in the Payment file list (on 

page 158).  

• 
If you are transferring funds to multiple accounts, then the system creates multiple 

payments in the same payment file. 

• 
If your company is set up to upload payment files directly to a bank’s SFTP site, then 

the system automatically sends the payment file to the bank when the file is 

generated.  

5. 
In the Date field, type or select the actual transfer date.

Importing Funds Transfers 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Funds Transfer > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Funds Transfer > Import/Template`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed 
on the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized 
based on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve 
created. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for funds transfers: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, click the Funds transfer menu option. 

The Funds transfer list opens. 

3. 
Click the Import button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

The Import box opens. 

4. 
Click the Download template link. 

The system either downloads the Funds Transfer.xls file or prompts you to open or save the 

file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

5. 
Open the Funds Transfer.xls file and fill in the required fields: 

---


<!-- Page 99 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
FROM_ACCOUNT: Type the ID of the bank account from which you are transferring 

the funds. 

• 
TO_ACCOUNT: Type the ID of the bank account to which you are transferring the 

funds. 

• 
DATE: Type the actual transfer date for the funds. See Formatting Dates for a list of 

valid date formats. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the transfer amount. 

If you are transferring funds between credit card accounts, you must enter a 
positive amount. 

6. 
Optionally, fill in the following fields 

• 
REFERENCE_NO: Type the transaction number. 

This field is not required, but it is recommended. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description for the transfer of funds. 

7. 
If you have enabled alternate G/L accounts for the bank accounts, then you also have the 

option to fill in the following fields: 

• 
FROM_BANK_GLACCOUNT_NO: Type the ID of the G/L account that corresponds with 

the bank account in the FROM_ACCOUNT column. 

• 
TO_BANK_GLACCOUNT_NO: Type the ID of the G/L account that corresponds with the 

bank account in the TO_ACCOUNT column. 

8. 
If you are using dimensions for tracking or reporting purposes, fill in the remaining fields 

with the corresponding dimension value; for example, a location ID in the LOCATION_ID 

field, a department ID in the DEPARTMENT_ID field, and so on. 

9. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

Importing Data from the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
Return to the Import box. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload.

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with

Reversing a Funds Transfer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Funds Transfer > Reverse`


You cannot edit or void funds transfers. However, you can reverse a transfer and then enter a new 

one with the correct information. This ensures that the original transaction, the reversal, and the 

new transaction are GAAP-compliant and provide an audit trail. 

To reverse a funds transfer: 

1. 
In the Funds transfer list, locate the transfer that you want to reverse, and then click the 

Reverse link. 

The Transaction reversal date box opens. 

2. 
In Reverse the transaction on date, type or select the effective date of reversal. This date is 

typically the original transaction date or later. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type a short description of the reversal. 

4. 
Click the Submit button. 

The system reverses the fund transfer and displays it in the list. When a funds transfer reversal is 

waiting to reach the reversal date, the system displays the word Reversal instead of the Reverse 

link. The system displays Reversed for reversed fund transfers. 

To ensure that there is a valid audit trail, RealPage does not recommend undoing a reversal. 
Instead, you can re-enter the original transaction to correct any errors.

#### About Manual Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 110*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

About Manual Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment`


Occasionally, you must deviate from the normal Accounts Payable workflow to pay A/P invoices. 

For example, if you had food delivered to the office and paid for it immediately or if you paid an 

unexpected COD for a delivered package. Previously, if you paid by check, you could quickly add 

an A/P invoice and record its payment at the same time. Manual payments allow you to easily 

record payments made by cash, credit card, or funds transfer. 

Manual Payments vs. Quick Checks 

Manual payments involve recording each payment, including handwritten checks, one at a time. If 

you have many handwritten checks to record, you can use quick check entry to enter the data for 

up to 100 handwritten checks on a single page. The difference between these two methods of 

recording is that manual payments provide more flexibility for reporting on various dimensions, 

while quick check entry offers support only for reporting on departments and locations. 

---



#### Manual Payments List
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 111*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Manual Payments List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment`


Use the Manual payments list to record one-off payments outside of the Accounts Payable 

workflow, such as: 

• 
Payments made with a hand-written check 

• 
Funds transfers from your bank to a utility company 

• 
Credit card payments made over the phone 

Adding a manual payment allows you to quickly add an A/P invoice and record the payment at 

the same time, bringing your General Ledger up to date. You can record payments made by 

check, cash, credit card, or funds transfer. 

If you have A/P invoices already entered into the system, you can use the record transfer feature 

to record any payment made outside of the system.

1.

 No symbol appears, indicating that you cannot select

After you enter the account, the system automatically populates the Amount field. As you

##### Posting a Manual Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 114*

Periodic Tasks

Posting a Manual Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment`


How you post the payment to the General Ledger (G/L) depends on the payment method. 

Posting a Payment Made by Check 

To post a payment made by a handwritten check: 

• 
Click the Save & confirm button.  

The system posts the check to the G/L. In the Manual payments list, the State of the 

payment appears as Confirmed and the Payment method appears as Manual check. 

If you want to print the check before posting it, complete the following steps: 

1. 
Click the Save & print button. The details for the check reappear on the Manual payment 

page. 

2. 
Click the Print button. A PDF of the check appears in a new window. 

3. 
Send this PDF to the printer that has your check stock loaded and verify that the printed 

check is correct. 

In the Manual payments list, the State of the payment appears as Printed, and the Payment 

method appears as Manual check. 

4. 
Return to the Manual payment page for this payment, and then click the Confirm button. 

In the Manual payments list, the State of the payment changes to Confirmed. After you 

confirm the check, the system posts the check to the G/L. 

If you don’t confirm the check immediately, then you can continue adding other manual 
payments. However, you can’t add and print another check until you confirm this check. To 
return to the Manual payment page to confirm the check, click the View link next to the 
payment. 

Posting a Payment Made by Cash, Credit Card, or Record Transfer 

To post a payment made by cash, credit card, or record transfer: 

• 
Click the Save & confirm button.  

The system posts the check to the G/L. In the Manual payments list, the State of the 

payment appears as Confirmed.

##### Voiding a Manual Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 115*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Voiding a Manual Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment > 
Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment > Void`


You cannot edit or delete manual payments after they are saved and confirmed. However, you 

can void the payment, which automatically reverses the A/P invoice. Voiding a payment reverses 

its effect on the General Ledger (G/L) and leaves a record of both the original and voided 

payment. 

When you void a payment: 

• 
The system creates a new transaction that is the reverse of the transaction you are voiding. 

In other words, the transaction is not zeroed out, resulting in an audit trail. This produces a 

net effect of zero for that transaction. 

• 
The system treats the reversed entry as a new payment and places the reversed manual 

payment into its payment summary based on the auto-summary frequency. 

• 
Both transactions are labeled as Voided. However, there are now two: the original positive 

one and the new negative reversing one. The title of the summary contains wording similar 

to “Reversed Quick Payments.” 

• 
The system also reverses the A/P invoice that is associated with the voided payment in a 

similar manner, leaving two A/P invoices: the original positive one and a new negative 

reversing one. Both are labeled as Reversed. 

If a manual payment is in a summary, you must open the summary before you can void the 
payment. You cannot void a reconciled payment or a payment in a closed period. 

To void a manual payment: 

1. 
In the Manual payments list, locate the payment that you want to void, and then click the 

corresponding Void link. The Void payment date box opens. 

2. 
In the Void the payment on date field, type or select a date on or after the transaction date. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type an optional note to store with the G/L entry. 

4. 
Click the Submit button.

rom the A/P invoices list, find the A/P invoice associated with the manual payment.

#### Other Receipts
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 125*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Other Receipts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Other Receipts`


Other receipts are receipts that are not associated with either a customer or invoice and can 

include cash, a card charge, a cash transfer, or check payment. For example, the receipt can be a 

cash reimbursement from an employee who used the company account to ship a personal item. 

When you record the receipt, you can choose either of these options: 

• 
Select the bank where you want the payments deposited to. 

• 
Define the payments as going to an undeposited funds account so you can deposit them 

later. 

Receipts automatically post to the General Ledger and appropriate subledgers. After you 
deposit the receipt, the deposit is also automatically posted to the G/L and appropriate 
subledgers. 

After you record a payment receipt and the deposit, the system performs the following actions: 

• 
Removes the payments you selected from the list. You cannot select them to include in 

other deposit slips and you can no longer void or reverse these payments. 

• 
Posts the amount of the deposit to the General Ledger. The deposit appears on the 

Deposits list and the Bank Register report. 

• 
Debits the bank account and credits the undeposited funds account that previously held this 

transaction. 

Multi-Entity Shared Companies 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you can use this feature only in 

the entity where you recorded the transaction in the entity’s base currency.

To view or edit a receipt: 

1. 
In the Other receipts list, click the View or Edit link next to a receipt. 

The Other receipts information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the receipt as needed. 

3. 
Click Done or Save. 

Reversing a Receipt 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Other Receipts > Reverse`


You can reverse other receipts if you want to maintain an audit trail. The reversal process depends 

on whether you deposited the receipt into your bank account or your undeposited funds. 

The option to delete or reverse appears depending on the status of the receipt: 

• 
The Delete option is only available before you deposit the funds into the bank.  

• 
The Reverse option is only available after you make the deposit. 

If you do not see either option, it may be because the transaction has already been reconciled 

during bank reconciliation. In that case, reopen the reconciliation (on page 334), and then make 

your changes. 

Reversing a Receipt Deposited to Undeposited Funds 

You can use this option only after you have deposited the receipts. 

To reverse a receipt that was deposited to undeposited funds: 

1. 
On the Other receipts page, locate the receipt that you want to reverse, and then click the 

corresponding Reverse link. 

---

The Transaction reversal date box opens. 

2. 
In the Reverse the transaction on date field, type or select the effective date of reversal. 

This date is typically the original transaction date or a later date. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type a short description of the reversal. 

4. 
Click the Submit button. 

You cannot undo the reversal after you click Submit. 

Reversing a Receipt Deposited to Your Bank Account 

To reverse a receipt that was deposited directly to your bank account: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select Cash Management, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select Registers, and then select Bank.  

The Bank register page opens. 

3. 
Set the applicable Reporting period and Bank account filters to include the receipt you 

want to reverse. 

4. 
Click View to display the Bank Register report. 

5. 
Locate the receipt you want to reverse, and then click the corresponding Reverse link.

This date is typically the original transaction date or a later date. 

7. 
In the Memo field, type a short description of the reversal. 

8. 
Click the Submit button. 

You cannot undo the reversal after you click Submit. 

After the reversal, the system displays two line items for the transaction. One line item is the 

original transaction, now labeled Reversed. Another line item, labeled Reversal, is the reverse of 

the transaction. It produces a net effect of zero and serves as an audit trail.

Configuring Available Cash in Cash Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration > Available Cash`


To configure available cash settings: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click Configuration, and then find the Available Cash section. 

Automatically Setting Up Available Cash Locations 

Select the Automatically set up for new locations check box to automatically create a new record 

in the Available cash locations list when a new location is added in RealPage Accounting. 

Defining Where to Transfer the Available Cash 

Use the Transfer requirements section to transfer a location’s total holdback amount into a 

separate account after it’s calculated and record a journal entry for the transfer. 

1. 
In the Journal for transfers drop-down list, select the G/L journal in which to record the 

transfer. 

2. 
In the Transfer to account drop-down list, select the cash account to which you want to 

transfer the holdback amount.  

Creating Fields for Entering Available Cash Information by Location 

Use the Name captions section to create custom fields for entering available cash information on 

the Available cash location page. 

• 
In the Name caption fields, type a label for up to three custom text fields. For example, you 

could create a field named “Property Manager” or “Investor”. 

Summarizing Account Groups in the Available Cash Report 

Use the Summary options section to summarize account groups into a single line in the report on 

the Available cash location page. If you do not enable these options, then each account in the 

account group displays on an individual line. 

Select the check box for each account type you want to summarize:  

• 
Summarize cash accounts 

• 
Summarize A/P accounts 

• 
Summarize A/R accounts

Adding an Available Cash Location 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > 
 Available Cash`


Add locations to the Available cash location list so you can generate a report of their available 

cash after adjusting for the location’s holdbacks (on page 635). You can also define the G/L 

accounts to associate with each location.  

• 
Cash Group/Account

To add a location record for calculating available cash:

Open the Cash Management menu.

In the Periodic tasks section of the menu, click the 
 Add button next to Available cash. 

The Available cash location page opens. 

3. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location (property) for which you want to calculate 

available cash. 

4. 
If you defined any Name captions when configuring available cash in Cash Management, 

then those custom text fields will appear here. Fill in each field. For example, if you created a 

Property manager field, then you would type the name of the person who is responsible for 

managing the property.

when calculating the location’s available cash.

use when calculating the location’s available cash.

In the A/R group/account drop-down list, select the A/R account that the system should 

use when calculating the location’s available cash.

Click Save. After you save the record, you can view the available cash calculation by clicking

Edit custom text fields (these are the Name captions defined on the Configure cash 

management page)

Available Cash Location Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Available Cash > 
Add/Edit/View`


Use the Available cash location page to add, edit, and view locations for which you are 

calculating available cash. After you have created a new location, you can open the record in View 

or Edit mode to view a report of the location’s projected cash balance, which you can use when 

paying invoices. The report calculates this projection using holdbacks for expected expenses that 

have not been received for the current period.   

When you are viewing or editing a location record, the page has two tabs: 

• 
Main: This tab displays general information about the location as well as a report with the 

current available cash calculation. The actions you can perform on this report (on page 128) 

change depending on whether you are in View or Edit mode.  

• 
Accounts: This tab displays the G/L accounts or account groups used to calculate available 

cash for the location.

##### Printing or Exporting the Available Cash Report for a Location
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*



##### Recalculating Available Cash Locations
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Printing or Exporting the Available Cash Report for a Location 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Available Cash > Print/Export`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Available Cash > Edit/View > 
Print to PDF/Export to Excel`


You can print the report on the Available cash location page to a PDF file or export it to an Excel 

file. 

There are two ways to print or export the report: 

• 
In the Available cash locations list, click the Print or Export link next to the location record. 

• 
In the Available cash locations list, click the View or Edit link to open the location record, 

and then click the Print to PDF or Export to Excel button. 

The PDF or Excel file automatically downloads to your local drive. 

Recalculating Available Cash Locations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Available Cash > Edit/View`


RealPage Accounting automatically recalculates available cash every morning at 3:00 a.m. CST. 

However, if you make any changes that will affect a location’s available cash before the next 

refresh—for example, adjusting a holdback amount—then you can manually refresh the data on 

the Available cash location page to update the report. 

Recalculating an Available Cash Location 

To manually refresh the data in the available cash report: 

1. 
In the Available cash locations list, click the Edit or View link next to a location record. 

The Available cash location page opens. 

2. 
On the Main tab, click the Refresh data button. 

The system automatically recalculates available cash and refreshes the report data. 

Recalculating All Available Cash Locations 

You can manually recalculate and refresh the data of all available cash locations simultaneously. 

• 
In the Available cash locations list, click the Recalculate all locations button. 

The system adds the job to the offline job queue for processing. You will receive an email 

notification when it’s complete. 

---



##### Removing and Hiding Holdbacks from the Available Cash Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 145*



##### Transferring Holdbacks to a Separate Cash Account
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 145*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Removing and Hiding Holdbacks from the Available Cash Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Available Cash > Edit`


You can remove one or more holdbacks on the Available cash location page to exclude the 

holdback amount(s) from report totals. You can also toggle whether to show or hide these 

holdbacks in the report itself. 

To remove holdbacks from the report: 

1. 
In the Available cash locations list, click the Edit link next to the location record. 

The Available cash location page opens. 

2. 
Select the Remove check box next to the holdbacks you want to exclude from the report.  

The report totals are automatically adjusted. 

3. 
If you want to hide these holdbacks from the report, then click the Hide removed 

holdbacks button.  

The row(s) are hidden from the report. If you want to show hidden holdbacks in the report 

again—or if you need to change which holdbacks are removed—then click the Show 

removed holdbacks button. 

Transferring Holdbacks to a Separate Cash Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Available Cash > Edit`


You can transfer a location’s holdbacks to a separate cash account directly from the available cash 

report. This process creates a journal entry to move the Total holdbacks amount from the cash 

account to the transfer account. 

Use the Transfer requirements section on the Configure cash management page to define a 
transfer journal and account (on page 126 ). 

To transfer holdbacks: 

1. 
In the Available cash locations list, click the Edit link next to the location. 

The Available cash location page opens. 

2. 
Click the Total holdbacks amount in the Remaining column. 

The Journalize holdback box opens. 

3. 
If you want the system to automatically reverse the journal entry at a later date, then type or 

select a Reversal date. 

4. 
Click the Create journal button.

Bank Account Holdbacks Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Bank Account Holdbacks`


You can use the Bank account holdbacks page to enter or import holdbacks and external 

balances. Bank account holdbacks, along with holdbacks from available cash (on page 635), allow 

you to set aside monthly expenses—not yet incurred—to ensure that you can make accurate 

payments. Holdbacks are subtracted from your bank balance so you can see the adjusted balance 

when paying A/P invoices. 

By default, the Bank account holdbacks page displays all top-level and entity-level bank 

accounts. 

The Cash Visibility report (on page 458 ) provides more visibility into your company’s cash 
balance. It displays your G/L bank balance, external bank balance, and final adjusted balance. The 
adjusted balance is calculated by subtracting all approved payments, payments pending 
approval, invoices posted but not paid, invoices pending approval, bank account holdbacks, and 
available cash holdbacks from your G/L bank balance.

Defining Custom Names for Bank Account Holdbacks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration`


By default, RealPage Accounting provides four (4) categories for bank account holdbacks. These 

categories are labeled Holdback 1-4 on the Bank account holdbacks page and the Cash Visibility 

report (on page 458). However, you can change these names on the Configure cash management 

page. 

To define custom names for bank account holdbacks: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select Cash Management, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the Configuration option. 

The Configure cash management page opens. 

3. 
In the Accounting section, select the Enable custom holdback name check box. 

4. 
For each Holdback, type a new name in the Holdback custom name field; for example, 

“Mortgage” or “Insurance”. 

5. 
Click Save.

Manually Entering and Editing Bank Account Holdbacks and External Balances 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Bank Account Holdbacks`


You can manually enter and edit holdback amounts and external balances on the Bank account 

holdbacks page. If you would rather enter or edit this information in bulk, then you can import 

the information (on page 147) instead. 

To enter or edit holdbacks and external balances: 

1. 
On the Bank account holdbacks page, insert your cursor in one of the following editable 

fields: 

• 
(Holdbacks 1-4): Type a holdback amount for each of the holdback categories. By 

default, the categories are named Holdback 1, Holdback 2, Holdback 3, and Holdback 

4. However, you can define custom holdback names (on page 146) on the Configure 

cash management page. 

• 
External balances: Type the balance as it appears in your bank statement. 

The other fields on this page are read-only. 

2. 
Click Save. 

Importing Bank Account Holdbacks and External Balances 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Bank Account Holdbacks`


Whether you’re importing data into a company for the first time or updating existing data, 

importing data into RealPage Accounting is a two-step process: first, you download and populate 

a template, and second, you import the data from the template into the system. 

We recommend downloading a new template whenever you import information. This is important 

because the template can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. An older version of the template may not work. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the template for bank account holdbacks: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select Cash Management, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, select the Bank account holdbacks option. 

The Bank account holdbacks page opens. 

3. 
Click the Download entries form link. 

The system either downloads the BankAcctHoldBackEntries.csv file or prompts you to open 

or save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

---

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

By default, the Bank account holdbacks page includes all top-level and entity-level bank 
accounts. When you download the import template, it will automatically populate with this 
information.  

4. 
Edit the following fields as needed: 

• 
(Holdbacks 1-4): Type a holdback amount for each of the holdback categories. By 

default, the categories are named Holdback 1, Holdback 2, Holdback 3, and Holdback 

4. However, you can define custom holdback names (on page 146) on the Configure 

cash management page. 

• 
External balances: Type the balance as it appears in your bank statement. 

5. 
Save the CSV template. 

Importing Data From the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
On the Bank account holdbacks page, click the Choose file button. 

2. 
Select your CSV template. 

3. 
Click the Upload button. 

The Bank account holdbacks page refreshes with the imported information.

add to the payment file. 

3. 
Generate the payment file (on page 152).

files. 

1. 
Download the payment file. 

2. 
Send the payment file to your bank for processing.
