Generate File Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Electronic Payments > File Generation > 
Customize List`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > File Generation > Customize List`


Use this page to filter your list of electronic payment requests. Filtering your list of electronic 

payments enables you to simplify your workflow processes. By setting specific filters, you can limit 

your list of payments to only those payment files that you want to generate right now. 

This page appears when you select the Customize list button from the Generate file list. 

The Generate file (filter page) contains three sections. Each section contains a group of controls 

that affects the payment files that ultimately get generated. 

• 
Payment range/sorting: This section contains controls that determine the number of 

payments displayed on a page, and allows you to select the fields by which to sort the 

electronic payments. 

• 
Filters: This section contains options by which you can restrict or filter the electronic 

payments. 

• 
Time period: This section allows you to constrain the electronic payments by a time period. 

Customizing the Generate File List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > ACH > ACH File Generation 
> Customize List`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Electronic Payments > 
File Generation > Customize List`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Electronic Payments > File 
Generation > Customize List`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH > ACH File 
Generation > Customize List`


You can simplify your workflow process by filtering the list of electronic payments. By setting 

specific filters, you can limit your list of payments to only the payment files you want to generate 

at a time. 

To customize the list of payments: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Accounts payable or Cash management, and then 

select the All tab. 

2. 
Select ACH file generation.  

---


<!-- Page 167 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

3. 
Click the Customize list button. The system opens the Generate ACH File parameters page. 

Filling In the Payment Range/Sorting Section 

Define the sorting and number of records to display. By default, the system sorts electronic 

payments by date. 

1. 
In Sort by, click the Select link and select fields by which you want to sort by clicking 

Add next to the desired field. See Using the multi-select box for help. 

2. 
In Max rows, you can change the number of payments displayed on a page. Select 50, 100, 

or 200 rows. 

Assigning Filters in the Filters Section 

1. 
To filter the payments by the account they are drawn on, in the Checking account 

drop-down list, select the account. 

2. 
Specify whether you want to include only vendor payments, employee payments, or both by 

selecting the Select all vendors and Select all employees check boxes. 

3. 
In the From vendor/To vendor and From employee/To employee drop-down lists, select a 

beginning and ending range by ID number.  

4. 
In the Entity/Entity group drop-down list, select the entity or entity group by which you 

want to filter the payments. 

5. 
Select the Show entity level payments check box to include payment details for payments 

generated at the entity level. 

Set Date Filters in the Time Period Section 

1. 
To limit the listed payments by date, under Time period, you have two options: 

• 
Choose a time period by clicking Payment period and clicking a standard accounting 

period such as Current month, Prior quarter, and so on. Then enter an As of date 

from which the system calculates the corresponding time period. The As of date 

default is the current date. 

• 
Choose a date range by entering a start and end date in Start date and End date, 

respectively. 

2. 
When you have the filters set how you want them, click View. To return to the filters and 

format page, click the View button.

Confirming an Electronic Payment 

When the bank notifies you that the electronic payment has been processed, you need to confirm 

the payment file. 

To confirm a standard electronic payment: 

In the Payment File list, locate the payment that you want to confirm, and then click the 

corresponding Confirm link. 

The system updates the payment state from Pending to Confirmed, and removes the Confirm 

and Delete links. You cannot delete confirmed payments. 

Uploading Payment Files to SFTP 

To use this function, make sure you have configured an SFTP storage site in Company > All > 

Cloud Storage, and added the SFTP details during ACH bank configuration (on page 579 ). 

To upload a payment file directly to a bank’s SFTP site: 

1. 
In the Payment file list, locate the file that you want to upload, and then select the 

corresponding check box. 

2. 
Click the Upload to bank button. 

The system will send a status notification to inform the user whether the upload was 

successful or not. When the upload is successful, the system automatically confirms the 

payment on the user’s behalf. 

If you have enabled the Disable auto-confirmation of ACH files check box on the Configure 

cash management page, then you will need to manually confirm with your bank that the file 
was successfully uploaded before confirming the payment in RealPage Accounting. This 
setting applies to ACH, EFT, and BACS files. 

Deleting a Payment File 

See the How to Get Here (on page 159) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Deleting a payment file from the Payment File list voids all individual payments and sends them 

back to the Generate File page. 

To delete a payment file: 

1. 
In the Payment File list, find the payment file that you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the corresponding Delete link.

Voiding Electronic Payments 

See How to Get Here (on page 162) for a list of ways to access this area. 

Voiding an electronic payment is similar to how you would void a check. The way you void a 

payment depends on whether or not it was confirmed. For pending electronic payments 

(payments you haven’t confirmed to the G/L), you can void a single payment or the entire 

payment file. 

 Voiding a payment in the system does not affect the bank’s payment process. If you’ve already 

sent the payment to the vendor or employee, you’ll need to contact your bank to alert them that 

you need to void the payment. 

Voiding Pending Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Electronic Payments > Payment File > Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Electronic Payments > Payment File > Delete`


Void a Single Pending Payment within a Payment File 

If you’ve already sent the payment to the vendor, you’ll need to contact your bank to alert them 

to void the payment on their side. 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Cash management and then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Electronic payments section, select Payment file. 

3. 
When the Payment File list page displays, click the link for the payment file which contains 

the payment you want to void. 

The Payment File Details page appears with a list of payments that are either pending or 

confirmed. 

4. 
Click Void next to the individual payment you want to void. 

The voided payment then goes back to the View Payment Requests page where you can 

cancel the payment request. You can then reprocess the payment if necessary. 


> **Navigation Path:** `(Optional) To void the payment request, go to Accounts Payable > All > Payments > View`


payment requests. 

Void a Pending Payment File 

You can void a pending payment file by deleting it. The individual payments will then go back to 

the Generate File page. To cancel the individual payments, follow the steps above. If you’ve 

already sent payments to the vendor or employee, you’ll need to contact your bank to alert them 

to void the payment on their side. 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Cash management and then select the All tab.

Voiding an electronic payment is similar to voiding a check. The way you void a payment depends 

on whether or not it was confirmed. 

To void a payment from the Check Register report: 

1.

##### Voiding a Confirmed Electronic Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 178*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Voiding a Confirmed Electronic Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Check 
Register > View > Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Registers > Check`


The way you void a confirmed electronic payment is similar to how you void a confirmed check. 

You can void confirmed electronic payments in the Check Register report. 

However, you’ll need to contact your bank and let them know you need to void the payment. 
Electronic payments aren ’t posted until the file is confirmed by the user. 

To void a confirmed electronic payment: 

1. 
Open the Cash management menu. 

2. 
In the Reports section, pause on Registers, and then select Check. 

3. 
On the Check Register page, you can filter to find the payment you want to void. You can 

also click View to view all payments. 

4. 
Locate the payment and click Void for the payment you want to void. 

The voided payment then goes back to the Pay A/P invoices page. You can then edit the 

payment and regenerate it in a new payment file. 

After the payment is voided, the associated A/P invoice appears again on the Pay A/P 

invoices page. There, you can regenerate or edit the A/P invoice and regenerate it as a new 

electronic payment. 

Electronic payments are posted after you confirm the payment. To avoid having to void a 
confirmed payment (for example, you find out it can’t be processed by your bank), send the 
file to your bank first and then confirm. This way, if your bank isn’t able to process one of 
your payments, you can void the payment individually before you confirm the file.

#### Schedule ACH File Generation List
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 181*

Schedule ACH File Generation List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > Schedule (ACH) File Generation`


Use the Schedule (ACH) file generation list to automate ACH file generation so you don’t have to 

spend time selecting which payments to create a file for. From this list, you can: 

• 
Schedule a new ACH payment file. 

• 
View, edit, and delete scheduled files. 

• 
View the last execution date and next execution date. 

• 
View the result of the last execution. 

• 
Open a history log showing the results of all previous executions. 

• 
Turn a schedule off to stop generating the payment file. 

If the schedule runs successfully, the ACH file is created and added to the Payment file list (on 

page 158), where you can download the file (on page 160) or upload it directly to the bank via a 

secure FTP connection (on page 161).  

If the schedule fails to run, you can click the Failure link in the Last result column to open the 

Execution log list and view the corresponding error log to help you troubleshoot your automated 

payment file (on page 171).

##### Scheduling an ACH Payment File
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 182*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Scheduling an ACH Payment File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > 
 Schedule 
(ACH) File Generation`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > 
 Schedule (ACH) File Generation`


To schedule an ACH payment file: 

1. 
Click the Add button in the upper-right corner of the Schedule ACH file generation list. 

The Schedule ACH file generation page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule ID field, type a name for the schedule. This is a required field. 

3. 
In the Entity/entity group drop-down list, select the entity or entity group for which you are 

scheduling the payment file. If you want to schedule the payment file for all locations, leave 

the field blank. 

• 
Select the Include entity level check box if you want to include the entity or entity 

group name in the payment file. 

4. 
To include only payment requests from specific vendors in the payment file, select a range 

of vendor IDs from the Vendor from and Vendor to fields. 

5. 
To include only payment requests from a specific bank in the payment file, select a bank ID 

from the drop-down list. 

6. 
To include only payment requests of a specific vendor type in the payment file, select a 

vendor type from the Vendor type drop-down list. 

7. 
Leave the Status field as Active. 

8. 
In the Schedules section, set up a one-time or recurring schedule for generating the 

payment file: 

• 
Start date: Type or select the start date for the schedule. 

• 
Ending on: Select when the schedule should end. 

• 
Never: Continues running the schedule indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stops running the schedule after a specific number of 

occurrences. Define that number in the End after X occurrences field. 

• 
End date: Stops running the schedule on a specific date. Define that date in the 

End on field. 

• 
Repeat: Select the frequency of the schedule. This is how often a new payment file will 

be generated. 

• 
None: Runs once and does not repeat. 

• 
Days: Runs once every X number of days. 

---

##### Viewing Execution Logs for a Scheduled ACH Payment File
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 184*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide

Viewing Execution Logs for a Scheduled ACH Payment File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > (Last Result)`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > Schedule (ACH) File Generation > (Last Result)`


Each time the schedule for an ACH payment file runs, the system creates a log file to record the 

result of the file generation attempt. These logs are added to an Execution log list specific to that 

schedule. You can open individual log files to view the status details and troubleshoot errors. 

To view execution logs for a scheduled ACH payment file, click the Success or Failure link in the 

Last result column. The Execution log list opens for that schedule. 

If Successful 

If you clicked the Success link, the execution log opens to show the list of successful log entries 

for that payment file schedule. From this list, you can: 

• 
Click the View link to open the Scheduler log page containing the details of an individual 

log file. 

• 
Click the Delete link to delete an individual log file.

• 
Click the Export button to export the list of successful log files. 

If Failed 

If you click the Failed link, the execution log opens to show the list of failure log entries for that 

schedule. From this list, you can: 

• 
Click the View link to open the Error log page containing a detailed error log. 

• 
Click the Delete link to delete an individual log file. 

• 
Click the Export button to export the list of failure log files.

##### Turning a Payment File Schedule On or Off
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 186*



##### Deleting a Scheduled ACH Payment File
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 186*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Turning a Payment File Schedule On or Off 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > Turn Off/On`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > Schedule (ACH) File Generation > Turn Off/On`


You can turn off schedules for ACH payment files so they don’t continue running and generating 

payment files on a recurring basis. Schedules that are turned off are hidden from the Schedule 

ACH file generation list, but you can turn them back on at any time to resume the schedule. 

Turning a Payment File Schedule Off 

To turn a schedule off, click the Turn off link. The Status of the schedule is changed to Inactive, 

and it is hidden from the list. 

Turning a Payment File Schedule Back On 

To turn a schedule back on: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box at the top of the Schedule ACH file generation list. 

All inactive schedules are included in the list again. 

2. 
Find the schedule you want to make active again, and then click the Turn on link. 

The Status of the schedule is changed to Active, and it is unhidden from the list. 

Deleting a Scheduled ACH Payment File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > Delete`


Deleting a schedule is permanent and cannot be undone. If the schedule has already run on a 

previous date—or if you want to pause or disable the schedule temporarily—we recommend that 

you turn it off (on page 173) instead of deleting it so you don’t erase the log files from previous 

runs. 

To delete a scheduled ACH payment file: 

1. 
In the Schedule ACH file generation list, click the Delete link next to the payment file 

schedule. 

A confirmation message appears. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm.

##### Adding a Charge Payoff
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 199*



##### Reversing a Charge Payoff
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 199*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Adding a Charge Payoff 

To add a charge payoff: 

1. 
Click 
 Add next to Charge payoffs. The system opens the Charge Payoffs Information 

page. 

2. 
In the Credit card drop-down list, select, or add the applicable credit card account. 

3. 
Click the Continue button. The system displays the Payoff details section and the credit card 

transaction list. 

4. 
In Date, select or enter the payoff date. 

5. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, select an existing attachment or add a new file. 

6. 
In the credit card transaction list, select the check boxes for the transactions you want to 

include in the payoff. 

7. 
For each transaction selected, edit the value in the Amount to pay column as needed. 

8. 
Click the Save button. 

Reversing a Charge Payoff 

You cannot edit charge payoffs because the system automatically links them to an Accounts 

Payable invoice. However, you can reverse a charge from the Charge Payoffs page. You can only 

reverse payoff charges that you haven’t paid. 

To reverse a charge payoff: 

1. 
In the Charge Payoffs list, locate the payoff transaction that you want to reverse, and then 

click the corresponding Reverse link. 

The system opens a Transaction Reversal Date box. 

2. 
In Reverse the transaction on date, enter or select the effective date for reversing the 

transaction. This date is typically the original transaction date or a later date. 

3. 
In Memo, enter a short description of the reversal. 

4. 
Click the Submit button to complete the reversal. 

The A/P invoice and the charge payoff are reversed, making the charge card transaction available 

again for selection. 

The Charge Payoffs page refreshes to display the transaction state as Reversal.

• 
Date: This field displays the transaction date or the date you entered the transaction into 

the system. Click the link to view the transaction page for each entry.

Vendor ID: This field displays the unique identifier assigned to the vendor. 

• 
Vendor name: This field displays the vendor name. 

• 
Payee: This field displays the payee name. 

• 
Transaction type: This field indicates whether it was a charge card transaction or a credit 

card finance charge. 

• 
Description: This field displays the charge description. 

• 
Total entered: This field displays the total charge amount of each transaction. 

• 
Total due: This field displays the remainder amount of the charge for partial payments.  

• 
Total paid: This field displays the total paid amount for each transaction.

#### Positive Pay File List
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 204*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Positive Pay File List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Positive Pay > Positive Pay File`


Use the Positive pay file list to view and manually generate Positive Pay files. Positive Pay files 

include the account number, check number, and dollar amount of each check your company 

issues. When you “generate” a Positive Pay file, the system transmits the file to the bank for 

review. The bank compares and matches the information in the files against checks that are 

presented for payment. If you scheduled your Positive Pay files, then the system will automatically 

generate the files on a daily basis according to the schedule dates specified in the Positive Pay 

configuration (on page 601). 

By default, the list does not show files created without any checks. If you want to see those files, 

select the Show zero check entries check box.

##### Manually Generating a Positive Pay File
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 206*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Manually Generating a Positive Pay File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Positive Pay > Positive Pay File > Generate File`


You can manually generate Positive Pay files to transmit them to the bank on a one-time, 

on-demand basis. This method also allows you to perform testing by sending test files to the 

bank with sample data. 

If you defined a schedule in the Positive Pay configuration (on page 603 ), then the system 
automatically generates the files on a daily basis according to the length of the schedule. 

To manually generate a Positive Pay file: 

1. 
In the Positive pay file list, click the Generate file button. 

The Generate positive pay file page opens. 

2. 
Click the Select link to select which Positive pay configuration(s) to generate files for. See 

Using the Multi-Select Box for more information. 

3. 
If you are providing a file to the bank for testing purposes, select the Test file with sample 

data check box. Otherwise, do not select this option. 

Test files contain accurate bank information but fake payment information. 

4. 
Under Options, select which checks to generate the file for: 

• 
Checks not sent: Generates a Positive Pay file for any checks that have not been 

marked as sent. 

• 
Checks in a date range: Generates a Positive Pay file for any checks within the selected 

date range. Type or select the starting date and ending date in the Date from and 

Date to fields, respectively. 

5. 
Click the Generate button. 

The system generates the file and transmits it to the bank for review. The file will be 

formatted according to the layout specifications defined in the Positive Pay configuration.  

You can view the status of the generated file under the State column in the Positive pay file 

list. To download a copy of the file, click the Download link. 

---



##### Deleting a Positive Pay File
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 207*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Deleting a Positive Pay File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Positive Pay > Positive Pay File > Delete`


Deleting a file from the Positive pay file list permanently deletes the record from the RealPage 

Accounting system. Positive Pay files contain lists of checks issued by your company and sent to 

the bank to help prevent fraud such as counterfeit checks; be careful not to delete any files you 

want to maintain for your company’s record-keeping. 

To delete a Positive Pay file: 

1. 
In the Positive pay file list, click the Delete link next to the file. 

A confirmation box opens. 

2. 
Click OK to proceed. 

---

range.

Pay configuration. For example, if you set the Effective date as 
1/01/2023 and the file generation date is 3/15/2023, the 
File date 

range would be 1/01/2023 - 3/15/2023. 

The Effective date determines how far back the system looks for checks 
that have not been marked as sent. For each run, the system checks if any 
confirmed payments within the file date range have not been sent in a 
Positive Pay file. 

Date created

#### Bank Reconciliation (New)
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 224*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Bank Reconciliation (New) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New!`


The bank reconciliation feature includes: 

• 
Reconciliation box (on page 215): Use this box to select the bank account to reconcile, add 

initial open items, and import a bank file. 

• 
Reconcile bank account page (on page 229): Use this page to complete the reconciliation, 

view transactions, unmatch transactions, create adjusting entries, or view alternate bank 

accounts. 

Reconciliation in Multi-Entity Companies 

In a multi-entity company, you can reconcile any account for which you have top-level access or 

equal or greater entity restrictions than the bank account. 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you reconcile the account at the 

level where you created that account. In other words, if you created the account at the top level, 

then you reconcile at the top level. 

Best Practices 

• 
To correctly account and reconcile all transactions to your bank statement, conduct or 

record transactions with your foreign currency bank only in that bank’s currency. For 

example, you should generally transact only in Canadian dollars with a Canadian bank. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 225*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
If your bank uses a different exchange rate from transactions in your accounting system, 

then adjust the exchange rate differences by booking a G/L journal entry for your bank 

reconciliation to complete your month-end bank reconciliation. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to reconcile bank accounts. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Cash Management 
Reconciliation – Bank 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Reconcile, 

Report, Reopen, Attachment 

Reconciliation – Credit Card

Accounts Payable

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Before your first reconciliation, gather the following items: 

• 
Last reconciliation from your previous accounting system: Obtain a report from your 

previous accounting system of the last reconciliation you completed for the account. This 

report should include a list of transactions that did not clear the bank at the time you 

reconciled. 

• 
Current bank statement: Prepare the bank statement for the first statement period that you 

want to reconcile. 

Before reconciling, make sure that you’ve entered any recent transactions that affect 
that bank account. For example, enter any wire transfers, manual payments, or deposits 
that may have been processed by your bank but haven’t yet been recorded in RealPage 
Accounting. 

Although GAAP journal entries appear in the reconciliation process, GAAP transactions do not 

affect the book balance total. A GAAP book is used solely to create financial adjustment journal 

entries for reporting purposes only.

Adding Initial Open Items 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New!`


Use the Initial open items button to enter transactions that will be included in the initial 

reconciliation. This button will appear only if the account has not been reconciled. After the 

account is reconciled for the first time, the button will not appear as an option for that account 

when reconciling. 

Negative initial open items can cause data issues in your reconciliation. Use positive entries 
instead. For example, instead of entering a deposit of -$10.00, enter a check with a value of 
$10.00. 

To add initial open items one at a time: 

1. 
In the Reconciliation box, click the Initial open items button. The system opens the Initial 

open items list. 

2. 
Click the Add button. The system opens the Initial open items box. 

3. 
In the Date field, enter the transaction date. 

4. 
In the Doc no field, type the transaction’s document number.

easier.

the account, so that you can reconcile them along with any new activity that occurred during the 

current statement period.

Download the Template

A separate Initial open items page opens.

Enter the Transactions

a time. Refer to the column descriptions to determine what you should enter for each 

transaction. 

2. 
Enter your transactions, and then save the spreadsheet. 

Import the Data 

1. 
On the Initial open items page, click the Choose file button. 

If you returned to the Reconciliation box, click the Initial open items button, and then click 
the Import button to re-open the Initial open items page. 

2. 
Browse to the spreadsheet that you filled out, and then double click the file. 

3. 
In the Email results to this address field, type the email address to which you want to send 

the reconciliation results. 

4. 
Click the Import button.

list.

#### Reconcile Bank Account Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 241*

Reconcile Bank Account Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New! 
> Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation > 
Continue`


The Reconcile bank account page opens after you select the account to reconcile and import 

transactions from the Reconciliation box. Use this page to complete the reconciliation, view 

transactions, manually match transactions, unmatch transactions, and create adjusting entries. 

• 
The header shows a summary of the current reconciliation status, including the current book 

balance and the amount left to reconcile. 

• 
The Recon detail section expands to show the full reconciliation details, including the 

matched and unmatched amounts, the Quick match options where you can specify a range 

of checks or transaction document numbers to match multiple transactions at the same 

time, and the filter options for transactions. 

• 
The RealPage and Bank sections display a list of transactions in the system and imported 

transactions, respectively.  

Filters 

By default, the Reconcile bank account page displays all transactions for the bank account—both 

matched and unmatched—regardless of the transaction type.  

You can filter the list by state (matched or unmatched), transaction type, bank amount, check or 

document number, and more. See Filtering and Sorting Transactions (on page 230) for more 

information. 

---

RealPage vs. Bank Transactions 

The Reconcile bank account page contains two lists of transactions: 

• 
RealPage: This section displays a list of transactions that were entered into RealPage 

Accounting directly. 

• 
Bank: This section displays a list of transactions that were imported from a CSV or BAI 

file. It appears only when you have imported transactions. 

Click the Match link to open the Find match page (on page 239) so you can match imported 

transactions with transactions in the system. 

Click the Action link to perform one of the following actions: 

• 
Create JE (on page 243): Create a journal entry when a matching transaction does not exist. 

• 
Exclude (on page 242): Exclude the transaction from the reconciliation. 

• 
Reconciling (on page 242): Mark a transaction as a reconciling item. 

After you reconcile a bank, you can view reconciling items in the Reconciling items list (on page 

322). 

More Actions 

Click the More actions button in the upper-right corner of the page to perform additional tasks 

during reconciliation: 

• 
Adding bank interest and service charges 

• 
Creating a journal entry 

• 
Adding a manual payment 

• 
Adding a receipt 

• 
Making a deposit 

• 
Transferring funds 

• 
Paying A/P invoices 

• 
Applying payments 

• 
Adding bank transactions 

Each page will open in the form of a pop-up box so you don’t have to leave the Reconcile bank 

account page.

By default, the Reconcile bank account page displays all transactions—matched or 

unmatched—regardless of transaction type. However, you can filter and sort the list of 

transactions to target the transactions you need. 

Filtering Transactions 

Apply one or more filters to filter the list of transactions by specific criteria: 

1. 
On the Reconcile bank account page, click and expand the Recon detail section. 

The full bank reconciliation details appear, including filter options for your transactions. 

2. 
In the State drop-down list, select the transaction status by which you want to filter. 

• 
All 

• 
Unmatched 

• 
Matched 

3. 
In the Transaction type drop-down list, select the type for which you want to filter. 

• 
All 

• 
Checks/debits 

• 
Deposits/credits 

4. 
In the Bank amount field, type a specific transaction amount. 

5. 
In the Check # range and Doc # range fields, type a range of check numbers or document 

reference numbers to find specific checks or transactions. 

If needed, you can apply additional filters. See the next section for instructions. 

6. 
Click the Apply filters button. 

Using Advanced Filters 

To apply additional filters: 

1. 
Click the More filters link, and then set filter criteria as needed: 

• 
Check #/doc #: Type a check number or document reference number to find a specific 

check or transaction. 

• 
Transaction date range or Date range: Type or select a beginning and ending 

transaction date to filter by a range of dates. 

---


<!-- Page 244 -->
Periodic Tasks

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
G/L posting date range: Type or select a beginning and ending G/L posting date to 

filter by a range of dates. 

• 
Payee: Type the vendor or customer name to filter by transactions associated with a 

specific vendor or customer name. 

• 
Description: Type the description text that was entered on the transaction(s). 

• 
Bank currency: Select the bank currency. This field appears only if your company uses 

multiple currencies. 

• 
Bank amount range: Set a bank amount range to filter transactions by bill amount. 

In the Bank amount range drop-down list, select >=, =, or >. 

Type a bottom-of-range amount in the Amount field. 

In the third field, select <= or <. 

In the second Amount field, type a top-of-range amount. 

• 
Transaction currency: Select the transaction currency. This field appears only if your 

company uses multiple currencies. 

• 
Transaction amount range: Set a transaction amount range to filter transactions by 

transaction amount. 

In the Transaction amount range drop-down list, select >=, =, or >. 

Type a bottom-of-range amount in the Amount field. 

In the third field, select <= or <. 

In the second Amount field, type a top-of-range amount. 

• 
Payment status: Select the Voided or Reversed check box to display all voided or 

reversed transactions. The system displays both the original transaction and the 

reversed transaction to help you reconcile them. 

2. 
Click the Apply filters button. 

Using Quick Filters 

The Reconcile bank account page includes several Quick filters to quickly display unmatched

RealPage section above the list of transactions.

Reconciling an Account Manually 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New! 
> Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation > 
Continue`


If you are matching transactions entered into RealPage Accounting against a physical copy of 

your bank statement—or if there are unmatched transactions remaining after importing a bank 

file (on page 269) or auto-matching transactions (on page 283) through reconciliation rules—then 

you can match the transactions manually. RealPage Accounting allows you to match transactions 

on a one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many basis. 

The Reconcile bank account page displays two sections from which you can match transactions: 

• 
RealPage: Displays transactions created in the system. 

• 
Bank: Displays imported transactions and retrieved bank feeds. 

Manually Reconciling a Bank Account 

To manually reconcile a bank account: 

1. 
On the Reconcile bank account page, apply filters (on page 279) as needed to filter the list 

of transactions. 

2. 
In the RealPage section, select the check box next to the RealPage transaction(s) you want 

to match. 

You can match different transaction types (on page 283 ) on a bank reconciliation if the 

Remaining amount to match field is zero. For example, you can match a single check to a 

---


<!-- Page 246 -->
Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

mix of checks and deposits or a single deposit to a mix of deposits and checks. This applies 
only when matching transactions on a one-to-many basis, not many-to-many.  

3. 
Click the Match transactions button. 

The system updates the Amount to reconcile field. 

4. 
If the Amount to reconcile field is not zero, you can create adjusting entries (on page 292), 

or you can save your work, and then complete the reconciliation at a later time. 

5. 
When the Amount to reconcile field is zero, click the Reconcile button to complete the 

reconciliation. 

If bank reconciliations require approval, then click the Submit button. This option is 
available only if you have permission to submit transactions for approval. 

Manually Reconciling Unmatched Transactions 

If you imported a bank file and there are still unmatched transactions—or if auto-matching was 

not able to match all of your transactions—you can continue manually matching them: 

1. 
Apply filters to display the applicable transactions. 

2. 
Select the check box for an existing transaction, and then click the Match link to open the 

Find match page. 

3. 
On the Find match page, select one or more transactions to match with your transaction, 

and then click the Match button. Alternatively, click the Match and go to next button to go 

to the next available transaction for mapping. 

The system updates the remaining amount to match. 

You can match different transaction types (on page 283 ) on a bank reconciliation if the 
amount in the Remaining to match field is zero. For example, you can match a single check 
to a mix of checks and deposits or a single deposit to a mix of deposits and checks. The 
transaction amounts do not have to be a one-to-one match as long as the total amount 
being matched is equal.  

4. 
When the Amount to reconcile field is zero, click the Reconcile button to complete the 

reconciliation.  

If bank reconciliations require approval, then click the Submit button. This option is 
available only if you have permission to submit transactions for approval. 

If the Amount to reconcile field is not zero, you can create adjusting entries (on page 
292 ), or you can save your work and complete the reconciliation at a later time.

##### Reconciling Accounts with Intelligent Bank Matching
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 247*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Reconciling Accounts with Intelligent Bank Matching 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > 
 Rules`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > 
 Rule Sets`


Intelligent bank matching allows you to expand the criteria for auto-matching transactions in 

RealPage Accounting to bank transactions from bank feeds, BAI files, or CSV files. You can set up 

multiple reconciliation rules to match bank transactions on a one-to-many or many-to-many basis 

as they are imported into RealPage Accounting. 

If auto-matching is not able to match all of your transactions, then you can manually match (on 
page 280 ) the remaining unmatched transactions. 

To use intelligent bank matching, you’ll need to set up rules (on page 567) and then pair them 

with rule sets (on page 559): 

• 
Rules determine the logic that the system will use to match bank transactions to 

transactions in RealPage Accounting.  

• 
Rule sets apply a set of rules to one or more bank accounts. The system will apply the rules 

in the order you configure them. 

Default rules (on page 554 ) are set up for checks and deposits; however, you can create 
additional rules to suit your business needs.

##### Matching Bank Transactions Without Matching to G/L Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 248*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Matching Bank Transactions Without Matching to G/L Transactions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New! 
> Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation > 
Continue`


If the balance of your bank account is transferred to a separate account at the end of each day 

and then transferred back the next morning, you will see a record of these ins and outs recorded 

in the Bank section on the Reconcile bank account page, but there won’t be any G/L transactions 

to match them with in the RealPage section. For example, you might see a transaction 

for -120,000 at the end of 12/2, a transaction for 120,000 at the start of 12/3, a transaction 

for -110,000 at the end of 12/3, a transaction for 110,000 at the start of 12/4, and so on. This can 

be cumbersome during bank reconciliations as you will accrue around 60 bank transactions a 

month. To help you quickly clear out these account transfers, RealPage Accounting allows you to 

mark the bank transactions as Matched without actually matching them to any G/L transactions. 

To quickly clear out bank transactions recorded for account transfers: 

1. 
In the Bank section, select all of the bank transactions you want to clear. You can select 

transactions individually or select the check box in the column header to select all 

transactions at once. 

The Remaining amount to match field changes to reflect the total amount of the selected 

transactions. 

2. 
Click the Match transactions button at the top of the Bank section. 

The State of each transaction changes to Matched. 

---



##### Matching Different Transaction Types if the Amount to Match is Zero
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 249*



##### Matching a Range of Checks (Quick Match)
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 249*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Matching Different Transaction Types if the Amount to Match is Zero 

You can match different transaction types (i.e. debits and credits) on a bank reconciliation as long 

as the Remaining amount to match is zero. For example, you could match a single check to a mix 

of checks and deposits or a single deposit to a mix of deposits and checks. 

Consider the following scenario: 

• 
One bank transaction—a check in the amount of $3,730.62. 

• 
Three RealPage transactions—a check for $3,653.70, a check for $96.15, and a deposit for 

$19.23. 

Even though the RealPage transactions include a mix of checks and deposits, the system will still 

allow you to match them to the bank transaction because they add up to the same amount, 

$3,730.62. The Remaining amount to match will be zero because the sum totals are equal. 

Matching a Range of Checks (Quick Match) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New! 
> Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation > 
Continue`


Use the Quick match options section of the Reconcile bank account page to match or unmatch all 

of the transactions in a range of checks.  

This feature is not available for bank feeds or transactions that you import in CSV or BAI bank 
files. 

To use quick matching: 

1. 
On the Reconcile bank account page, click and expand the Recon detail section, and then 

find the Quick match options section. 

2. 
In the From check# / doc# field, type the first check number in the range of checks. 

3. 
In the To check# / doc# field, type the last check number in the range of checks. 

4. 
Click the Match button or Unmatch button to match or unmatch the checks.

Fields 

Fields on the Find Match page are different depending on whether you’re matching RealPage 

transactions to bank transactions or vice versa. 

Header 

These are the read-only fields that appear in the header at the top of the page. They correspond

##### Troubleshooting Reconciliations
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 259*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Troubleshooting Reconciliations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank > Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation > 
Continue`


Reconciliation differences must be resolved before you can finalize the reconciliation. 

The following procedures walk you through resolving common reconciliation issues. 

Amount to Reconcile Field Is Not Zero 

A non-zero value in the Amount to reconcile field indicates an error made in the reconciliation 

process. 

There are uncleared checks or deposits. 

If there are uncleared checks or deposits for bank or check reconciliation, or uncleared charges 

and payments for credit card reconciliation: 

1. 
Make sure all transactions that have cleared the bank are marked as cleared. 

2. 
Make sure that you entered all manual checks and that their amounts in the system are the 

same on the statement. 

An item was accidentally cleared. 

Cause: 

You accidentally cleared an item that didn’t clear the bank yet. 

Solution: 

Only check off items that you are sure have cleared. Uncheck the item that was inadvertently 

cleared. Uncheck items that have not cleared the bank. 

Transactions were entered in a previously reconciled period. 

If there are transactions entered in a previously reconciled period: 

• 
If the transaction is in the correct period, reopen the reconciliation and reconcile again. 

• 
If the transaction is not in the correct period, edit the transaction to fall in an open period or 

the correct period. 

Other reasons the Amount to Reconcile field might not be zero. 

1. 
Verify that you entered the statement ending balance correctly. 

2. 
For first-time reconciliations, make sure that you entered the initial open items correctly and 

that you cleared the compensating initial open items entry. 

---


<!-- Page 260 -->
Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

3. 
Make sure that you entered all miscellaneous charges that appear on your statement, such 

as service charges and interest earned for bank reconciliations, or finance charges and other 

fees for credit card reconciliations. 

4. 
Verify that you selected the Clear check boxes for all of the checks, deposits, charges, 

payments, or adjustments that have cleared the bank. 

If the balance is still not zero 

If the balance is still not zero, perform the following steps: 

1. 
If you can divide the difference by nine, resulting in a whole number, go back and examine 

each item by comparing it to the amount shown on the bank statement. You can correct 

any error by making an adjustment in the G/L. 

2. 
Reopen the last reconciliation and examine a snapshot of your last reconciliation to check 

for errors in transposing two items that look similar, such as two $100 checks. 

If you still cannot find the difference, you can make an adjusting entry by clicking the Add interest 

& charges link and entering a debit or credit with the description “Reconciliation Adjustment 
Entry. ” However, RealPage does not recommend this action. 

Incorrect Reconciliation Ending Date or Balance 

Perform the following steps if you accidentally entered the wrong statement ending date or 

statement ending balance for the previous reconciliation. 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then select the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Reconciliation section, select View reconciliation histories.  

3. 
Find the previous reconciliation, and then click the Reopen link.  

The Reopen reconciliation confirmation box opens. 

RealPage recommends that you save a record of your cleared and open items before 
reopening a reconciliation. On the Reconciliation histories page, use the links to generate a 
Reconciliation report, an Outstanding Items report, and an Adjusted Items report. 

4. 
Click Yes to reopen the reconciliation. 

When you reopen a reconciliation for a period prior to the last reconciliation, the system 
reopens all reconciliations from that point forward. For example, say your last 
reconciliation was on 5/30, and you had previously reconciled on 4/30 and 3/30. If you 
reopen the 3/30 reconciliation, then the system will also reopen the 4/30 and 5/30 
reconciliations at the same time.  

5. 
Update the incorrect statement ending date or statement ending balance. 

---


<!-- Page 261 -->

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

6. 
Click the Continue button. 

7. 
Make the necessary changes, and then click the Reconcile button. 

If you are correcting the most recent reconciliation, your previously cleared items will still 
be selected. However, if you reopen a reconciliation from two or more periods back, all 
reconciliation data will be removed.

#### Why Doesn’t My Bank Reconciliation Balance Match the Bank Statement?
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 263*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Why Doesn’t My Bank Reconciliation Balance Match the Bank 
Statement? 

If your bank reconciliation does not match your bank statement, the difference is usually caused 

by timing, missing or duplicate transactions, incorrect statement information, or changes made to 

previously posted activity. In most cases, the reconciliation and the bank statement are not being 

compared on the same basis. 

Common Causes 

1. Incorrect beginning balance: If the beginning balance in the reconciliation does not match the 

ending balance from the prior completed reconciliation, the current period will not tie out. 

2. Incorrect statement ending balance or date: If the bank statement ending balance or 

statement date is entered incorrectly, the reconciliation will not match even if the transaction 

activity is correct. 

3. Missing transactions: Checks, deposits, or other items may be missing because: 

• 
They were posted after the statement cutoff 

• 
They were entered to the wrong bank account 

• 
They were not posted yet 

• 
They were excluded by filters or settings 

4. Duplicate transactions: Duplicate checks, deposits, journal entries, or adjustments can cause 

the book balance to differ from the bank statement. 

5. Outstanding transactions: Open checks or deposits in transit may still be valid outstanding 

items, but users sometimes expect them to appear on the statement immediately. 

6. Voids, reversals, or adjustments: Voided transactions, reversals, and manual adjustments can 

create differences, especially when they are entered after the original reconciliation period. 

7. Changes to previously reconciled activity: If a transaction that was already cleared is later 

edited, voided, or reclassified, future reconciliations may no longer match. 

8. Bank-only items not entered in the system: Service charges, interest, fees, or other bank 

activity may appear on the statement but not yet exist in the Financial Suite. 

9. Data entry or setup issues: Incorrect transaction amounts, dates, account coding, or bank 

account setup can all affect reconciliation results. 

How to Troubleshoot 

Use the following steps to compare balances, dates, and transactions and locate the variance: 

1. 
Confirm the statement ending date and ending balance entered. 

---


<!-- Page 264 -->
Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

2. 
Verify that the beginning balance matches the prior completed reconciliation. 

3. 
Review for missing or duplicate transactions. 

4. 
Check for outstanding checks and deposits in transit. 

5. 
Look for voids, reversals, edits, or manual adjustments. 

6. 
Confirm that bank fees, interest, and other bank-only items were entered. 

7. 
Verify the user is reconciling the correct bank account and period. 

Best Practice 

When reconciling to a bank statement, make sure both sides are being reviewed using the same: 

• 
Statement date 

• 
Bank account 

• 
Transaction population 

• 
Posted activity 

When to Escalate 

If the reconciliation still does not match after reviewing balances, dates, and transactions, gather 

the following information: 

• 
Bank account name 

• 
Statement ending date 

• 
Statement ending balance 

• 
Amount of the variance 

• 
Examples of missing, duplicate, or changed transactions 

Then route the issue for deeper accounting or product support review. 

---

#### Bank Reconciliation (Legacy)
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 272*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Bank Reconciliation (Legacy) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank`


The bank reconciliation feature includes: 

• 
Reconciliation box: (on page 263) Use this box to select the bank account to reconcile, add 

initial open items, and import a bank file. 

• 
Reconcile bank account page: (on page 277) Use this page to complete the reconciliation, 

view transactions, unmatch transactions, create adjusting entries, or view alternate bank 

accounts. 

Reconciliation in Multi-Entity Companies 

In a multi-entity company, you can reconcile any account for which you have top-level access or 

equal or greater entity restrictions than the bank account. 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you reconcile the account at the 

level where you created that account. In other words, if you created the account at the top level, 

then you reconcile at the top level. 

Best Practices 

• 
To correctly account and reconcile all transactions to your bank statement, conduct or 

record transactions with your foreign currency bank only in that bank’s currency. For 

example, you should generally transact only in Canadian dollars with a Canadian bank. 

• 
If your bank uses a different exchange rate from transactions in your accounting system, 

then adjust the exchange rate differences by booking a G/L journal entry for your bank 

reconciliation to complete your month-end bank reconciliation. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 273*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to reconcile bank accounts. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Cash Management 
Reconciliation – Bank 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Reconcile, 

Report, Reopen, Attachment 

Reconciliation – Credit Card 
List, View, Add, Edit, Reverse 

Initial Open Items 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

Accounts Payable 
Check Reconciliation 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Before your first reconciliation, gather the following items: 

• 
Last reconciliation from your previous accounting system: Obtain a report from your 

previous accounting system of the last reconciliation you completed for the account. This 

report should include a list of transactions that did not clear the bank at the time you 

reconciled. 

• 
Current bank statement: Prepare the bank statement for the first statement period that you 

want to reconcile. 

Before reconciling, make sure that you’ve entered any recent transactions that affect 
that bank account. For example, enter any wire transfers, manual payments, or deposits 
that may have been processed by your bank but haven’t yet been recorded in RealPage 
Accounting. 

Although GAAP journal entries appear in the reconciliation process, GAAP transactions do not 

affect the book balance total. A GAAP book is used solely to create financial adjustment journal 

entries for reporting purposes only. 

Multi-Entity Companies 

Reconcile the account in the entity in which it was originally created. For example, if you created 

the account at the top level, you must reconcile at the top level. Similarly, if you created the 

account in an entity, switch to that entity to reconcile that account.

##### Adding Initial Open Items
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 278*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Initial Open Items 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank`


The first time an account is reconciled in RealPage Accounting, the Reconcile Bank Account page 

will only reflect transactions made after the conversion to RealPage Accounting. Any open items 

from a previous accounting system must be entered manually in order to reconcile the account 

for the first time.  

Use the Initial open items button for reconciling the first bank statement following conversion. 

The Initial open items button appears only if the account has not been reconciled in RealPage 

Accounting. After the account is reconciled for the first time, the button will not appear as an 

option for that account when reconciling. 

The entries posted with the Initial open items button do not post to the general ledger. 

Use the Import button to import initial open items instead of entering initial open items manually 

when you have a large number of open items to enter. See Importing Initial Open Items (on page 

268). 

To add initial open items manually: 

1. 
In the Reconciliation box, in the Account to reconcile field, select an account that has not 

been reconciled in RealPage Accounting. 

2. 
Click the Initial open items button. The Initial open items list opens. 

3. 
Click the Add button. The system opens the Initial open items box. 

4. 
In the Date field, enter the transaction date. 

5. 
In the Doc no field, type the transaction’s document number. 

6. 
In the Type drop-down list, select whether the transaction is a Check/Debit or 

Deposit/Credit. 

For Check/Debit transactions, entering the name of the payee will make reconciliation 

easier. 

7. 
In the Amount field, type the transaction amount. 

---


<!-- Page 279 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Negative initial open items can cause data issues in your reconciliation. Use positive entries 

instead. For example, instead of entering a deposit of -$10.00, enter a check with a value of 

$10.00. 

8. 
In the Payee field, type the name of the payment recipient. 

9. 
In the Description field, type optional text to describe the transaction. 

10. 
Click Save. You can also click the Save & New button to continue entering items.  

The system refreshes the Initial open items list with the new transaction. 

After you have entered all open items, the account is ready to be reconciled.

RealConnect Lesson on Reconciliation

Reconciling an Account Manually 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank > Continue`


If you are matching transactions entered into RealPage Accounting against a physical copy of 

your bank statement—or if there are unmatched transactions remaining after importing a bank 

file (on page 269) or auto-matching transactions (on page 283) through reconciliation rules—then 

you can match the transactions manually. RealPage Accounting allows you to match transactions 

on a one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many basis. 

The Reconcile bank account page displays two tabs from which you can select transactions to 

match: 

• 
RealPage: Displays transactions created in the system. 

• 
Bank: Displays imported transactions and retrieved bank feeds. 

Manually Reconciling a Bank Account 

To manually reconcile a bank account: 

1. 
On the Reconcile bank account page, apply filters (on page 279) as needed to filter the list 

of transactions. 

2. 
On the RealPage tab, select the check box next to the RealPage transaction(s) you want to 

match. 

3. 
Click the Match transactions button. 

The system updates the Amount to reconcile field. 

4. 
If the Amount to reconcile field is not zero, you can create adjusting entries (on page 292), 

or you can save your work, and then complete the reconciliation at a later time. 

5. 
When the Amount to reconcile field is zero, click the Reconcile button to complete the 

reconciliation. 

---

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Manually Reconciling Unmatched Transactions 

If you imported a bank file and there are still unmatched transactions—or if auto-matching was 

not able to match all of your transactions—you can continue manually matching them.  

To continue reconciliation if there are unmatched transactions: 

1. 
Apply filters to display the applicable transactions. 

2. 
On either the RealPage tab or the Bank tab, select the check box for an existing transaction, 

and then click the Match link to open the Find match page. 

3. 
On the Find match page, locate the transaction(s) to match with your selected transaction, 

and then click the Match button. Alternatively, click the Match and go to next button to go 

to the next available transaction for mapping. 

The system updates the remaining amount to match.

Reconciling Accounts with Intelligent Bank Matching 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > 
 Rules`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > 
 Rule Sets`


Intelligent bank matching allows you to expand the criteria for auto-matching transactions in 

RealPage Accounting to bank transactions from bank feeds, BAI files, or CSV files. You can set up 

multiple reconciliation rules to match bank transactions on a one-to-many or many-to-many basis 

as they are imported into RealPage Accounting. 

If auto-matching is not able to match all of your transactions, then you can manually match (on 
page 280 ) the remaining unmatched transactions. 

To use intelligent bank matching, you’ll need to set up rules (on page 567) and then pair them 

with rule sets (on page 559): 

• 
Rules determine the logic that the system will use to match bank transactions to 

transactions in RealPage Accounting.  

• 
Rule sets apply a set of rules to one or more bank accounts. The system will apply the rules 

in the order you configure them. 

Default rules (on page 554 ) are set up for checks and deposits; however, you can create 
additional rules to suit your business needs.

##### Matching Different Transaction Types if the Amount to Match is Zero
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 296*



##### Matching a Range of Checks (Quick Match)
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 296*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Matching Different Transaction Types if the Amount to Match is Zero 

You can match different transaction types (i.e. debits and credits) on a bank reconciliation as long 

as the remaining amount to match is zero. For example, you could match a single check to a mix 

of checks and deposits or a single deposit to a mix of deposits and checks. 

Consider the following scenario: 

• 
Two bank check transactions, one for $3,711.39 and one for $19.23. 

• 
Two RealPage check transactions—one for $3653.70 and one for $96.15—and one 

RealPage deposit transaction for $19.23. 

In both cases, the sum total of the transactions is $3,730.62. Even though the RealPage 

transactions include a mix of checks and deposits, the system will still allow you to match them to 

the two bank check transactions. The Remaining to match amount will be set to zero because the 

transactions on both ends add up to the same amount. 

Matching a Range of Checks (Quick Match) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank > Continue`


Use the Quick match options section of the Reconcile Bank Account page to match or unmatch 

all of the transactions in a range of checks.  

The Quick Match feature is not available for bank feeds or transactions that you import in CSV 
or BAI bank files. 

To use quick matching: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
Click the Reconciliation option.  

3. 
Click the Continue button. 

4. 
On the Reconcile Bank Account page, find the Quick match option section. 

5. 
In the From Check #/Doc# field, type the first check number in the range of checks that you 
want to match. 

6. 
In the To Check#/Doc# field, type the last check number in the range that you want to 
match. 

7. 
Click the Match button.  

You can also unmatch a range of checks. Click the Unmatch button to unmatch the checks.

After you match all appropriate transactions and the Amount to reconcile field is zero, click the

1.

Editing or Voiding Reconciled Transactions 

If you need to edit or void a transaction from a prior period that has already been reconciled, 

reopen (on page 334) the reconciliation and make your change, then re-reconcile. This ensures 

that the reconciliations are still valid and maintain compliance standards. 

If you need to go back to a prior reconciliation period, after you make the necessary change, you 

need to re-reconcile all subsequent periods to make sure all of your information is correct.

Troubleshooting Reconciliation 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank > Continue`


Reconciliation differences must be resolved before you can finalize the reconciliation. 

The following procedures walk you through resolving common reconciliation issues. 

Amount to Reconcile Field Is Not Zero 

A non-zero value in the Amount to reconcile field indicates an error made in the reconciliation 

process. 

There are uncleared checks or deposits. 

If there are uncleared checks or deposits for bank or check reconciliation, or uncleared charges 

and payments for credit card reconciliation: 

1. 
Make sure all transactions that have cleared the bank are marked as cleared. 

2. 
Make sure that you entered all manual checks and that their amounts in the system are the 

same on the statement. 

An item was accidentally cleared. 

Cause: 

You accidentally cleared an item that didn’t clear the bank yet. 

Solution: 

Only check off items that you are sure have cleared. Uncheck the item that was inadvertently 

cleared. Uncheck items that have not cleared the bank. 

Transactions were entered in a previously reconciled period. 

If there are transactions entered in a previously reconciled period: 

• 
If the transaction is in the correct period, reopen the reconciliation and reconcile again. 

• 
If the transaction is not in the correct period, edit the transaction to fall in an open period or 

the correct period. 

---


<!-- Page 315 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Other reasons the Amount to Reconcile field might not be zero. 

1. 
Verify that you entered the statement ending balance correctly. 

2. 
For first-time reconciliations, make sure that you entered the initial open items correctly and 

that you cleared the compensating initial open items entry. 

3. 
Make sure that you entered all miscellaneous charges that appear on your statement, such 

as service charges and interest earned for bank reconciliations, or finance charges and other 

fees for credit card reconciliations. 

4. 
Verify that you selected the Clear check boxes for all of the checks, deposits, charges, 

payments, or adjustments that have cleared the bank. 

If the balance is still not zero 

If the balance is still not zero, perform the following steps: 

1. 
If you can divide the difference by nine, resulting in a whole number, go back and examine 

each item by comparing it to the amount shown on the bank statement. You can correct 

any error by making an adjustment in the G/L. 

2. 
Reopen the last reconciliation and examine a snapshot of your last reconciliation to check 

for errors in transposing two items that look similar, such as two $100 checks. 

If you still cannot find the difference, you can make an adjusting entry by clicking the Add interest 

& charges link and entering a debit or credit with the description “Reconciliation Adjustment 
Entry. ” However, RealPage does not recommend this action. 

Incorrect Reconciliation Ending Date or Balance 

Perform the following steps if you accidentally entered the wrong statement ending date or 

statement ending balance for the previous reconciliation. 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
In the Reconciliation section, select View reconciliation histories.  

3. 
Find the previous reconciliation, and then click the Reopen link.  

The Reopen reconciliation confirmation box opens. 

RealPage recommends that you save a record of your cleared and open items before 
reopening a reconciliation. On the Reconciliation histories page, use the links to generate a 
Reconciliation report, an Outstanding Items report, and an Adjusted Items report. 

4. 
Click Yes to reopen the reconciliation. 

When you reopen a reconciliation for a period prior to the last reconciliation, the system 
reopens all reconciliations from that point forward. For example, say your last 
reconciliation was on 5/30, and you had previously reconciled on 4/30 and 3/30. If you 

---


<!-- Page 316 -->
Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

reopen the 3/30 reconciliation, then the system will also reopen the 4/30 and 5/30 
reconciliations at the same time.  

5. 
Update the incorrect statement ending date or statement ending balance. 

6. 
Click the Continue button. 

7. 
Make the necessary changes, and then click the Reconcile button. 

If you are correcting the most recent reconciliation, your previously cleared items will still 
be selected. However, if you reopen a reconciliation from two or more periods back, all 
reconciliation data will be removed. 

Incorrect Initial Open Item 

If you mistakenly entered an initial open item: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
In the Reconciliation section, click Bank. 

3. 
Select the account to reconcile. 

4. 
Click the Continue button. 

5. 
Click the Edit button. 

6. 
Click the Initial open items button. The Initial Open Items box opens. 

7. 
Click the Delete link next to the reconciliation to be voided. 

8. 
Repeat the steps until you have voided all reconciliations, and then close the Initial Open 

Items box. 

If one of your initial open items was a check that a vendor did not cash, and you need to void the 

check: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select Journal Entry to open the Journal entries list. 

3. 
Click the corresponding View transactions link for the applicable journal. 

4. 
Click the Add button. 

5. 
Enter the required information, and then click the Submit or Post button, depending on 

your G/L configuration. 

6. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

7. 
In the Reconciliation section, click Bank to return to the current bank reconciliation. 

8. 
Select the applicable account. 

9. 
Enter the required information, and then click the Continue button. 

---


<!-- Page 317 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

10. 
Select the old check and the newly created journal entry to zero them out and remove them 

from your outstanding list of items. 

See also Editing or voiding reconciled transactions (on page 295). 

Missing Journal Entries 

If the transaction currency of the journal entry does not match the currency of the bank account: 

1. 
Check the journal currency: 

• 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

• 
In the Search & Find section, select Journal Entry to open the Journal entries list. 

• 
Locate the applicable journal, and then click the corresponding View transactions link. 

• 
Locate the applicable journal entry, and then click the corresponding View link. 

• 
Take note of the base currency. 

2. 
Check the bank currency: 

• 
Open the Cash Management menu.  

• 
In the Search & Find section, select Bank Accounts. 

• 
Locate the applicable bank account, and then click the corresponding View link. 

• 
Take note of the bank currency. 

3. 
Make sure that the currencies match. 

If the G/L account used for the journal entry does not match the G/L account used for the bank: 

1. 
Determine which G/L account was used for the checking account: 

• 
Open the Cash Management menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

• 
In the Accounts section, select Bank Accounts. 

• 
Locate the applicable checking account, and then click the corresponding View link. 

• 
Check the G/L account used. 

2. 
Determine which G/L account was used for the journal entry: 

• 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

• 
In the Search & Find section, select Journal Entry. 

• 
Locate the applicable journal entry, and then click the corresponding View link. 

• 
Check the G/L account used. 

3. 
Make sure that the accounts used match. 

If the beginning balance cut-off date used for the first reconciliation is incorrect: 

1. 
If this is your first reconciliation: 

• 
Open the Cash Management menu.

• 
In the Reconciliation section, select Bank. 

• 
Select the applicable account. 

• 
 Check the Beginning balance cut off date field. 

2. 
If you have reconciled more than once: 

• 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

• 
In the Reconciliation section, select View Reconciliation Histories. 

• 
Select the preferred output for download. 

• 
Check the beginning balance cut-off date. 

3. 
Make sure that the date is correct.

##### Setting Up an Account for Reconciliation
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 320*

Periodic Tasks

Setting Up an Account for Reconciliation 

To set credit card reconciliation options: 

1. 
In the Credit card drop-down list, select the credit card that you want to reconcile. 

2. 
In Beginning balance cut off date, select or enter when you want to begin the 

reconciliation. Typically, this is the day before the first day of the statement period. For 

example, if the first statement you are reconciling is for the period 8/1/2018 - 8/31/2018, 

the beginning balance cut off date is 7/31/2018. 

3. 
In Statement ending date, select or enter the date the statement ends. 

4. 
In Sort by, select how you want to sort and display the columns in the reconciliation list.  

5. 
In Group by, select Charges and credits if you want to group all the charges together and 

the credits together. Otherwise, select None. 

6. 
Click the Initial Open Items button to add in-transit items or items that were open as of the 

last reconciliation you performed in your previous system. 

See Adding Initial Open Items to add one transaction at a time, or Importing Initial Open 

Items (on page 268) to import transactions from a spreadsheet. 

7. 
In Ending credit card balance, enter the account balance at the end of the statement. 

8. 
In the Book transaction columns list, the system displays columns left to right according to 

the order of the items. Click the up and down arrows to arrange the items in the list.  

9. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, select or add a supporting document. 

10. 
Click the Continue button. 

After the first reconciliation, the system assumes that you already have account activity before 

creating this account, and there are no balances from your last reconciliation.
