##### Editing or Voiding Reconciled Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 321*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Reconciling Credit Cards 

Credit card reconciliation involves entering miscellaneous charges from your credit card 

statement and then checking off the items that cleared.  

To reconcile credit cards: 

1. 
Follow the steps in Setting Up a Credit Card for Reconciliation (on page 307). 

After you click Continue, the system displays the Reconcile credit card page with a list of 

items for reconciliation. This page is where you perform the actual reconciliation procedure 

that balances your account. 

If you entered initial open items, the system supplies an entry with the description 

“Compensating Initial Open Items Entry.” The amount of this entry equals the opposite value 

of the sum of open items. The entry corrects the difference caused by the initial open items 

because the system already reflects these. 

2. 
Clear the Compensating initial open items entry check box during the first reconciliation. 

3. 
Click the Add charges and other fees link at the right side of the page to enter any interest 

and bank charges.  

4. 
Select the Clear check box for each transaction that has cleared the credit card company. 

5. 
Click the Save button to save the cleared checks. 

6. 
When the Amount to reconcile field equals 0.00, click the Reconcile button. 

If your account is still not in balance after reconciliation, make adjustments, and then try 

again. When you return to this page, the system will display only uncleared transactions. 

If you exit the page without clicking the Reconcile button, the system will display the page as you 
left it the next time you access it. 

Editing or Voiding Reconciled Transactions 

If you need to edit or void a transaction from a prior period that has already been reconciled, 

reopen (on page 334) the reconciliation and make your change, then re-reconcile. This ensures 

that the reconciliations are still valid and maintain compliance standards. 

If you need to go back to a prior reconciliation period, after you make the necessary change, you 

need to re-reconcile all subsequent periods to make sure all of your information is correct.

Use the Consolidated file section on the Bulk bank feed import page to import a single BAI or

mapped to RealPage Accounting before you can import them.  

Importing a Consolidated BAI File 

To import a consolidated BAI file: 

1.

3.

4.

Importing a Consolidated CSV File 

To import a consolidated CSV file: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, below Reconciliation, click the Bulk bank feeds import option. 

The Bulk bank feed import page opens. 

3. 
In the Consolidated file section, select the CSV file format from the Type drop-down list.  

4. 
Click the Choose file button to upload the file. 

5. 
Create a layout to map the information from your CSV file to RealPage Accounting: 

• 
In the Layout name field, type a name for the layout. We recommend using the bank’s 

name. 

• 
In the Amount, Posting date, Document number, Account number, and Description 

fields, type the name of the column in your CSV file that corresponds with each field.    

The Amount, Posting date, and Account number fields are required to save and 
import your file. The Document number and Description fields are optional.

Importing a CSV or BAI File for an Individual Bank Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bulk Bank 
Feeds Import`


Use the Individual bank account files section on the Bulk bank feed import page to import bank 

transactions associated with a specific bank account.  

To import individual bank account files: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, below Reconciliation, click the Bulk bank feeds import option. 

The Bulk bank feed import page opens. 

3. 
In the Individual bank account files section, select any filters you want to apply to the list of 

Bank accounts: 

• 
Location/location group: Displays bank accounts associated with a location or 

location group. 

• 
Bank name: Displays bank accounts associated with a specific bank. 

4. 
Click the Filter button to apply the filters. 

A list of bank accounts matching your criteria appears. 

5. 
In the Type drop-down list, select whether you want to import transactions using a BAI or 

CSV file format.  

BAI files have preset specifications and do not require any additional setup in RealPage 

Accounting to import the file. If you are using a CSV file, click the Download CSV 

transaction template link to download the required import template. Fill in the template as 

follows: 

• 
POSTING DATE: Type the G/L posting date for the transaction using any valid date 

format. This is a required field. 

• 
TRANSACTION TYPE: Specify the transaction type, either “withdrawal” or “deposit”. 

This is a required field. 

• 
DOCUMENT TYPE: Specify the payment method used for the transaction. Valid values 

include “check,” “card,” or “ach”. This is an optional field. 

• 
DOCUMENT NUMBER: For checks, type the check number. For electronic payments, 

type the transaction ID. This is an optional field. 

• 
PAYEE: Type the name of the payee. This is an optional field. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the transaction amount. Use a leading hyphen (-) to designate any 

negative amounts; for example, -500. This is a required field.  

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description for the transaction. This is an optional field.

#### Bulk Reconciliation Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 336*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Bulk Reconciliation Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bulk 
Reconciliation`


Use the Bulk reconciliation page to manage bank reconciliations for multiple bank accounts 

across one or more properties.  

To reconcile accounts in bulk, you first need to populate a list of bank accounts by selecting a 

location or bank name filter. This displays a list of bank accounts that have bank feeds. From 

there, you can enter the statement ending date and ending balance that you want to sync to 

those bank accounts and then initiate the reconciliation process using the Start reconciliation 

button. After it starts, the system runs the auto-matching process based on your company’s bank 

reconciliation rules to match bank transactions with ledger entries, accelerating the reconciliation 

workflow and reducing manual effort.  

If there are any unmatched transactions remaining after you run the auto-matching process, you 
can click the Amount to reconcile link to match bank transactions manually from the Reconcile 

bank account page. When the Amount to reconcile field is zero, you can click the Reconcile 
button to reconcile the selected account(s).

Starting a Bulk Reconciliation on Demand 

If you have set up reconciliation rules (on page 554) for your company, RealPage Accounting 

automatically matches bank transactions to ledger entries whenever bank transactions are 

imported or retrieved from bank feeds. However, you can start the reconciliation process on 

demand from the Bulk reconciliation page. This page allows you to manually initiate the 

reconciliation process for multiple bank accounts. 

To start a bulk reconciliation on demand: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, find the Reconciliation section, and then click the Bulk 

reconciliation menu option. 

The Bulk reconciliation page opens. 

3. 
In the Statement ending date field, type or select the ending date to sync to the bank 

accounts that you will be reconciling. 

4. 
Use one or both of the following filters to populate a list of bank accounts: 

• 
Location/location group: Select a specific location or location group to view the bank 

accounts associated with it. 

• 
Bank name: Select a specific bank name to view the bank accounts associated with it. 

5. 
Click the Continue button to view a list of bank accounts. 

6. 
Select the check box next to each bank account you want to reconcile.

##### Reopening and Adjusting a Closed Reconciliation
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 347*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Reopening and Adjusting a Closed Reconciliation 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > View 
Reconciliation Histories > Reopen`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Reconciliation History > 
Reopen`


You can reopen a closed reconciliation and make adjustments to it. The system retains any 

documents or bank statements that you attached to the original reconciliation, so you don’t need 

to re-upload them. 

Before You Begin 

• 
Download the Reconciliation Report so that you have a history of what was originally 

matched and reconciled. 

• 
Make the appropriate corrections inside your company. For example, you might have 

written a check to a vendor but forgot to create the record in the system. 

Adjusting a Closed Reconciliation 

To make an adjustment to a closed reconciliation: 

1. 
In the Reconciliation histories list, find the desired reconciliation period, and then click the 

Reopen link. 

A confirmation box opens with the number of reconciliations that will be reopened. 

2. 
Click Yes to reopen the reconciliation. This action can’t be undone. 

3. 
In the Account to reconcile drop-down list, select the account that you want to reconcile, 

and then click Continue. 

The Reconcile bank account page appears. You can now re-reconcile the account for that 

period and for all subsequent periods that were reopened. For example, if you’re currently in 

the month of August and reopen the reconciliation from June, you need to re-reconcile for 

June and July. 

If you originally reconciled with an import file but now you are using bank feeds, make sure 
you have the original CSV import file. You’ll need to re-import the file. If you don’t have the 
original file, download the Reconciliation Report as a CSV or Excel file and manipulate the 
data to create a new import file. 

---

You can generate a PDF package that contains multiple bank reconciliation histories. Packages

bank statement. 

To generate a package of bank reconciliations:

In Finance Agent, select the Reconciliation History menu option in the Cash

6.

drive. 

• 
Summary: Include a summary page with a list of reconciled bank accounts that are 

included in the package. 

• 
Attachments: Include the bank statement attached to the reconciliation record. 

• 
Reconciliation report: Include a copy of the Reconciliation report for each 

reconciliation history. 

• 
Outstanding items report: Include a copy of the Outstanding Items report for each 

reconciliation history. 

• 
Adjusted items report: Include a copy of the Adjusted Items report for each 

reconciliation history.

The Approve bank reconciliations list displays a list of all bank reconciliations submitted for 

approval. From this list, you can: 

• 
View the details of a pending bank reconciliation. 

• 
Generate a report of pending bank reconciliations. 

• 
View the user who submitted the bank reconciliation for approval, including the date they 

submitted it. 

• 
Approve or decline bank reconciliations individually or in bulk. 

• 
Export the list of reconciliations to a CSV, Excel, or PDF file. 

You must have the Approve permission for bank reconciliations to access this list. If a bank 
account is set up at the entity level, then you need access to that entity to approve the 
reconciliation. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

##### Submitting Bank Reconciliations for Approval
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 356*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Entity Restrictions 

The Approve bank reconciliations list honors entity restrictions. If a bank account was set up at 

the entity level, then only approvers with access to that entity will be able to review and approve 

the reconciliation. 

Approval Notifications 

By default, submitters and approvers will receive email notifications related to bank reconciliation 

approvals. If you don’t want to receive these notifications, then you can opt out of them in your 

user preferences (on page 346). 

Submitting Bank Reconciliations for Approval 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Bank - New!`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation`


If you have the Submit permission (on page 343) for bank reconciliations, then you can submit 

bank reconciliations for approval. 

To submit a bank reconciliation: 

1. 
On the Reconcile bank account page, when you’ve matched your transactions and the 

Amount to reconcile is zero ($0.00), click the Submit button. 

2. 
After you submit the reconciliation, the system: 

• 
Adds the reconciliation to the Approve bank reconciliations list. 

• 
Sends an email to any users who have the Approve permission, respective of entity 

restrictions. 

• 
Locks the reconciliation to anyone who does not have the Approve permission.  

As the user who submitted the transaction, you can still view the reconciliation, but 
the Save button will no longer be available on the 
Reconcile bank account page. 

---



##### Approving and Declining Bank Reconciliations
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 357*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Approving and Declining Bank Reconciliations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Approve 
Reconciliations`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All  > Cash Management > Approve Reconciliation`


If you have the Approve permission (on page 343) for bank reconciliations, then you can approve 

or decline bank reconciliations that have been submitted for approval. 

Approving Bank Reconciliations 

To approve bank reconciliations: 

1. 
In the Approve bank reconciliations list, select one or more bank reconciliations. 

2. 
Click the Approve button. 

The system validates whether the amount to reconcile on the account is zero ($0.00). 

• 
If the amount is zero, then the account is automatically reconciled. The reconciliation is 

removed from the Approve bank reconciliations list and a new entry is added to the 

Reconciliation histories list. The system also sends an email (on page 347) to each 

submitter notifying them that their reconciliation has been approved. 

• 
If the amount is not zero, then you will receive the error message “You cannot approve 

the bank reconciliation because the amount to reconcile is not zero.”  

Declining Bank Reconciliations 

To decline bank reconciliations: 

1. 
In the Approve bank reconciliations list, select one or more bank reconciliations. 

2. 
Click the Decline button. 

The Decline comments box opens. 

3. 
Type the Reason for declining the reconciliation(s). 

4. 
Click Done. 

The system sends an email (on page 347) to each submitter notifying them that their 

reconciliation has been declined. The reconciliation is removed from the Approve bank 

reconciliations list. 

---

Opting Out of Approval Notifications for Bank Reconciliations 

By default, the system sends email notifications related to bank reconciliation approvals: 

• 
If you have permission to Submit bank reconciliations, then you will receive an email 

notification if your reconciliation has been declined. 

• 
If you have permission to Approve bank reconciliations, then you will receive a single, 

consolidated email at the end of each day with a list of bank reconciliations you need to 

review. 

If you don’t want to receive these notifications, then you can opt out of them in your user 

preferences: 

1. 
Click your user name in the upper-right corner, and then select the My preferences option 

from the drop-down list. 

The Preferences page opens. 

2. 
In the Email notifications section, select the Exclude from bank reconciliation approval 

notifications check box. 

3. 
Click Save. You will no longer receive email notifications for bank reconciliation approvals.

#### Debit Cards for Petty Cash
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 362*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Debit Cards for Petty Cash 

Site staff at a property—along with other staff in a property management company—often have a 

small amount of “petty cash” on hand for minor or incidental expenses, such as office supplies, 

postage, or travel. It can be difficult for a company to compare the actual cash on hand versus the 

amount of cash spent and what it was spent on.  

The Debit cards for petty cash feature in RealPage Accounting allows property management 

companies to track this petty cash through a prepaid debit card. The company can issue the card 

to a property with one or more authorized users or issue the card to someone who is not located 

at the property. After the card is issued and a cardholder purchases items with the card, their 

transactions are loaded into RealPage Accounting where they can be submitted as expenses to 

reimburse the petty cash fund. 

---



##### Configuring Debit Cards for Petty Cash
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 363*



##### Enabling Debit Cards for Petty Cash
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 363*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Configuring Debit Cards for Petty Cash 

Configuring petty cash cards, or PC cards, is a multi-step process: 

1. 
Enable the Debit cards for petty cash feature (on page 351) on the Configure Cash 

Management page and set up your expense categories for petty cash reimbursements. 

2. 
Enable bank accounts (on page 352) for RealPage Debit Card payments so the system can 

process payments for petty cash reimbursements. 

3. 
Set up permissions (on page 352) for cardholders. 

4. 
If you want to require approval for PC reimbursement invoices, then create an approval 

workflow (on page 354) that applies to the Petty cash reimbursement (PCR) transaction 

type. 

Enabling Debit Cards for Petty Cash 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration`


To configure petty cash (PC) cards: 

1. 
Select the Enable debit cards for petty cash check box. 

2. 
In the Payment processing subsection, select the time interval to send the payment to the 

third-party service provider. 

• 
Immediately: Select this option to immediately process the payment requests and 

complete the payment. 

• 
Process end of each day: Select this option to include the payment requests when the 

system processes all requests at the end of each day. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to manually process the payment requests through the 

Third party payments queue. 

3. 
In the Unrestricted users for submitting the expenses multi-select box, add one or more 

unrestricted users or user roles. Unrestricted users can submit expenses for cards even if 

they are not issued to them. These are typically administrators. 

4. 
In the Reimbursement categories section, define the expense categories that will be available 

when users are submitting their debit card transactions. The system predefines a number of 

expense categories, but you can add, edit, or remove categories based on your business 

needs. 

• 
Expense category: Type the name of the expense category or rename an existing 

category. 

• 
G/L account: Select the G/L account to map the expense category to. 

• 
Attachment required: Select this check box to require users to include an attachment 

when submitting the expense category. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 364*

If you have configured expense reports in Accounts Payable, then these are the same

What’s Next? 

When this feature is enabled: 

• 
A new sub-section labeled Debit cards for petty cash is added to the Cash Management 

menu in the Periodic tasks section to access the following lists and pages: 

•

•

•

your company. 

• 
Two additional reports are added to the Cash Management menu in the Reports section: 

• 
PC cards: Use this report to view all PC cards issued in your company. 

• 
PC transactions: Use this report to view all PC card transactions from a single property, 

user, or both. 

• 
PC billing: Use this report to view any PC cards activated this month or still active from 

previous months so you can identify which properties you need to bill back.  

Make sure to grant Cash Management permissions to users as needed for these lists, pages, 
and reports. 

Enabling Bank Accounts for Petty Cash Reimbursements 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts`


In order to process payments for petty cash (PC) reimbursements, you must enable RealPage 

debit card payments for your operating bank accounts at the top-level entity and property level. 

To enable bank accounts for PC reimbursements: 

1. 
In the Bank accounts list, click the Edit link next to the bank account. 

The Bank account information page opens. 

2. 
At the bottom of the Details tab, select the Enable for RealPage debit card payments or PC 

reimbursement payments check box. 

3. 
Optionally, select the Override MID and LID for RealPage debit card payments check box if 

you want to use an alternate bank account that is not connected with RealPage Payments. 

An implementation consultant will help set this up.

##### Issuing a PC Card
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 368*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Issuing a PC Card 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > 
Issue Card`


You can issue a petty cash (PC) card to a property and select the people who are authorized to 

use the card. 

To issue a new PC card: 

1. 
In the Cash Management application, select the All tab, and then click the Issue card 

option. 

The Issue card page opens. 

2. 
In the Property drop-down list, select the property for which you are issuing the card. 

3. 
If a contact record is associated with the property, then the Address for the property will 

automatically populate. Otherwise, select an existing contact or create a new one. 

The full property address is required when issuing a card. 

4. 
In the Amount field, type the amount of petty cash you’re funding to the card. This is the 

total card limit. 

5. 
In the Petty cash account field, select the balance sheet account. This will be used in the 

journal entry to reflect the distribution of funds. 

6. 
In the First name and Last name fields, type the name that will appear on the card. The 

combined character count of the first and last name cannot exceed 21 characters. Special 

characters are not allowed. 

7. 
In the Authorized users section, select one or more users authorized to submit expenses for 

the card. 

8. 
Click the Issue button. 

The system creates a vendor record for the card and creates an A/P invoice (a petty cash 

reimbursement invoice) to pay the original balance on the card. After the invoice is paid, the 

funds will be available on the card.

##### Issuing PC Cards in Bulk via Import
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 372*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Issuing PC Cards in Bulk via Import 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Petty Cash Cards > Template/Import 
Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card 
Maintenance > Import`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed 
on the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized 
based on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve 
created. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for petty cash (PC) cards: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Debit cards for petty cash section, click the Card maintenance menu option. 

The Card maintenance list opens. 

3. 
Click the Import button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

The Import box opens. 

4. 
Click the Download template link. 

The system either downloads the Petty Cash Cards.xls file or prompts you to open or save 

the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

5. 
Open the Petty Cash Cards.xls file and fill in the following fields: 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique ID of the property for which you are issuing the card. 

• 
ADDRESS_1: Type the property’s primary street address. 

• 
ADDRESS_2: Optionally, type the property’s secondary address information, such as a 

suite or floor number. 

• 
CITY: Type the city where the property is located. 

• 
STATE: Type the state where the property is located. 

• 
ZIP: Type the property’s ZIP code. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of petty cash you’re funding to the card. This is the total 

card limit. 

---


<!-- Page 373 -->
Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
PETTY_CASH_ACCT: Type the G/L account number for the balance sheet account. This 

will be used in the journal entry to reflect the distribution of funds. 

• 
FIRST_NAME and LAST_NAME: Type the name to print on the card. The combined 

character count of the first and last name cannot exceed 21 characters. Special 

characters are not allowed. 

• 
AUTHORIZED_USERS: Type the unique ID of the user authorized to submit expenses 

for the card. If you are authorizing multiple users, then you’ll need to fill in a separate 

row for each user. You can copy and paste the property and account information from 

the first row. 

The full property address is required when issuing a card. 

6. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

Importing Data from the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
Return to the Import box. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

---

Adding or Removing Authorized Users on a PC Card 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card

This topic applies only to petty cash (PC) cards that were issued to a property. 

To add or remove authorized users:

In the Card maintenance list, click the View link next to the card.

2. 
In the Authorized users section:

 Add icon to add a new row.

•

 Delete icon to delete a row and remove the user.

Increasing or Decreasing the Card Limit for a PC Card 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card 
Maintenance > View`


If you have the Update card limit permission (on page 358) for petty cash (PC) cards, then you 

can update the original amount of a card to increase or decrease the card limit. 

To update the card limit for a PC card: 

1. 
In the Card maintenance list, click the View link next to a card. 

The Issue card page opens in edit mode. 

2. 
In the Amount field, type a new card limit. 

3. 
Click the Update card limit button. 

• 
If the amount is more than the original card limit, the system creates a PC 

reimbursement invoice for the difference between the original amount and the new 

amount. 

• 
If the amount is less than the original card limit, the system creates a credit PC 

reimbursement invoice for the difference between the original amount and the new 

amount. 

These types of adjustment PC reimbursement invoices do not go through the approval 
process even if an approval workflow is set up for this type of invoice.

##### Adding Funds to a PC Card

##### Putting a PC Card on Hold
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 378*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide

Adding Funds to a PC Card 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card 
Maintenance > View`


If you have the Change funds permission (on page 358) for petty cash (PC) debit cards, then you 

can add funds to a card. 

To add funds to a PC card: 

1. 
In the Card maintenance list, click the View link next to the card. 

The Issue card page opens in edit mode. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the Add funds option from the drop-down 

menu. 

The Add funds box opens. 

3. 
In the Increase funds by field, type the amount by which to increase the funds. 

4. 
Click the Add funds button.  

When you add funds: 

• 
A PC reimbursement invoice is immediately created for the amount of funds added to 

the card. This type of adjustment invoice will not go through the approval process 

even if an approval workflow is set up for PC reimbursement invoices. 

• 
A credit invoice will be created 7 days after you add the funds. The credit invoice is 

used to pay the charge after it is submitted as an expense in RealPage Accounting. 

Putting a PC Card on Hold 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card 
Maintenance > View`


If you have the Update card status permission (on page 358) for petty cash (PC) debit cards, you 

can put a card on hold to suspend all card activity and prevent purchases from being made with 

the card while fraud claims are being reviewed or resolved. You can still submit expenses (on 

page 369) while the card is on hold, but you’re not required to submit all expenses associated 

with the card before placing the hold. 

To put a PC card on hold: 

1. 
In the Card maintenance list, click the View link next to a card. 

The Issue card page opens in edit mode. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the Put card on hold option from the 

drop-down menu. 

The Card status field changes to On hold. 

---



##### Canceling or Inactivating a PC Card
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 379*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Canceling or Inactivating a PC Card 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card 
Maintenance > View`


If you have the Update card status permission (on page 358) for petty cash (PC) debit cards, then 

you can cancel a card. Canceling a card is a permanent action; if you’re unsure whether you want 

to permanently cancel it, or you think you may want to use it again in the future, then you can 

inactivate it instead. 

You can’t cancel or inactivate a card if there are still open invoices for the card vendor in the 
system. 

Canceling a PC Card 

To cancel a PC card: 

1. 
In the Card maintenance list, click the View link next to the card. 

The Issue card page opens in edit mode. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the Cancel card option from the drop-down 

menu. 

The system checks whether any invoices for the card vendor are still open. Invoices are 

considered open if their status is still set to Posted, Selected, or Partially paid. If there are not 

any open invoices, then the card will be canceled. Otherwise, you will receive an error 

message stating that the invoices must be fully paid before canceling the card. 

When a PC card is canceled, RealPage Accounting creates a journal entry to debit the petty 

cash balance sheet account that was originally credited upon issuing the card. 

---


<!-- Page 380 -->
Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Inactivating a PC Card 

To inactivate a PC card: 

1. 
In the Card maintenance list, click the View link next to the card. 

The Issue card page opens in edit mode. 

2. 
In the Status drop-down list, select “Inactive”. 

3. 
Click Save. 

The system checks whether any invoices for the card vendor are still open. Invoices are 

considered open if their status is still set to Posted, Selected, or Partially paid. If there are not 

any open invoices, then the card will be inactivated. Otherwise, you will receive an error 

message stating that the invoices must be fully paid before inactivating the card. 

---

##### Submitting an Expense for a PC Card
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 382*

Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide

Submitting an Expense for a PC Card 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > Card 
Maintenance > View Transactions`


You can submit transactions as expenses on petty cash (PC) debit cards for which you have been 

issued or authorized to use. This can be done from core Accounting, the RealPage Accounting 

Mobile app, or Spend Management Site View for properties. 

To submit a PC card transaction as an expense in core Accounting: 

1. 
In the Card maintenance list, click the View transactions link next to a card. 

The Card transactions page opens. 

2. 
Select an Expense type for the transaction you are submitting. 

3. 
Optionally, type a Memo for the expense.  

4. 
If required, upload a supporting document for the expense, such as a receipt or invoice: 

• 
Click the 
 Add button next to the Attachment column. 

• 
Click the Choose files button. 

• 
Select the file you want to upload. 

• 
Click the Upload button. 

Attachments may or may not be required depending on the expense type. 

5. 
Repeat the above steps for each transaction you want to submit. 

6. 
Select the check box next to each transaction you want to submit. 

7. 
Click the Submit expense button. 

After an expense is submitted successfully, the system will create PC reimbursement 

invoices to request reimbursement for the petty cash. 

---



##### Splitting a PC Card Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 383*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Splitting a PC Card Transaction 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > 
Card Maintenance > View Transactions > Split`


You can split petty cash card transactions across different expense categories, properties, and 

allocations. RealPage Accounting creates one invoice per location so you can reconcile your card 

transactions more easily. For example, if you split a transaction across multiple expenses 

categories for the same property, then the system creates a single invoice consolidating all of the 

line items. 

To split a transaction: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, below Debit cards for petty cash, click the Card maintenance 

menu option. 

The Card maintenance list opens. 

3. 
Click the View transactions link next to the card. 

The Card transactions page opens with a list of transactions associated with the card. 

4. 
Click the Split link next to the card transaction. 

The Split Transaction Amount box opens. 

5. 
Click the 
 Add button at the end of the transaction row to add more line items. 

6. 
Type the Amount to allocate to each transaction. The total amount of the line items must 

equal the original transaction amount listed at the top of the box. 

7. 
Select the Property to which each transaction should be assigned. 

If your company has enabled allocations on invoices, then the Property column appears as 

Property/Allocation instead. This drop-down list includes a list of properties and 
allocations set up in the company so you can submit petty cash transactions more quickly. 
If you don’t see the option to allocate, ask your administrator to enable allocations on the 
configuration pages for Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and the General Ledger. 

8. 
Select an Expense type for each transaction. 

---


<!-- Page 384 -->
Periodic Tasks 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

9. 
Optionally, type a Memo for each transaction. 

10. 
If required, upload a supporting document as an attachment. Attachments may or may not 

be required depending on the expense type. 

• 
Click the 
 Add button next to the Attachment column. 

• 
Click the Choose files button. 

• 
Select the file you want to upload. 

• 
Click the Upload button. 

The system automatically adds the attachment to each line item. You can delete the 

attachment as needed. When you remove the attachment from one line item, it will be 

removed from all line items. 

11. 
When you are finished splitting the transaction, click the Save & Submit Expense button. If 

you don’t want to submit the expense yet, you can click the drop-down arrow next to the 

button and select the Save option instead.   

• 
The Card transactions page refreshes to show the additional transactions. These 

changes also apply to the Card transactions page in Spend Management Site 

Experience. The Transaction number now has a suffix corresponding with the split line 

items; for example, -1 for the first line item, -2 for the second line item, and so on. 

• 
After an expense is submitted successfully (on page 369), the system creates PC 

reimbursement invoices to request reimbursement for the petty cash. 

If the total amount of the line items does not equal the original transaction amount, you 
will receive an error message.

Excluding a PC Card Transaction 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > 
Card Transactions > Exclude`


If you suspect a fraudulent charge was made using a petty cash (PC) card, you can exclude the 

transaction from the Card transactions list so it won’t be expensed or submitted as an expense. 

To exclude a PC card transaction: 

1. 
In the Card transactions list, select the Select check box next to one or more transactions.  

You can’t exclude a transaction after it ’s been submitted as an expense and the system 
has created an invoice for the expenditure. 

2. 
Click the Exclude button. 

The system hides the transaction from the list. 

Re-Including an Excluded PC Card Transaction 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Debit Cards for Petty Cash > 
Card Transactions > Include Excluded > Include`


If you excluded a transaction from the Card transactions list by mistake, you can re-include it in 

the list. 

To re-include an excluded PC card transaction: 

1. 
In the Card transactions list, select the Include excluded check box. 

Any transactions that were previous excluded will be visible in the list again. 

2. 
Select the Select check box next to the transaction(s) you want to re-include. 

3. 
Click the Include button.

periods for all entities or a single entity.

Use the Print payment copies page to print copies of payments made with checks. You can print 

copies of payments that you issued out of Accounts Payable or Cash Management. For checks, 

the system prints non-negotiable copies of the original check.  

The Print payment copies page also lets you send payment notification emails. Learn more about 

notifying vendors that they’ve been paid. 

Workflow 

Printing checks is a multi-part process, much like running a report: 

1. 
Set up parameters so that the system retrieves the records you want to print. Specify the 

coverage period, set filters, select the check range, and how to sort, and select desired 

payment notifications. 

2. 
Click View to retrieve the records you want to print. 

3. 
Select the records for which you want to print checks, and then click Print/Email.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Printing Payment Copies 

Printing payment copies is a two-part process similar to running a report. Set up filters for the 

system to find the group of payments you want, and then select the items to print. 

Open the Print Payment Copies page from either Accounts Payable or Cash Management. 

To print payment copies: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Print payment copies. 

To quickly see all payments sorted by check, in the Print payment copies page, click View. 
To refine the list of payment copies to print, click Customize to return to the Print 

Payment Copies filters page and follow the steps in Customizing and printing payment 

copies below. 
Copies of the check contain the same information as the original check. If any information 
changed since the check was paid originally (for example, if the contact name or address 
has changed), the copies will not reflect those changes.

1. 
In the Time period section, select the payment period from the drop-down menu, or type

period, the system uses the current month to date. You can specify either the payment 

period or the start and end dates, but not both. 

2. 
In the Filters section, set up the filters to get the specific data you want. 

Filters enable you to include or exclude specific types of data, such as banks, vendors, and 

check numbers. You can also include voided checks as part of the print run. As a general 

rule, to get fewer and more precise results, set more filters.

Setting the Time Period 

You can use one of the predefined payment periods available from the Payment period and As of 

date fields, or create your own payment period using the Start date and End date fields. 

To set the time period you want to search:

In the Time period section, define the time period for the report.

##### Setting Print Filters
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 401*

Chapter 3: Periodic Tasks

Setting Print Filters 

Use the filters to focus the results of your print job. In effect, filters enable you to isolate and 

assemble just the data you want. You can set any combination of filters. 

To customize your results, change the filters as follows: 

1. 
To select the types of payments to include in your print job, click the Payment method 

drop-down list, and then click the payment type to include (check, credit card, record 

transfer, cash, or electronic payment). 

2. 
If you selected Check for your payment type, select how many Checks per page you want to 

print by clicking the drop-down list. To print one check per page and include a check and 

vendor stub, select One. To use the entire paper space to print three checks per page 

(without check or vendor stubs) select Three. 

3. 
To select a particular checking account, click the Checking account drop-down list, and then 

click the account you want to include. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Administrators can preset a default financial institution in Cash Management 
configuration (Cash Management > All > Setup > Configuration). For multi-entity shared 
companies, you can set a default bank account on an entity-by-entity basis.`


4. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, use the Vendor from and Vendor 

to drop-down lists. 

5. 
To show results for a specific check or range of checks, use the From check and To check 

drop-down lists. 

6. 
To show voided checks, select the Include voided checks check box. 

7. 
To use the printed copies as remittance information for your vendors, then omit the 

watermark by clearing the Include File Copy Watermark check box. To use the printed 

copies as true internal file copies, then leave the check box selected. 

• 
This applies to any payment information that’s not part of a check stub. The stubs that 

accompany checks will always retain the File Copy watermark. 

The following filter options display only if you work in a multi-currency and multi-entity 

environment: 

• 
To filter the report by entity or entity group, select the entity or entity group from the 

Entity/Entity group drop-down list.  

You must select an entity if you want to run this report at the top level. The system 
uses the entity you specify to determine the appropriate currency. 

• 
Select the Show entity level checks check box to see the checks paid by the top-level 

company as well as the selected entity.

Sorting Payments 

Use the filters in the Check Range/Sorting section to control the sort order and the number of 

records to display per page. By default, the system sorts payments by date. You can sort by one or 

more of the items in the Sort By boxes. 

1. 
In the Check range/sorting section, in the Sort by, click the Select link to open the Selection 

box. See Using the Selection Box for instructions. 

• 
Click 
 Add to add an item to the Selected items list.  

• 
Remove an item by clicking the item in the box on the right, and then clicking the left 

arrow to move it back to the box on its left. 

• 
The system sorts the checks according to the order of the items in the Selected items 

column on the right. 

• 
To change the sort order of an item, select 
 Drag, and then drag the item to the 

desired sort order.  

2. 
To change the number of checks displayed on a page, in Max rows, select 50, 100, or 200. 

Sending Payment Notification Emails 

The system gives you the option to notify vendors and employees that they’ve been paid. Email 

notifications are available for vendor payments processed through Accounts Payable. 

For checks that you’ve already printed, you have the option to send payment notification emails 

from the Print payment copies page. 

You can also set up the system to automatically send payment notification emails whenever a 

payment is confirmed. If you set up automatic payment notifications, you don’t need to manually 

send notifications from the Print payment copies page unless you want to resend a notification. 

Learn more about Notify vendors that they’ve been paid. 

To send payment notification emails: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Print payment copies. 

3. 
Use the filter options to narrow the list of payments. You can also click View to see all check 

payments. 

4. 
Select the Email option for any payments for which you want to send notification emails. 

5. 
For each payment, verify that there’s at least one email address listed in the Email address 

field. 

If the vendor or employee has an email address on record, it is completed for you.

#### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 412*

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 401) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

#### Storing Standard Reports and Charts
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 415*



##### Viewing a Stored Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 415*

Chapter 4: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center. 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
Select the My stored reports option located in the Reports column of the menu. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
View Status: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud 

link for the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 408). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details. 

If you have not yet processed the report offline, then click the Create offline link to process 
the report.

You can generate reports on demand and store them in the My stored reports list for later

In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field.

Group on Demand.

In the Delivery options section, select the Store report option.

•

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime . 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you ’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets. 

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report.

#### Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 428*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 428*

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 416) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

A memorized report can be public or private. Public reports are available to all system users. 
Private reports are available only to the report owner and system administrators. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list (on page 418) and in the Reports 

center. 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Memorized Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 416) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Memorized reports list to view and manage reports that you saved in an application or 

that other users saved and then made public. From this list, you can: 

• 
Run memorized reports. 

• 
Edit memorized reports that you created. 

• 
Process large reports in the background and store them in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Schedule reports so that they run at a future date. 

• 
Delete memorized reports. 

• 
Export the list of memorized reports. 

Memorized reports are also accessible from the Reports center. 

Editing a Memorized Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 416) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

You can edit a memorized report or chart only if you are the owner or a system administrator, 

even if the report or chart was made public. As the owner, you can change any parameter, 

including who owns it. The only field you cannot change is the report type.  

To edit a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, click the Edit link next to the report or chart that you want to 

change. The Edit memorized report page opens. The fields on this page correspond with 

the report’s type.  

2. 
Update the fields in the General information section as needed: 

• 
In the Report name and Report description fields, type a new name and description 

for the report, respectively.

• 
In the Report owner drop-down list, select a different user to be the owner of the 

report. If you change the report’s owner, then you will no longer be able to edit this 

memorized report after you save the changes. However, you can continue to run the 

report if it’s still public.  

• 
Select the Public check box to make the report available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to make the report private; that is, 

available only to yourself and system administrators. 

Others can see private memorized reports by selecting the Include private check box 
in their Memorized reports list. 

3.

See the How to Get Here (on page 416) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports.

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, find the report or chart you want to view, and then click the 

Run link.  

2. 
In the Select report type drop-down list, select a format for the report or chart output:  

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file so you can view it in your web browser. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report as a comma-separated value (CSV) file so you can import the

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 432*

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here (on page 416) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 426) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 426) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

---


<!-- Page 433 -->
Chapter 4: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

---

• 
Years: Run the report once a year.

in the Every field.

the report results, and then click Save.

#### Adjusted Available Cash Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 445*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 445*

Chapter 4: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Adjusted Available Cash Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Adjusted Available Cash`


The Adjusted Available Cash report displays true balances for all bank accounts by including all 

pending transactions. For example, immediately after you complete the select-to-pay process, you 

can run this report to view your available bank balance. The cash balance automatically reflects 

the A/P invoices that you paid and any other applicable pending transactions that have yet to hit 

the bank (beginning balance – pending transactions = ending balance). 

All payments that are not yet confined to be pending bank transactions are considered as follows: 

• 
Selected: Amounts for A/P invoices selected for payment 

• 
Approved: All approved payments 

• 
Partially approved: Payments that are not yet approved by all required approvers 

• 
Rejected: All rejected payments 

• 
Unconfirmed check: Printed, but not unconfirmed checks 

• 
Delivered: ACH file generated 

On the Adjusted available cash page, you can set the time period, checking account, location, 

department, and more to meet your reporting output needs. In addition, you can format the 

report to show only the level of detail that you want to see.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Customizing and Running the Adjusted Available Cash Report 

To run the report immediately, click the View button. The system displays the report based on the 

default date. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button on the report page, and then perform the 

following: 

1. 
In the Time period section, fill in the following: 

• 
As of date: Use the default date or enter a date that determines the beginning bank 

balances and pending transactions included in the report. The system only includes 

transactions that occurred on or earlier than this date. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

• 
Show all pending transactions: Select this check box if you want to override the as of 

date and display all pending transactions. 

2. 
In the Filters section, fill in the following: 

• 
Checking account: Select the account by which you want to filter. This drop-down list 

displays all active checking accounts, including entity-level accounts. 

• 
Location: Select or enter the name of the region, country, state, province, or city to 

filter the report by geographic location. This option is only available for multi-entity 

environments. 

You must enter or select a location if you want to run this report at the top level. The 
location determines the appropriate currency. 

• 
Individual report: Select this check box... This option is only available for multi-entity 

environments.  

You must choose Process and Store if you select the Individual report check box. 

• 
Prompt on run: Select this check box...This option is only available for multi-entity 

environments. 

• 
Show for: Select one of the following options if you want the report to cover certain 

locations regardless of what you click in the location box. This field is only available for 

multi-entity environments. 

• 
All locations: Select this option if you want the report to include data for all 

locations regardless of the entity you are currently using. 

• 
This location: Select this option if you want the report to include data only for 

the entity you are currently using. 

---


<!-- Page 447 -->
Chapter 4: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
Child locations: Select this option if you want the report to include data only for 

child locations of your current entity. 

• 
Show details: Select this check box if you want the report in detail mode. 

• 
Hide bank accounts with no transactions: Select this check box if you want to reduce 

clutter in the report by only displaying accounts with transactions for the period. 

3. 
In the Format section, fill in the following: 

• 
Group by: Select how you want to group the information for display: 

• 
None: Leave this default option if you do not require any grouping within the 

report. This option is useful for generating raw data for easy manipulation. 

• 
Bank account ID: Select this option to display information outputs grouped by 

bank ID. 

• 
Bank name: Select this option to display information outputs grouped by bank 

name. 

• 
Subtotals: If you set the Group by option to bank account ID or name, you can select 

the one following from this drop-down list to display subtotals for the specified 

groups: 

• 
None: Leave this default option if you do not require subtotals within the report. 

• 
Payment method: Select this option to display subtotals by payment method. 

• 
Payment status: Select this option to display subtotals by payment status. 

• 
Payment method and payment status: Select this option to display first-level 

subtotals based on payment method and second-level subtotals based on 

payment status. 

• 
Sort by: Click the Edit link and select options to control the sorting of data in the 

report output. 

• 
Page orientation: Select whether you want the report displayed in landscape or 

portrait orientation. 

4. 
In the Titles section, enter a label and footer text for the report. 

5. 
Click the View button to generate the report.  

6. 
Click the Print button to generate a printable copy of the report.

Adjusted Available Cash Report Columns 

The Adjusted Available Cash report consists of the following columns:

Payment date: This is the A/P invoice date. 

•

employee name—for the payment. 

• 
Bank: This is the bank associated with the payment. 

This column appears only if you set the Group by field to “None” when customizing the 
report. 

• 
Payment method: This is the mode of payment. 

• 
Payment status: This is the status of the payment, such as Submitted, Approved, Printed 

unconfirmed, File generated unconfirmed (ACH), and so on. 

• 
Currency:  This is the currency associated with the bank account. 

This column appears only if your company has enabled multi-currency. 

• 
Amount: This column displays the payment amount. 

• 
Balance: This column displays the beginning cash balance in the account and the adjusted 

cash balance. 

This column appears only if you grouped the report by bank account ID or bank name.

Cash Balances Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Cash Balances`


The Cash Balances report displays balances for each of your cash accounts, and the totals for the 

selected accounts. Cash accounts include the following: 

• 
Checking accounts 

• 
Savings accounts 

• 
Credit card accounts  

The system derives the balance by adding all the transactions in the General Ledger account 

associated with the cash account. Unreconciled activities are included in the balance, even though 

the report notifies you if the account has never been reconciled, or if it has the date of the last 

reconciliation.

Cash Analysis Report

The Cash Analysis report displays the balances for your selected checking and savings accounts, 

including current amounts, past due amounts, and amounts due in the future. The report always 

includes amounts for Accounts Payable, but you can also add amounts for Accounts Receivable. 

You can customize the report to show increasing levels of detail that include totals for all A/P and 

A/R, subtotals for each vendor or customer, or an individual line for each document.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Cash Analysis`


To customize and run the Cash Analysis report: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Cash Management. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select the Cash visibility option. 

Filtering the Report 

In the Filters section, select any filters you want to apply to the report: 

• 
Bank account: Select whether you want to filter the report by all bank accounts, all checking 

accounts, all savings accounts, or an individual account.  

• 
Location: Select whether you want to filter the report by a specific location or location 

group.

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you want the system to generate only one 

report per location. If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store 

button at the end. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt the user to 

select a location or location group before running the report. 

• 
Department: Select whether you want to filter the report by a specific department in the 

company. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you want the system to generate only one 

report per department. If you select this option, then you must click the Process & 

store button at the end. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt the user to 

select a department before running the report. 

• 
Show for: Select one of the following options if you want the report to cover certain 

locations regardless of what you click in the location box. This field is available only for 

multi-entity environments. 

• 
All locations: Select this option if you want the report to include data for all 

locations regardless of the entity you are currently using. 

• 
This location: Select this option if you want the report to include data only for 

the entity you are currently using. 

• 
Child locations: Select this option if you want the report to include data only for 

child locations of your current entity. 

Setting Aging Options 

In the Aging options section, fill in the following: 

• 
Based on: Select whether you want the results based on the transaction date or the due 

date. 

• 
Display by: Select any additional details to include in the report. 

• 
Include accounts receivable: Select this check box to include the amounts for Accounts 

Receivable in your report. 

• 
Standard interval selection: Leave this check box selected if you want to use standard aging 

and future period intervals. Otherwise, clear the check box and specify the intervals. 

• 
Include invoices pending approval: Select this check box to include invoices that are still 

pending approval. Including pending invoices does not reconcile to the General Ledger. 

• 
Aging intervals and Future period intervals: Select your preferred intervals, or select “None” 

to create a custom interval. 

• 
Custom aging intervals and Custom future period intervals: Define your preferred intervals. 

---


<!-- Page 454 -->
Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Formatting the Report 

In the Format section, choose how to format the report. 

1. 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select whether to sort the report by Bank name or Account 

ID. 

2. 
Select a Page orientation, either Portrait or Landscape. 

Labeling the Report 

In the Titles section, define the report title, subtitle, and footer text: 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type a title for the report. The system assigns a report name by 

default, but you can customize it as needed. The report title displays in large typeface at the 

top of the page directly beneath your company’s name.  

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, type the text that you want to appear below the title of the report. 

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the PDF 

version). You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each field. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file. 

• 
Process & store: Allows you to process and store the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Add to dashboard: Adds the report to one of your custom dashboards. 

• 
Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file. 

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can email the report to others. Use trial and error to get the precise 

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 

process as needed.

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 458*

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can email the report to others. Use trial and error to get the precise 

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this
