PC Cards Report Columns 

PC Cards Report Columns 

Card ID 
This is the unique, system-generated card identification code. Click the link 

to view the card details.  

Location ID 
This is the unique identifier of the property to which the card was issued.  

Location name 
This is the name of the property to which the card was issued. 

Name on card 
If the card was issued to a property, then this is the Name on card that was 

defined when issuing the card. 

If the card was issued to a user, then this is their system user name. 

User 
This is the user to which the card was issued. 

If the card was issued to a property with multiple authorized users, then 

“Multiple” will display in this column. 

Vendor 
When a new card is issued, the system creates a vendor record for the card 

and creates an A/P invoice (with the PC reimbursement invoice type) to pay 

the original balance on the card. This column displays the name of the 

system-generated vendor record as Vendor ID--Vendor Name.  

Vendor records for petty cash (PC) cards are set to the Petty cash 

reimbursements vendor type. The Vendor ID will have the prefix “PC” 
followed by a unique four-digit number; for example, PC-0001, PC -0002, 
PC-0003, and so on. 

Balance 
This is the card’s outstanding balance. 

Amount 
This is the total amount issued to the card. 

Card status 
This is the status of the card: 

• 
Active: The card is active and can be used to make purchases. 

• 
Inactive: The card is inactive and restricted from making purchases. 

• 
Canceled: The card has been canceled and can no longer be used to 

make purchases. 

• 
On hold: The card is temporarily restricted from making purchases, 

but users can still submit their transactions as expenses.

Chapter 4: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Number of 

uncoded 

transactions 

This is the number of open transactions on the card that have not been 

submitted as an expense. Click the link to view a list of transactions 

associated with the card. 

Issued date 
This is the date on which the card was issued to the property or user. 

Canceled date 
If the card was canceled, then this is the cancelation date. 

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports in the system, 

and then access them with the My stored reports option in the menu.  

Email 
Sends the report as an email message. Click to open the Email report box, 

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report.

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 462*

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Customizing and Running the PC Card Transactions Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > PC Transactions`


To customize and run the PC Card Transactions report: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Cash Management. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select the PC transactions option. 

Defining the Report Period 

In the Time period section, define the time period for the report. You can either select the 

Reporting period and As of date or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period 

but not both. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 

Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

To run a report for a reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the reporting period. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select the date to begin the report coverage.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the reporting period 

and As of date when you run the report. 

To run a report for a date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage. 

Filtering the Report 

Optionally, in the Filters section, select any filters you want to apply to the report: 

• 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location or location group for which you want to 

run the report. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you want to generate one report per location. 

If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store button at the end. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a 

location before it will run the report. 

• 
In the User drop-down list, select a specific user for which you want to run the report. 

Formatting the Report 

In the Format section, choose how to format the report: 

1. 
Select a Group by option: 

• 
None: Does not group card transactions in the report. 

---


<!-- Page 463 -->
Chapter 4: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
Property: Groups card transactions by property with running subtotals for each 

property. 

• 
User: Groups card transactions by user with running subtotals for each user. 

2. 
Select a Page orientation for the report, either Portrait or Landscape. 

Labeling the Report 

In the Titles section, define the report title, subtitle, and footer text: 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type a title for the report. The system assigns a report name by 

default, but you can customize it as needed. The report title displays in large typeface at the 

top of the page directly beneath your company’s name.  

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, type the text that you want to appear below the title of the report. 

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the 
PDF version). You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each field. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file. 

• 
Process & store: Allows you to process and store the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Add to dashboard: Adds the report to one of your custom dashboards. 

• 
Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file. 

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can email the report to others. Use trial and error to get the precise 

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 

process as needed.

Location

Transaction ID 
This is the unique identifier for the card transaction. 

Date 
This is the transaction date, i.e., the date the purchase was made. 

Merchant 
This is the vendor at which the purchase was made. 

Expense type 
This is the expense category assigned to the transaction when it was 

submitted as an expense; for example, Hotel, Gasoline, Meals, etc. 

Invoice number 
After a transaction has been successfully submitted as an expense, the 

system automatically creates an A/P invoice for the petty cash (PC) 

reimbursement. The number assigned to that invoice appears in this column. 

Click the link to open the invoice details.  

Attachment 
This displays whether or not the PC reimbursement invoice includes an 

attachment.  

Amount 
This is the transaction amount.

#### Cash Visibility Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 470*

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cash Visibility Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Cash Visibility`


Use the Cash Visibility report to view your G/L bank balance compared to your external bank 

balance. 

You can use the Bank account holdbacks page to enter or import holdbacks and external 

balances. Bank account holdbacks, along with holdbacks from available cash (on page 635), allow 

you to set aside monthly expenses—not yet incurred—to ensure that you can make accurate 

payments. Holdbacks are subtracted from your bank balance so you can see the adjusted balance 

when paying A/P invoices.  

The Cash Visibility report displays your bank balance, external balance, and final adjusted balance. 

The adjusted balance reflects the total bank balance remaining after adjusting for:  

• 
A/P invoices you’ve selected to pay 

• 
A/P payments pending approval 

• 
Aging invoices 

• 
A/P invoices pending approval 

• 
Bank account holdbacks 

• 
Available cash holdbacks 

You have the option to include or exclude the Payments selected and pending approval, Total 

invoice pending approval, and Total holdbacks totals from the report. 

Summary View 

The Summary report view shows totals for Payments selected and pending approval, Invoices 

aging, Invoices pending approval, and Holdbacks with adjusted G/L bank balances.

Reports

Customizing and Running the Cash Visibility Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Cash Visibility`


To customize and run the Cash Visibility report: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Cash Management. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select the Cash visibility option. 

Filtering the Report 

In the Filters section, select any filters you want to apply to the report: 

1. 
Optionally, select a Bank account, Bank name, and/or Vendor type for which you want to 

view cash balances. Leave these fields blank if you want to include all of a property’s bank 

accounts in the report. 

2. 
Optionally, in the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists, select a range of vendor IDs. 

Only the vendors that fall within the selected range will be included in the report. 

3. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location or location group for which you want to 

run the report. This is a required field. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per 

location. If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store button at 

the end. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a 

location before it will run the report. 

4. 
Select whether to include or exclude the following totals from the report: 

• 
Include payments selected and payments pending approval: Select this check box to 

include the sum total of all A/P payments that you’ve selected to pay and all A/P 

payments that are pending approval. Clear the check box to exclude the total from the 

report. 

• 
Include invoices pending approval: Select this check box to include the total of all A/P 

invoices pending approval. Clear the check box to exclude the total from the report. 

• 
Include holdbacks: Select this check box to include the sum total of all bank account 

holdbacks and available cash holdbacks. Clear the check box to exclude the total from 

the report. 

• 
Show only default accounts: Select this check box to show only the default payable 

and receivable accounts set up in the entity. These are the bank accounts selected on 

the Additional information tab in the entity record. 

• 
Include savings accounts: Select this check box to include checking and savings 

accounts in the report. Clear the check box if you want to include only checking 

accounts.

Customizing and Running the Bank Transactions Summary Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Bank Transactions Summary`


To customize and run the Bank Transactions Summary report: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Cash Management. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select the Bank transactions summary option. 

Defining the Report Period 

In the Time period section, define the time period for the report. You can either select the 

Reporting period and As of date or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period 

but not both. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 

Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

To run a report for a reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the reporting period. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select the date to begin the report coverage.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the reporting period 

and As of date when you run the report. 

To run a report for a date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage. 

Filtering the Report 

In the Filters section, select any filters you want to apply to the report: 

• 
In the Report on field, select how to group bank feeds in the report: 

• 
Monthly: Shows the number of bank feed transactions added each month during the 

reporting period or date range. 

• 
Daily: Shows the number of bank feed transactions added each day during the 

reporting period or date range. 

• 
In the Bank name drop-down list, select the bank for which you want to run the report. 

Leave this field blank to run the report for all banks. 

• 
In the Bank account drop-down list, select the bank account for which you want to run the 

report. Leave this field blank to run the report for all bank accounts. 

• 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location or location group for which you want to 

run the report. Leave this field blank to run the report for all locations. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you want to generate one report per location. 

If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store button at the end.

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a 

location before it will run the report. 

• 
Select whether to include the total number and total amount of matched, unmatched, and 

reconciling transactions in the report. Additional columns will appear in the report with 

these totals. 

Formatting the Report 

In the Format section, choose how to format the report: 

1. 
Select a Group by option: 

• 
None: Does not group bank transactions in the report. 

• 
Bank account: Groups bank transactions by bank account. 

2. 
Select a Page orientation for the report, either Portrait or Landscape. 

Labeling the Report 

In the Titles section, define the report title, subtitle, and footer text: 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type a title for the report. The system assigns a report name by 

default, but you can customize it as needed. The report title displays in large typeface at the 

top of the page directly beneath your company’s name.  

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, type the text that you want to appear below the title of the report. 

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the 
PDF version). You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each field. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file. 

• 
Process & store: Allows you to process and store the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Add to dashboard: Adds the report to one of your custom dashboards. 

• 
Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file.

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you

Bank Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Registers > Bank`


You can generate the Bank Register report in detail mode or summary mode. In detail mode, the 

report shows all bank transactions with the reconciliation status of each. In summary mode, the 

report is highly condensed and shows only the bank name, beginning and ending balance, and 

the totals of the debits and credits. 

You can use the Bank Register report to void payments and reverse other types of transactions.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Bank Register report. 

Application 
Reports

Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Customizing and Running the Bank Register Report 

To run the report immediately, click the View button. The system displays all the report results for 

the default period. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button on the report page, and perform the following: 

1. 
In the Time period section, fill in the following fields: 

• 
Select a reporting period, and then set the baseline date for the reporting period. 

Leave the As of date field blank to use today’s date. 

OR 

• 
Enter a specific start date and end date. Leave the Start date field blank to include 

information from the earliest date you entered data into your company up to and 

including the end date. Leave the End date field blank to include all information from 

the start date up to today. 

---

Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

If you fill in all fields, the system bases your report only on the specified start and end 
dates.  

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box for the system to require a time period before it 

runs the report. 

2. 
In the Filters section, fill in the following: 

• 
Payment method: Select one or more payment methods by which to filter the report. 

• 
Bank account: Select whether you want to include all bank accounts or filter by a 

specific bank account. 

• 
Location: Select the geographic location by which you want to filter results.  

• 
Individual report: Select this check box to display each department and location 

combination on its own report page. Clear the check box to display the summary in a 

single report. 

• 
Show for: Select whether you want to display transactions for the current location, for 

child locations, or all locations. This field is only available for multi-entity shared 

companies. 

• 
Department: Select the specific department by which you want to filter results. 

• 
Show details: Select this check box if you want to display more detail in additional 

columns, such as the document date, description, document number, and 

reconciliation status. Otherwise, clear the check box to only display the beginning 

balance, debits and credits, and the balance. 

• 
Show only voided/reversed: Select this check box if you only want to include voided 

or reversed items. 

• 
Show reconciliation status: Select this check box to display whether the checks have 

cleared or are in transit. 

• 
Reconcile state: Select whether you only want to display items in a specific 

reconciliation status. 

• 
Hide bank accounts with no transactions: Select this check box if you only want to 

display accounts with transactions to remove clutter from the report. 

• 
Report by: Select “Document date” to see a report based on when the transactions 

were created, or select “Posted date” to see a report that matches the General Ledger.  

3. 
In the Format section, you can change the page layout and specify the sort order for this 

report by filling in the following fields: 

• 
Sort by bank field: Select whether to display results for each account by the ID or 

bank account name. 

• 
Sort by: Select the order in which you want to sort the results. If the Bank filter field is 

set to “All bank accounts,” the list is first sorted by bank, and then by the sort order 

selected here.

Bank Register Report Columns 

The default Bank Register report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Account: This is the ID or the name of the bank account. 

• 
Transaction date: This is the date of the bank transaction. 

• 
Description: This is the text entered to describe the bank transaction. 

• 
Transaction number: This is the check number for a customer payment or the check 

number for your payment to a vendor. 

• 
Cleared: This is the date on which the bank transaction cleared in the account reconciliation 

process. Transit indicates transactions that have not yet been cleared. 

• 
Currency: This is the currency for the bank transaction. This column appears only if your 

company has enabled multi-currency. 

• 
Payment method: This is the method used to pay the bank transaction. 

• 
Debit: This is the amount received for the transaction. 

• 
Credit: This is the amount paid for the transaction. 

• 
Balance: This is the running total of the bank account balance. 

• 
(Void/Reverse): This column contains a link for you to void or reverse the corresponding 

transaction. 

• 
Owner/Entity: This column appears only at the top level for multi-entity companies and 

shows the entity in which the transaction was created.

Check Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Check 
Register`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Registers > Check`


Use the Check Register report to view and output check register entries. This report provides a list 

of payments made through a specified bank (or multiple banks). You can view a list of payments 

made by check or view a list of all payments and their corresponding payment method (for 

example, by check, EFT, cash, or transfer of funds). 

The Check Register report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report.  

Reconciliation Status 

By default, the report displays the reconciliation status of each payment entry, such as In Transit 

or Cleared. You can disable this option as needed when you customize and run the report. 

Voiding Checks 

You can void checks from Check Register report or filter the report to show only voided checks. 

The Void option appears only when the following conditions are true: 

• 
The check has been confirmed. 

• 
You have the appropriate permissions. To void A/P payments, you need permissions in 

Accounts Payable to void posted payments and (optionally) posted advances. 

• 
If you are in a multi-entity environment, you are in the same entity that made the payment. 

For example, if you are displaying the Check Register report for the top-level entity and do 

not see the Void link, try opening the report for the entity from which the payment was 

made. 

You cannot void payments when:

•

##### Customizing and Running the Check Register Report

Customizing and Running the Check Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Check 
Register`


The Check Register report includes payment information so that you can know whether you paid 

an A/P invoice by ACH, cash, check, or transfer. This report offers both Summary and Detail 

versions.  

You can access the Check Register report from the Cash management application as well, but the 
content is tailored to display information for all transactions that affect the register, not just 
A/P invoices. 

Before running the report, you can select the time period and types of items to include as well as 

specify how you want the report to appear. 

To customize and run the Check Register report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices and Registers section of the Reports column on the menu, select Check 

Register. 

Filling In the Reporting Account Labels Section 

1. 
Select the Substitute with reporting accounts labels check box to use reporting accounts 

labels instead of the G/L account (or account labels, if enabled). 

2. 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the set of reporting account labels you 

want to use in the report. 

If you select a reporting account set of labels, you must also select the Display transaction 

details check box in the Filters section. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this decision 

at run time. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting Period and As 

of Date fields, or create your own reporting period using the Start Date and End Date boxes. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

In the Time Period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period and then 

either type a date in the As of Date field or use the calendar to select a date. These periods 

are relative to the As of Date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that is, the 

first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

---


<!-- Page 492 -->
Reports 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of payments to that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or use the calendar in each field to 

select the desired date(s). 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

• 
Select Prompt on run to have the system prompt you for this information at run time. 

If you don’t specify a reporting period and you don’t select Prompt on run, the generated 
report uses the current month to date. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set the Filters to get the specific data you want. You can include or exclude specific types of data, 

such as specific vendors and check numbers. 

To get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

1. 
To filter the Checking account drop-down list so it includes only the bank accounts set up 

for the Positive Pay feature, select a Positive Pay configuration (on page 601) in the Positive 

Pay configuration drop-down list. 

Positive Pay is a fraud prevention system in which you send the bank a list of checks 
processed by your company’s Accounts Payable department for a specific time frame. The 
bank honors only the checks that appear on the list. You want to include Positive Pay in 
this report to see what will be sent to the bank and what should have been sent to the 
bank. 

2. 
In the Checking account drop-down list, select an account to limit the scope of the report 

to the activity in only the selected checking account. 

3. 
Use the Vendor from and Vendor to fields to choose one vendor, a range of vendors, or all 

vendors.  

4. 
Select the Transaction currency if you want to filter the report by currency. 

5. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to limit the scope of the Check Register 

report to one location or location group. 

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per location. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual Report 
option. 

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a location 

before it will run the report.

precise results you want. Fill in the desired fields, and click View to see the report. To 
refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 
process until you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly,

Depending on your configuration, the Check Register report contains the following columns.

Columns 

Bank 
This is the account ID and bank name associated with the checking 

account. 

Date 
This is the date on which the check was written. When you pay A/P 

invoices, the register displays the date you set in the Set payment date 

to field. 

When the check date and payment date are different, both dates appear 

in the column. The dates are formatted as [Payment Date]-Check Date 

[Check Date]. For example, if the check was dated 8/14/2025 but the 

payment date was set to 8/15/2025, then the Date column would 

display: 

08/15/2015-Check Date (08/14/2025) 

The transaction date is often different than the original check date for 

voided payments. 

The Date column does not display two dates when the Sort by field is 
set to Date on the report configuration page.  

A/P Invoice Date 

(Accounts Payable) 

Transaction Date 

(Cash Management) 

This is the date that was entered on the A/P invoice. 

This column appears only if you selected the Show details check box 
before running the report. 

A/P invoice No 

(Accounts Payable) 

Transaction No (Cash 

Management) 

This is the record number assigned to the A/P invoice by the vendor. 

This column appears only if you selected the Show details check box 
before running the report. 

Vendor (Accounts 

Payable) 

Payee (Cash 

Management) 

This is the ID associated with your vendor or payee followed by the 

vendor’s or payee’s name. Click the link to open the Vendor information

Deposits Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Registers > Deposits`


The Deposits Register report allows you to specify a report by bank, and then filter the deposits by 

date or reporting period. You can also view the individual receipts in that deposit. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Deposits Register report. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

Cash Management 
Deposits Register

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Customizing and Running the Deposits Register Report 

To run the report immediately, click the View button. The system displays all the report results for 

the default period. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button on the report page, and perform the following: 

1. 
In the Time period section, fill in the following fields: 

• 
Select a reporting period, and then set the baseline date for the reporting period. 

Leave the As of date field blank to use today’s date. 

OR 

• 
Enter a specific start date and end date. Leave the Start date field blank to include 

information from the earliest date you entered data into your company up to and 

including the end date. Leave the End date field blank to include all information from 

the start date up to today. 

If you fill in all fields, the system bases your report only on the specified start and end 
dates.  

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to force the system to wait for you to enter a time 

period before it runs the report.

2.

Bank: Select a bank account from which to include deposits. 

•

deposits. 

• 
Show receipts: Select this check box to show individual receipts within each deposit.  

3. 
In the Format section, you can change the page layout and specify the sort order for the 

report by filling in the following:

•

Deposits Register Report Columns 

The default Deposits Register report consists of the following columns: 

• 
Date: This column displays the deposit date. 

• 
Deposit ID: This column displays the ID associated with the deposit. 

• 
Description: This column displays any text entered to describe the deposit. 

• 
Txn currency: This column only applies to multi-currency and multi-entity companies, and 

displays the payment transaction currency. 

• 
Txn amount: This column only applies to multi-currency and multi-entity companies, and 

displays the amount of the A/P invoice in the payment transaction currency (that is, the 

amount of the transaction in the vendor’s currency). 

• 
Base currency: This column only applies to multi-currency and multi-entity companies, and 

displays the value of the transaction in your base currency at the time the transaction took 

place. 

• 
Amount: This column displays the amount of the deposit in your base currency. 

• 
Reconcile date: This column displays the date of reconciliation.

Receipts Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Registers & Reports > Receipts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Registers > Receipts`


The Receipts Register report lists your receipts and enables you to perform the following: 

• 
Navigate to the invoices to which the receipts were applied 

• 
Navigate to customer information 

• 
Reverse transactions 

• 
Locate payments that have not been fully applied, where the amount received is greater 

than the amount applied 

You can display the report in greater or lesser detail, and restrict it to those receipts that have not 

yet been deposited. 

The Receipts Register report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

Multi-entity shared users can reverse transactions when they are at the top level of the company 

or at the entity that created the transactions. Otherwise, the Reverse link is disabled.

•

•

• 
Invoices: This column contains links to the transaction details. 

•

Credit Card Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Registers > Credit Card`


The Credit Card Register report lists charges and payments for a specified time period per the 

selected credit card, or all credit cards. It also shows the reconciliation status of each transaction. 

Charges can result from paying A/P invoices in Accounts Payable and recording miscellaneous 

charges in the Cash Management application. 

Typically, treasurers, accountants, and controllers who need to see where the money is going from 

your credit card accounts generate the Credit Card Register report. 

Multi-entity shared companies 

Users can reverse transactions when they are at the top level of the company or at the entity that 

created the transactions. Otherwise, the Reverse link is disabled. This report is not available to 

multi-entity shared companies that use multiple base currencies.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

#### Configure Cash Management Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 514*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 514*

Configuration 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Configure Cash Management Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Applications > (Cash Management) 
Configure`


Use the Configure cash management page to configure and define the settings for the Cash 

Management application. This page contains four sections: 

• 
Accounting: Use this section to configure the journal to use for posting miscellaneous cash 

receipts and the default account for undeposited funds. You can also enable and define 

custom categories for bank account holdbacks. 

• 
Banking: Use this section to select the default bank account for recording deposits and 

receipts. 

• 
Standard dimension display: Use this section to define the dimensions for tracking and 

reporting cash management transactions. 

• 
Third-party payments: Use this section to enable third-party payment services. 

• 
Available cash: Use this section to define the journal and G/L account for recording cash 

transfers, create custom fields for entering a location’s available cash information, and 

summarize account groups in the available cash report on the Available cash location page. 

• 
Escheatment: Use this section to define which G/L account to credit when a journal entry is 

created for a payment marked as “Aged Payable”. When this occurs, the original payment is 

voided, and the funds are transferred into this account as part of the escheatment process. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to configure Cash Management. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to configure Cash Management. 

Application

##### Configuring Cash Management
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 515*

Chapter 5: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Configuring Cash Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Applications > (Cash Management) 
Configure`


To configure Cash Management: 

Accounting Section 

1. 
In the Transaction summary posting drop-down list, select when the transaction summary 

automatically posts. 

• 
Daily: Select this option to post a single summary to the General Ledger for each 

transaction day. 

• 
Monthly: Select this option to create a single summary at the end of each month, 

regardless of the transaction date within that period. 

 We recommend the daily posting option because it provides the most granular reporting. 

2. 
In the Journal for other cash receipts drop-down list, select the journal to which you want 

to post customer payments. 

For dual-method reporting companies, the options include journals defined as both accrual 
and cash-based. 

3. 
Select the Account labels check box to restrict access to G/L accounts by requiring account 

labels. If an account label is not set up for a particular G/L account, that account cannot be 

accessed. Account labels are created in A/P and A/R, and they provide a plain-English 

equivalent for G/L account numbers, which can be helpful for users. 

4. 
In the If posting in future period field, select what happens if someone tries to set a future 

period date as the General Ledger posting date. 

5. 
Select the Allow creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency transactions check box to 

enable users to enter transactions in currencies other than your base currency. This option is 

available only if your company uses multiple currencies. 

6. 
In the Default exchange rate type drop-down list, select the exchange rate required to 

process foreign currency transactions. 

7. 
In the Default undeposited funds account drop-down list, select the account into which 

you usually record undeposited funds for it to appear as the default when users make 

deposits and record other receipts. 

8. 
Select the Disable journal entry from bank reconciliation check box to remove the journal 

entry links from the Reconcile bank account page. 

---


<!-- Page 516 -->
Configuration 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

9. 
Select the Show OneSite transactions in a bank reconciliation based on the posting date 

to advance OneSite transactions posted during the month-end close process (the “dead 

zone”) to the next month. For example, a transaction dated June 1st would appear in the 

June reconciliation period instead of the May reconciliation period. 

10. 
If you want to be able to pay entity A/P invoices from the top level, select the Enable 

alternate G/L for bank account check box. After saving this change, edit the entity records 

and select an alternate bank account. After configuring this feature, you can use the Pay by 

entity option where you can select an alternate bank account.  

After you enable this feature, it cannot be disabled. 

11. 
Select the Enable foreign electronic payment formats check box to allow sending different 

types of electronic payment files, including ACH, EFT, and BACS. 

After you enable this feature, it cannot be disabled. 

12. 
Select the Show recent credits applied to invoices on check/payment remittance check 

box to display recent credits applied to invoices in the last 30 days at the end of the check 

and grouped by vendor. This information includes the invoice date, invoice number, invoice 

amount, and credits applied. These are included in the Print payment copies and 

Remittance email sent after successful payments via check and ACH payment methods. The 

system also includes invoices paid at the entity level using credits. 

When printing multiple checks for multiple vendors, recent credits are displayed only once 
per vendor. 

13. 
Select the Use the current date as check print date check box to print the current date on 

the check instead of the payment date. 

14. 
Select the Use current date as the payment date for ACH check box to automatically 

update the payment date to the current date when you generate a payment file from the 

ACH file generation page. 

15. 
Select the Use current date as the payment request date for check payments check box to 

set the payment date as the current date when you choose to print the checks on days 

other than the selected date. 

16. 
Select the Automatically confirm checks when they are printed check box to automatically 

confirm checks while they are being printed. The system will run an offline process to 

confirm the checks when you start a new check run or print the check from the Print checks 

page. You will receive an email notification when the process is complete.  

Allowing the system to auto -confirm checks saves time and prevents printed checks from 
sitting unconfirmed. 

---


<!-- Page 517 -->
Chapter 5: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

17. 
Select the Advance posting date when subledger is closed check box to allow users to 

make end-of-month payments even if the Cash Management subledger is closed. When this 

option is activated, the system automatically advances any cash management transactions 

(deposits, funds transfers, bulk funds transfers, payments, manual payments, or other 

receipts) to the first of the next month if the books are already closed for the period you’re 

posting them to. 

18. 
By default, the system provides four (4) categories for bank account holdbacks. These 

categories are labeled Holdback 1-4 on the Bank account holdbacks page and the Cash 

Visibility report (on page 458). If you want to change the names of these holdback 

categories:  

• 
Select the Enable custom holdback name check box. 

• 
For each Holdback, type a new name in the Holdback custom name field. 

Banking Section 

1. 
In the Default bank account drop-down list, select the bank into which you usually make 

deposits and record other receipts for it to appear as the default when users perform these 

transactions. 

For multi-entity organizations, you can set a default payment method and bank account on 
an entity-by-entity basis on the Additional information tab of the Entity information page. 

2. 
In the Currency to use on blank check stock field, select whether you want to print the 

Bank account or Country currency on blank check stocks. 

3. 
If your company uses standard ACH payments, then select the Include invoice ACH details 

check box to add ACH details when printing checks. If your company uses multiple 

currencies, then select the Include invoice electronic payments details check box to add 

electronic payment details when printing checks. 

4. 
When payment files are uploaded directly to a bank’s SFTP site (on page 161), they are 

automatically confirmed in RealPage Accounting. However, you can disable this feature by 

selecting the Disable auto-confirmation of ACH files check box. If you select this option, 

then you will need to manually confirm with your bank that the payment file was uploaded 

successfully before confirming the payment in RealPage Accounting. 

This setting applies to ACH, EFT, and BACS files. 

Standard Dimension Display Section 

Select the standard dimensions that you want to use in this application for tracking and reporting. 

The system displays the dimensions across your application screens where you can select 

dimension values to apply to specific transactions. 

---

User-defined dimensions (dimensions you create for your unique business needs) do not appear 
in this list because the system automatically propagates them across your applications at the 
time of creation. 

Third Party Payments Section 

Use this section to configure a third-party payment method for vendor payments. If this section 

does not display, click the Request information button to have a sales representative contact you 

about this additional feature. 

To configure third party payments: 

• 
Select the Enable third party payments check box to display the third-party payment 

configuration options.  

Configuring the RealPage Payments Service 

1. 
Select the RealPage payments check box if you want to use the RealPage Payments 

third-party payment service. 

2. 
Click the Select button under Notify user when invoice is put on hold to send an email 

notification to users when an invoice is put on hold. 

The system opens an Available items selection box. For more information, see Using the 

Multi-Select Box. 

3. 
In the RealPage Payments credentials subsection, type your Username and Password for the 

RealPage Payments third-party payment service. By providing the credentials, you are 

authorizing your company to send payment details to the service. 

4. 
In the Payment processing subsection, select the time interval to send the payment to the 

third-party service provider. 

• 
Immediately: Select this option to immediately process the payment requests and 

complete the payment. 

• 
Process end of each day: Select this option to include the payment requests when the 

system processes all requests at the end of each day. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to manually process the payment requests through the 

Third party payments queue.

1. 
Select the Enable Paymode-X check box. 

2. 
Enter the required account and file transfer protocol (FTP) information for the system to 

transmit payment request files via FTP to the Paymode-X third-party payment service.

Configuring RealPage Virtual Refunds 

You can enable Virtual Refunds so that residents can be paid via a card instead of a check. When 

Virtual Refunds are enabled, a new vendor type called Resident Refund becomes available. This 

vendor type is automatically assigned to any TEMP vendors that are imported from OneSite. 

1. 
Select the Enable RealPage Virtual Refunds check box. 

2. 
In the Payment processing subsection, select the time interval to send the payment to the 

third-party service provider. 

• 
Immediately: Select this option to immediately process the payment requests and 

complete the payment. 

• 
Process end of each day: Select this option to include the payment requests when the 

system processes all requests at the end of each day. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to manually process the payment requests through the 

Third party payments queue. 

Configuring Debit Cards for Petty Cash 

The Debit cards for petty cash feature allows you to track and replace your cash on hand at the 

property or staff with a Prepaid MasterCard. You can issue cards to a property or to individual 

users with a set limit. As they make purchases, purchase information is loaded into RealPage 

Accounting to submit as an expense. You can view and submit expenses in core Accounting, 

Spend Management Site View for properties, or the RealPage Accounting Mobile App. 

To configure petty cash (PC) cards: 

1. 
Select the Enable debit cards for petty cash check box. 

2. 
In the Payment processing subsection, select the time interval to send the payment to the 

third-party service provider. 

• 
Immediately: Select this option to immediately process the payment requests and 

complete the payment. 

• 
Process end of each day: Select this option to include the payment requests when the 

system processes all requests at the end of each day. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to manually process the payment requests through the 

Third party payments queue. 

3. 
In the Unrestricted users for submitting the expenses multi-select box, add one or more 

unrestricted users or user roles. Unrestricted users can submit expenses for cards even if 

they are not issued to them. These are typically administrators. 

4. 
In the Reimbursement categories section, define the expense categories that will be available 

when users are submitting their debit card transactions. The system predefines a number of 

expense categories, but you can add, edit, or remove categories based on your business 

needs. 

---

Expense category: Type the name of the expense category or rename an existing 

category. 

•

• 
Attachment required: Select this check box to require users to include an attachment 

when submitting the expense category. 

If you have configured expense reports in Accounts Payable, then these are the same 
categories that are set up for expenses. 

Available Cash Section 

Use this section to define the journal and G/L account for recording cash transfers. These settings 

also determine whether Cash, A/R, and A/P accounts are summarized.  

Automatically Setting Up Available Cash Locations 

Select the Automatically set up for new locations check box to automatically create a new record 

in the Available cash locations list when a new location is added in RealPage Accounting. 

Defining Where to Transfer the Available Cash 

Use the Transfer requirements section to transfer a location’s total holdback amount into a 

separate account after it’s calculated and record a journal entry for the transfer. 

1. 
In the Journal for transfers drop-down list, select the G/L journal in which to record the 

transfer. 

2. 
In the Transfer to account drop-down list, select the cash account to which you want to 

transfer the holdback amount.  

Creating Fields for Entering Available Cash Information by Location 

Use the Name captions section to create custom fields for entering available cash information on 

the Available cash location page.

could create a field named “Property Manager” or “Investor”. 

Summarizing Account Groups in the Available Cash Report

the Available cash location page. If you do not enable these options, then each account in the 

account group displays on an individual line.

Configuring Escheatment 

Use this section to define an Aged payable account to credit when a G/L journal entry is created 

for a payment marked as “Aged Payable”. When this occurs, the original payment is voided, and 

the funds are transferred into this account. The unclaimed funds are held in this account for a 

period of time before being transferred to the state. This process is known as escheatment; see 

the Escheatment Workbench (on page 14) for more information. 

Fields 

Configure Cash Management Page 

Accounting Section 

Transaction 

summary posting

reporting.

Monthly: Select this option to create a single summary at the end of

Journal for other 

cash receipts 

Select the journal where you want to post customer payments.  

For dual-method reporting companies, this drop-down menu displays

There are two primary ways to receive customer payments. One is via A/R, in 

which payments are tracked to customers and invoices. You select the

customers and invoices. You select the journal for those payments here.

to G/L accounts. G/L accounts without account labels cannot be accessed.

which can be helpful for users. You can create account labels in A/P and A/R 

and use them on Cash Management pages as follows: 

• 
Charge card transactions (A/P) 

• 
Credit card charges and other fees - finance charge/other fees (A/P) 

•

• 
Other receipts (A/R) 

•

The Credit card accounts list displays the credit card accounts in your system. From this list, you 

can add, edit, or delete accounts and even start the process of reconciling an account or 

generating reconciliation reports. 

Credit Card Accounts in Multi-Entity Shared Companies  

Credit card accounts can either be common to all entities, or exclusive to a specific entity. 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you can create credit card 

accounts at both the root and entity levels. To view credit card accounts at the top level, select the 

Include private check box at the top of the Credit card accounts list. Enter all credit card 

transactions at the entity level. When you create a credit card, a location is required. 

Consequently, in credit card transactions, the system knows to use the base currency for the entity 

associated with that location. Credit card transactions do not support foreign currency. 

If you do not see the Include private check box on your page, verify that you are not using a 
custom view.

When you edit an existing account, the ID, Last 4 digits of card number, Type, and Payment 

method fields are read-only. In addition, reconciliation information is displayed, which includes 
two read-only fields (Last reconciled balance and Last reconciled date) and a Reconcile link. The 
link opens the Credit card reconciliation page. 

To add a credit card account: 

Fill In the Credit Card Details Section 

1. 
In the ID field, enter a unique identifier to distinguish the card’s purpose.  

2. 
In the Description field, enter a short description to identify the card account. 

You can differentiate credit cards versus debit cards in both the ID and Description fields 
by using abbreviations such as CC and DB. 

3. 
In the Type drop-down list, select the applicable credit card type: 

• 
Visa 

• 
Mastercard 

• 
Discover 

• 
American Express 

• 
Diners Club 

• 
Other Charge Card

4. 
In the Last 4 digits of card number field, type the last four digits of the credit card number. 

5. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select between the following items: 

• 
Credit: Credit cards must have a vendor ID and a credit card offset account. 

• 
Debit: Debit cards used to pay A/P invoices must have an associated checking account 

and vendor ID. 

6. 
In the Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip code/Post code, and Country fields, enter the 

relevant address information. 

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select one of the following options: 

• 
Active: This is the default status. 

• 
Inactive: Select this option if you are no longer using the card and do not want it to 

appear on the list. You can always see inactive cards by selecting the Include Inactive 

check box in the Credit card accounts list. 

8. 
In the Month and Year drop-down lists, select the month and year when the credit card 

expires. 

Fill In the Accounting Section 

1. 
In the Credit-card offset account drop-down list, select an account that is different from the 

default offset account for Accounts Payable. This field appears only if you select Credit as 

the payment method. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 

find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

2. 
In the Debit-card checking account drop-down list, select a checking account to associate 

with the debit card. It must be the same account for which the card was issued. This field 

only appears if you select “Debit” as the payment method. 

3. 
In the Default G/L journal (accrual & cash basis) drop-down list, select the journal into 

which you want to place a charge card transaction performed in Cash Management. The 

default journal is the same one used for A/P payments. For credit cards, all transactions 

(charges on the card and payoffs for the card) use the same journal. For debit cards, banks 

have different journals. This field appears if you did not enable dual method reporting. 

4. 
In the Default G/L journal (accrual basis) drop-down list, select an accrual journal. This field 

appears if you enabled dual method reporting and only applies to credit cards. 

5. 
In the Default G/L journal (cash basis) drop-down list, select a cash journal. This field 

appears if you enabled dual method reporting and only applies to credit cards.

In the Finance charges account drop-down list, select an account to be used for credit card 

reconciliation. This field does not apply to debit cards.

Bank Accounts in Multi-Entity Shared Companies  

Bank accounts can either be common to all entities, or exclusive to a specific entity. 

In shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies, you can create bank accounts at 

both the root and entity levels. Create the bank account at the top level if you want to use it for 

inter-entity transactions. Always reconcile a bank account at the same level in which you created 

it. In addition, assign it a unique General Ledger account and a location. When you are at the top 

level, select the Include private check box to view entity-level banks. When you are at the entity 

level, both entity-level banks and top-level banks are available. 

If you do not see the Include private check box on your page, verify that you are not using a 
custom view.

user’s permissions. 

Adding a Bank Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > 
 Bank Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > 
 Bank Accounts`


Adding a bank account includes entering details about the account, such as your bank name, the 

journals and other accounts you want to map to, and how you want to print checks and pay your 

vendors. 

Entering the Bank Account Details 

In the Financial institution section, fill in the required information. 

1. 
In the Account type field, select whether you want to create a checking or savings account. 

2. 
In the Account ID field, type a unique number to identify the checking account. 

3. 
In the Account number field, type the 10-digit number found at the bottom of the check. 

4. 
In the Bank name field, type the bank name. If you have more than one account at this 

bank, include a description in the name. 

5. 
In the Name on the account field, type the official name that the bank has on file for the 

checking account. 

6. 
In the Routing number field, type the 9-digit number printed at the bottom of the check if 

you are printing on blank check stock. Otherwise, leave this field blank. 

7. 
In the Branch ID field, type the number found at the top of the check, above the date field. 

8. 
In the Address 1, Address 2, City/Town, State/Territory, Zip code/Post code, and Country 

fields, type your bank’s address. 

---


<!-- Page 542 -->
Accounts 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

9. 
In the Phone number field, type the phone number of your bank branch. 

10. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether the account is Active or Inactive. 

11. 
In the Currency field, select a default currency for the bank account. 

This field appears only in multi-currency companies. 

In the Accounting information section, fill in the required information. 

1. 
In the Default bank G/L account drop-down list, select an account from the General Ledger. 

How you assign G/L accounts determines where and how an account can be used. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 
find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

2. 
In the Bank G/L account field, click the Select link to choose alternate G/L accounts. You can 

select an unlimited number of alternate G/L accounts. Activity from these accounts appears 

in the bank reconciliation and is included in the bank balance. 

3. 
In the Default payables G/L journal drop-down list, select a journal to record payments and 

transfers out of the account. The default is the same journal used for Accounts Payable 

payments. 

4. 
In the Default receivables G/L journal drop-down list, select a journal to record deposits 

and transfers into the account. The default is the same journal used for Accounts Payable 

payments. 

5. 
In the Service charge G/L account drop-down list, select an account to post service charges 

and other fees to during reconciliation. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 
find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

6. 
In the Interest earned G/L account drop-down list, select an account to post interest to 

during reconciliation. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 
find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

7. 
In the Department ID drop-down list, select the default department for G/L posting. If your 

company does not use departments, then this field is not displayed. 

8. 
In the Location ID drop-down list, select the default location for G/L posting. Depending on 

your company, the location ID may be required to force the system to balance the 

associated journal entries. 

9. 
Select the Disable inter-entity transfers check box to exclude the account from inter-entity 

transfers, even if you have globally enabled inter-entity transfers for the entire structure. 

---


<!-- Page 543 -->
Chapter 6: Accounts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

10. 
In the bottom section, select whether to enable the bank account for specific third-party 

payment services enabled on the Configure Cash Management page. 

• 
Enable for RealPage Payments or third party payments: Select this check box to allow 

the bank account to be used for RealPage Payments or third-party payments. This 

option is available for both checking and saving accounts. 

If you enable the bank account for third-party payments, then the system displays 
the bank account in the payment options when you pay A/P invoices. 

• 
Enable for RealPage Debit Card, Virtual Refund or PC Reimbursement payments: 

Select this check box to allow the bank account to be used for RealPage Debit Card 

payments, RealPage Virtual Refunds, or petty cash (PC) reimbursements. This is 

required in order to process payments and reimbursements. 

• 
Select which Bank account type should be refunded for these types of payments 

and reimbursements. 

• 
Select the Override MID and LID check boxes if you want to use a bank account 

other than the property’s operating bank account for RealPage Debit Card 

payments, PC reimbursements, or RealPage Virtual Refunds. An implementation 

consultant will help set this up. If you choose to override MID and LID for 

RealPage Debit Card payments, then the system will not run a validation check 

with ResidentDirect. 

When RealPage Debit Card payments or PC reimbursement payments are enabled for 
a bank account, RealPage Accounting automatically validates whether the location 
associated with the bank account is set up in ResidentDirect, a bill payment service 
offered by RealPage Payments Services (RPPS). If the location is not in 
ResidentDirect, then you will receive an error message when you try to save. If this 
occurs, contact your account representative for more information.  

Setting Your Check Printing Preferences 

On the Check printing tab: 

1. 
Select a Print on option to determine how you want to print checks. 

• 
Pre-printed check stock: This option requires you to order check stock in advance, 

using separate check stock for each checking account, and printing from one checking 

account at a time. Print checks in U. S. and Canadian dollars only. 

• 
Blank check stock: This option requires MICR ink and a printer that supports the ink, 

and coordinating alignment of check details with your bank. Print checks in U. S., 

Canadian, or Mexican currency. 

• 
Disable check printing from this account: Select this option to disable check printing. 

2. 
Select the Print company address check box to print a company address on your checks. 

---


<!-- Page 544 -->
Accounts 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

For multi-entity shared companies, the system uses the address of the entity contact 
selected on the Entity information page if there is no address found. 

3. 
In the Company address field, select whether you want to use the address entered on the 

Company information page or enter a different address. 

• 
Select the Print logo check box to include your logo on the check. 

• 
Click the Upload logo button. The system opens the Uploading company logo for 

print checks box. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the logo file from your local drive. 

Logos must be 50 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall. 

5. 
Click the Upload button. 

6. 
Select the Use 2-signature checks check box to require two signatures when the check 

reaches a certain amount. 

• 
In the Amount requiring 2nd signature field, type a minimum amount to require a 

second signature. Type 0 to require two signatures regardless of the amount. 

7. 
In the Next check # field, type a starting number. For each succeeding check that you print, 

the number increments by one. 

8. 
In the Printing format drop-down list, select a format option depending on your preference 

in the Print on option. 

• 
Standard: Select this option if you want the checks to show your bank account 

number, bank routing number, and check numbers. 

• 
High security: Select this option to include the same information in the Standard 

option with additional features that reduce fraud related to check washing, forgery, 

and copying. This option appears if you chose to print on pre-printed checks. 

• 
Business: Select this option if you want to print the amounts in a font that makes 

alterations difficult. This option appears if you chose to print on blank check stock. 

• 
Canadian or Mexican: These options appear if you are set up for foreign currency. 

9. 
In the Designed custom layout drop-down list, select a custom layout if one has been 

designated for the company. 

10. 
In the Paper format drop-down list, select whether you want to print the check on the top, 

middle, or bottom panel. 

11. 
Select the Print line-item detail on check stubs check box if you want to add fields to the 

non-remittance panel of the check. These fields include columns for the account, 

department, and location of each line item. You can generate up to 18 line items per page 

in either summary or detail mode.

12. 
Select the Always include vendor stub details check box to add vendor stub information 

when printing checks.

shading over the check amount on blank check stock. The check amount will print with 

asterisks instead (for example, **101.00**). 

This setting applies when you print checks from the Print checks page or the Print payment 

copies page. It does not apply to custom check layouts. 

14. 
In the Print these location details on the check stub field, select one of the following: 

• 
ID: This option displays only the location ID in the location column. 

• 
Name: This option displays only the location name in the location column. 

• 
Both: This option displays both the location ID and name. 

15. 
In the Additional text field, type the text that you want to appear under the signature line of 

the check. For example, “Void after 60 days.” 

16. 
In the MICR (Magnetic ink character recognition) section, change the following settings only 

if your bank requires a special alignment of the account number on your check. You do not 

need to change the default values unless your bank requests you do so. 

• 
In Account number alignment, select the required alignment of the account number 

on your check. 

Normally, the account number is right-aligned. 

Select the Left alignment button to align the account number to the left. 

• 
In Account number positioning, enter the number of spaces required to position the 

account number on your check if you still need additional adjustment. You can enter 

up to a total of five spaces. 

• 
In Check number length, enter the number of zeros required to pad the check 

number. For example, if your checks are currently 6 digits, and your current check

number is 218 but you want the check number to be 7 digits, type “7” in this field.

• 
In Regional settings – United States, select the ON-US symbol check box if your bank

Setting Up ACH Payments 

This tab is replaced with the Electronic payments setup tab if you enable foreign electronic 
payments on the Configure cash management page. See the next section for instructions. 

1.

account. 

3. 
In the Company name field, type the name that you want to appear on the recipient’s bank 

statement. This field is pre-filled with the company name in your ACH bank record.

more than one checking account with the bank, you may be requested to enter a different 

ID for each account. 

5.

number. This field is pre-filled with the information from your ACH bank record. 

6.

In the Company discretionary data field, enter up to 20 characters of additional 

information, such as codes that describe any special handling of entries in this summary 

payment.

Restricting Bank Accounts 

The ability to restrict bank accounts by entity is a configuration option that your system 
administrator can turn on in a multi-entity shared environment. See Entity Restrictions for 
more information. 

If you create a bank account at the entity level, then it is already restricted to that entity, and 
the Restrictions tab does not appear. Similarly, if you create a bank account at the entity level of 
a parent entity, it is not accessible to the parent entity ’s child entities/locations. If you want to 
apply location restrictions and allow child locations to access a bank account, you must create 
the bank account at the top level. 

1. 
Select a restriction option: 

• 
Unrestricted: This option makes the account available to the top-level company and 

all entity-level locations. This is the default. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: This option makes the account inaccessible to entity-level 

locations. 

• 
Restricted: This option makes the account accessible to locations or location groups 

that you specify. 

2. 
If you select the Restricted option, click the Select button, and then use the multi-select box 

to choose one or more locations or location groups that can access the bank account. For 

instructions using the selection box, see Using the multi-select box. 

To save this account and create another, click the More actions drop-down menu, and then select 

Save & new. 

To save this account and go back to the Checking accounts list, click the Save button.

Restricting a Bank Account to One or More Entities/Locations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Bank Accounts > Edit > 
Restrictions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts > Edit >

In a shared multi-entity company, you can restrict an account to specific entities or locations to 

prevent entities from paying bills out of the wrong bank account. The ability to restrict bank 

accounts by entity is a configuration option that your system administrator can turn on in a 

multi-entity shared environment. See Entity Restrictions for more information. 

If you create a bank account at the entity level, then it is already restricted to that entity, and 
the Restrictions tab does not appear. Similarly, if you create a bank account at the entity level of 
a parent entity, it is not accessible to the parent entity ’s child entities/locations. If you want to 
apply location restrictions and allow child locations to access a bank account, you must create 
the bank account at the top level. 

Applying Entity Restrictions to a Bank Account 

To restrict a bank account: 

1. 
In the Bank accounts list, click the Edit link next to the account name.  

The Bank account information page opens. 

2. 
Click the Restrictions tab. 

3. 
Select a restriction option: 

• 
Unrestricted: This option makes the account available to the top-level company and 

all entity-level locations. This is the default. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: This option makes the account inaccessible to entity-level 

locations. 

• 
Restricted: This option makes the account accessible to locations or location groups 

that you specify. 

4. 
If you select the Restricted option, click the Select button, and then use the multi-select box 

to choose one or more locations or location groups that can access the bank account. For 

instructions using the selection box, see Using the multi-select box.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

You can’t remove a location restriction if the location is set as the owner location for the 
account, or if this bank account is configured as the default bank account. 

How Restricting by a Location Affects Inter-Entity Transactions 

When you restrict a bank account to a location or location group, only that location or group has 

access to that account. If another location is paying the A/P invoices for the first location, the 

location can’t use the account to pay A/P invoices, because it doesn’t own that account. If the 

locations are in different entities, the system can create an IET due-to/due-from transaction. 

For example, suppose a location for Texas receives an A/P invoice but a Corporate location pays it 

from an account owned by Corporate. In this case, an inter-entity transaction (due-to/due-from) 

will be created between the two locations or entities. You can see the IET in the following General 

Ledger report. 

In a case where a bank account is restricted by location and another location within the same 

entity pays the A/P invoice, no IET is generated because both locations are children of the entity.
