#### Intelligent Bank Matching for Bank Reconciliations
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 566*



##### Default Rules for Checks and Deposits
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 566*

Reconciliation Rules 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Intelligent Bank Matching for Bank Reconciliations 

Intelligent bank matching allows you to expand the criteria for auto-matching transactions in 

RealPage Accounting to bank transactions from bank feeds, BAI files, or CSV files. You can set up 

multiple reconciliation rules to match bank transactions on a one-to-many or many-to-many basis 

as they are imported into RealPage Accounting. 

If auto-matching is not able to match all of your transactions, then you can manually match (on 
page 280 ) the remaining unmatched transactions. 

To use intelligent bank matching, you’ll need to set up rules (on page 567) and then pair them 

with rule sets (on page 559): 

• 
Rules determine the logic that the system will use to match bank transactions to 

transactions in RealPage Accounting.  

• 
Rule sets apply a set of rules to one or more bank accounts. The system will apply the rules 

in the order you configure them. 

Default rules (on page 554 ) are set up for checks and deposits; however, you can create 
additional rules to suit your business needs. 

Default Rules for Checks and Deposits 

RealPage Accounting provides default rules for matching checks and deposits during bank 

reconciliations. They appear in the Rule list as ::SYS::CHECKS and ::SYS::DEPOSITS. You can 

include them in your rule sets, but you can’t change or edit them. 

If you’ve created a rule set for a bank account, then the default rules do not apply.  

System Default for Checks 

The default rule for checks searches for RealPage and bank transactions with the Checks/Debits 

transaction type and then matches transactions that have the same Document number (check 

number) and Amount. 

---


<!-- Page 567 -->
Chapter 7: Reconciliation Rules 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

System Defaults for Deposits  

The default rule for deposits searches for RealPage and bank transactions with the 

Deposits/Credits transaction type and then matches transactions that have the same Posting 

date (G/L posting date) and Amount. 

There are three additional default rules for auto-matching deposits that are one, two, or three 

days apart. 

---



##### Example of a One-to-Many Rule
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 568*

Reconciliation Rules 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Example of a One-to-Many Rule 

You have a CSV file that contains three deposits with the same check number. However, only one 

transaction was entered into RealPage Accounting for the entire deposit. With intelligent bank 

matching, you can set up a rule so that the system groups bank transactions by document 

number when matching transactions for reconciliation. 

Below is an example of a rule created to match RealPage and bank transactions that meet the 

following criteria: 

• 
Check transaction type 

• 
Same Amount and Document number 

• 
Posting date within ±3 days of the current date 

By selecting to group Bank transactions by Document number, the system will be able to match 

one RealPage transaction to multiple bank transactions, also called a “one-to-many” relationship. 

---


<!-- Page 569 -->
Chapter 7: Reconciliation Rules 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

In this example, the system matches the three imported transactions to a RealPage transaction 

with the same Document number and a Bank amount of $1,850.00, the sum total of the three 

deposits. 

---


<!-- Page 570 -->
Reconciliation Rules 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

If you click the Match link next to the RealPage transaction, you can see that the system has 

matched all three bank transactions to it.

Rule Set List

Use the Rule set list to assign a set of reconciliation rules to one or more bank accounts. From 

this list, you can add, view, edit, delete, and export rule sets. You can also click the Flip view 

button to display a list of bank accounts that are associated with your rule sets. 

Rule Set View 

The default view displays a list of rule sets you’ve created for your company, including the number 

of rules and accounts linked to the rule set. 

Rule Set Bank Accounts View 

The flip view displays a list of all bank accounts linked to your rule set(s). You can assign multiple 

bank accounts to a rule set, but you can’t assign the same bank account to more than one rule 

set.

##### Deleting or Inactivating a Rule Set
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 574*

Reconciliation Rules 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Deleting or Inactivating a Rule Set 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > Rule Sets > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > Rule Sets > Edit`


You can delete or inactivate a reconciliation rule set depending on whether you want to retain the 

settings you defined. 

Deleting a Rule 

If you no longer use a reconciliation rule set, then you can delete the set permanently. After you 

delete it, it can’t be restored. If you’re unsure whether you want to delete it, you can set its status 

to Inactive instead. 

To delete a rule set permanently: 

1. 
In the Rule set list, click the Delete link next to the rule set you want to delete. 

A confirmation box opens. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Inactivating a Rule 

Inactivating a reconciliation rule set retains the settings you’ve defined but removes the rule set 

from the Rule set list and prevents it from triggering when the system is auto-matching bank 

transactions for reconciliation. 

To inactivate a rule set: 

1. 
In the Rule set list, click the Edit link next to the rule set you want to inactivate. 

The Rule set information page opens. 

2. 
In the Details section, set the Status field to “Inactive”. 

3. 
Click Save. 

The system hides the rule set from the Rule set list and removes it from any system 

drop-down lists.

Rule List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Reconciliation Rules > Rules`


Use the Rule list to create intelligent bank matching rules for reconciling bank accounts. Rules 

determine the logic that the system will use when matching transactions in RealPage Accounting 

to bank transactions imported via bank feeds, BAI files, or CSV files. When you create a rule, you 

can: 

• 
Set filter criteria to target specific RealPage or bank transactions. 

• 
Group transactions by document number or G/L posting date to match one RealPage 

transaction to multiple bank transactions (one-to-many) or multiple RealPage transactions 

to multiple bank transactions (many-to-many). 

• 
Define the conditions that must be met for the system to match the transactions. 

Default rules (on page 554 ) are set up for checks and deposits; however, you can create 
additional rules to suit your business needs. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and manage bank matching rules: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Cash Management 
Rules 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

via bank feeds, BAI files, or CSV files; they appear in the Bank section on the Reconcile 

bank account page.

Amount 

•

•

 icon to add additional filter rows as needed.

In most cases, you will need to add the filter criteria twice; one for RealPage transactions 
and one for bank transactions. 

Grouping Transactions 

In the Group transactions by section, select whether you want to group RealPage transactions and 

bank transactions by Document number or Posting date to match them on a one-to-many or 

many-to-many basis. For example, if you have multiple transactions with the same document 

number in your import file but only one transaction was entered into the system, then grouping 

the transactions by document number would allow you to match multiple bank transactions to 

one RealPage transaction. 

Defining Matching Conditions 

In the Matching conditions section, define the condition(s) that must be met for the system to 

match the transactions: 

1. 
In the Bank transaction field drop-down list, select the field on which you want to base the 

condition: 

• 
Document number 

• 
Posting date 

• 
Description 

• 
Amount 

• 
Document number (leading zeros removed) 

The Match with this field in a RealPage transaction column automatically populates with 

the same selection. 

2. 
In the Operator drop-down list, select an expression for the matching condition: 

• 
Equals 

• 
Contains 

• 
Within 

3. 
In the Value field, type a field value to complete the expression. 

This field is not available if you set the Operator to “Equals”. 

Saving the Rule 

When you are finished setting up the rule, click Save to add it to the Rule list. 

What’s Next? 

Add the rule to a rule set (on page 560) to apply it to one or more bank accounts.

#### ACH Frequently Asked Questions
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 591*

Chapter 8: More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

ACH Frequently Asked Questions 

Can I pay my independent contractors via ACH? 

Yes. If the vendor has a non-business bank account, be sure to choose PPD as the Standard entry 

class code for ACH payments in their vendor record. The PPD option formats the ACH payments 

correctly for a consumer account. 

What determines the payment date for posted payments? 

The estimated payment date that you enter on the Pay A/P invoices or Reimburse expenses page 

as the payment date. The actual payment date depends on when the bank receives and processes 

the payment. 

Can I void an ACH payment that I already sent to the bank? 

Yes, but you also need to contact your bank to cancel the payment. Voiding a payment in the 

system doesn’t affect the bank’s payment process. If you don’t contact your bank, it will proceed 

to issue the payment regardless of whether you void the payment here. 

Learn how to void a confirmed electronic payment (on page 165) and how to void a pending 

electronic payment (on page 164). 

Can I use ACH payments in a multi-currency, multi-entity environment? 

Any company can process electronic payments. However, you can issue these electronic payments 

only when transactions are in US dollars and are drawn on US banks.

##### Adding an ACH Bank Configuration
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 592*

More 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an ACH Bank Configuration 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > 
 ACH Bank Configurations`


Adding an ACH bank allows you to issue standard ACH payments from any checking account 

linked to this bank. 

Before performing any of the following procedures, contact your bank and get their ACH payment 
specifications. 

Filling in the File Header Information Section 

To add file header information for an ACH bank configuration: 

1. 
In the Bank ID field, type a unique ID for your bank. This ID can be any name that helps you 

identify the bank. Enter up to 20 characters. 

2. 
In the Immediate destination name field, type the name of your bank, as specified by the 

bank. Enter up to 23 characters. 

3. 
In the Immediate destination ID field, type the bank’s routing number. Enter up to 9 

characters. 

4. 
In the Immediate origin name field, type the name of the origin bank. Enter up to 23 

characters. 

5. 
In the Immediate origin ID field, type the origin bank’s routing number. Enter up to 10 

characters. 

6. 
In the Reference code field, check with your bank whether this should be filled in or left 

blank. Enter up to 8 characters. 

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether this account is active or inactive. 

8. 
Select the Include EOF marker check box if your bank expects a carriage return at the end 

of the ACH payment file. 

Filling in the Bank SFTP Details Section 

1. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the SFTP storage site for the bank. 

To configure SFTP details, open the Company application, and then select the menu’s 

Setup tab. In the Storage section, click the Cloud Storage option. See Adding a cloud 
storage target . 

2. 
In the Path field, enter the SFTP path where you want to upload the payment file. If you 

leave this field blank, the system uploads the file to the root folder in the selected SFTP site. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

After generating the payment file, the system displays a check box next to the file in the 

Payment file list, which you can use to upload the file to the bank’s SFTP site (on page 161). 

---

##### Adding a Bank Feed Configuration

Adding a Bank Feed Configuration 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Bank Feed Configurations > Add`


To add a bank feed configuration: 

1. 
In the Financial institution field, type the name of the financial institution to which you are 

connecting your bank feed. 

2. 
Click the Connect button. 

A terms and conditions box opens. 

3. 
Click the Continue button. 

The system displays the available banks. 

4. 
Use the Search bar to locate your bank, and then select the bank’s icon. 

The system displays a login box for the selected bank. 

5. 
Enter your bank credentials, and then click the Submit button. 

The system displays a list of your available accounts. 

6. 
Select the accounts you want to connect, and then click the Continue button. 

The system displays the linked bank accounts in the Mapped bank accounts section. 

7. 
In the Mapped bank accounts section, use the Bank account (RealPage) drop-down list to 

select the bank account in RealPage Accounting you want to map to each linked account. 

8. 
Define the bank feed import schedule. 

• 
Schedule: Select this option to automatically fetch the bank feeds from a specific date 

up to the present, based on the selected frequency. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to run the bank feed manually by financial institution. You 

can run the bank feed using the Run link on the Bank feed configurations list. 

9. 
If you select the Schedule option: 

• 
Enter the Start date, from which you want to fetch bank feeds. 

• 
Use the Repeat drop-down list and Every field to define the frequency with which you 

want to fetch bank feeds. 

You can turn off the schedule by clicking the corresponding Turn off link on the Bank feed 

configurations list. This will automatically switch the bank feed configurations to run 
manually. 

10. 
If you select the Manual option, enter the Start date.

##### Updating Bank Feed Connections

Updating Bank Feed Connections 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > Bank Feed Configurations > Edit`


You can edit a bank feed configuration to update your bank feed connections by fetching bank 

accounts and mapping them to accounts in RealPage Accounting. 

1. 
In the Bank feed configurations list, click the Edit link next to the bank feed for which you 

are fetching bank accounts. 

The Bank feed configuration page opens. 

2. 
Click one of the following buttons: 

• 
Fetch bank accounts: Click this button to retrieve only the accounts that were linked 

during the bank feed’s initial setup. For example, if you originally linked 20 bank 

accounts, it will retrieve all 20 of those accounts, even if you only mapped a few of 

them initially. 

• 
Fetch new bank accounts: Click this button to retrieve existing accounts and new 

accounts that were added since the bank feed’s initial setup.  

3. 
Enter your bank credentials, and then click the Submit button. 

The system displays a list of your available accounts. 

4. 
Select the accounts you want to connect, and then click the Continue button. 

The system displays the linked bank accounts in the Mapped bank accounts section. 

5.

##### Notifying Users When Bank Feeds Fail
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 609*

Chapter 8: More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Notifying Users When Bank Feeds Fail 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Edit > Roles Information`


In some cases, a bank feed may fail to import transactions from one or more bank accounts. This 

typically occurs when the Plaid service fails to connect due to a change in credentials. You can 

assign the Bank Feed Failure Notifications role to one or more users to send them an email 

notification whenever a bank feed fails. This is a standard, pre-defined role in RealPage 

Accounting. The email serves as a reminder to re-enter credentials for their bank in Plaid.  

To set up a user with this role: 

1. 
In the Company application menu, select the Setup tab, and then click the Users option. 

The Users list opens. 

2. 
Click the Edit link next to the user. 

The User information page opens. 

3. 
Select the Roles information tab. 

4. 
If needed, click the 
 Add button to add a new row. 

5. 
In the Role name drop-down list, select the Bank Feed Failure Notification role. 

6. 
Click the Save button to save the user record. 

When a bank feed fails, the system automatically sends an email notification to all users set 

up with this role. The system sends only one email notification per financial institution even 

if the bank feed fails for more than one bank account in the same financial institution. The 

email serves as a reminder for them to re-enter the credentials for their bank in Plaid. You 

can do this by editing the bank feed configuration and clicking the Fetch bank accounts 

button.

#### Positive Pay Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 615*

Chapter 8: More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Positive Pay Overview 

What Is Positive Pay? 

Positive Pay is an automated fraud detection service that protects companies against financial 

losses and other liabilities due to fraudulent bank activity. It is offered and monitored by the Cash 

Management department of most banks. Positive Pay ensures that checks are not honored unless 

the bank can match them to the correct identifying information. With this service, a company’s 

funds are better secured against fraudsters and identity thieves who can create counterfeit checks. 

There is generally a fee associated with the service, although some banks now offer it for free. 

How Does Positive Pay Work? 

Positive Pay requires companies to transmit a daily file to the bank containing a list of checks they 

issued and payments they voided that day. When those checks are presented to the bank for 

payment, the bank compares them electronically against the file of transmitted checks. The file 

contains the account number, check number, and dollar amount of each check. If any of these 

numbers do not match, then the bank does not accept the payment. The payee name may also be 

included in the file; however, it is not part of the matching service. 

Each bank has unique format requirements when it comes to transmitting files, so be sure to 
select the appropriate layout specifications when you configure Positive Pay (on page 603 ) in 
RealPage Accounting. 

When a check is presented that does not have a “match” in the file, the bank flags it as an 

“exception item” and notifies a business representative from the company; for example, by 

sending a fax or image of the exception item. The representative reviews the item and instructs 

the bank to clear or return the check. 

Files that upload successfully have a state of Uploaded. When a positive pay file fails to upload to 

the bank, the State field changes to Upload Fail and a Retry link becomes available. If the upload 

fails a second time, a message shows why the file failed to upload. 

---



##### Adding a Positive Pay Configuration
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 616*

More 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding a Positive Pay Configuration 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > 
 Positive Pay Configuration`


To generate Positive Pay files, you must first configure the file details, layout specifications, 

schedule options, and bank accounts. 

Entering Configuration Details 

In the Details section, define the bank and file details: 

1. 
Type a Configuration name and Description. 

2. 
Optionally, select an entity from the Primary entity drop-down list if you want to restrict the 

Positive Pay configuration and files to a specific entity. Users must have access to that entity 

to view the configuration and generate files. 

3. 
In the Layout drop-down list, select a predefined bank layout. The layout defines the bank 

specifications for Positive Pay files; click the Layout specs link to view the specifications 

document for the selected financial institution. 

• 
You can override certain aspects of the layout specifications and rearrange columns 

for CSV-formatted Positive Pay files. See Overriding Bank Layout Specifications for 

Positive Pay CSV Files (on page 605) for more information. 

• 
If you do not see the bank specifications that you need, submit a Support ticket so it 

can be added to the list. You will need to provide a copy of the bank’s layout 

specifications with your ticket. 

4. 
Type the Bank number, Bank ID, and Bank text, if specified by the bank. 

5. 
Type a File name for the Positive Pay file. 

You can also include date and time stamps in the file name. The system automatically 
replaces {TIMESTAMP} with Date.Time or replaces {YYYYMMDD} and {MMDDYY} 
with their equivalent date formats.  

If you don’t specify a file name, then the name will default to the Configuration name with 

the date and time stamp. 

6. 
To upload the Positive Pay files directly to the bank, select a cloud-storage target from the 

FTP drop-down list, and then type the FTP path. 

7. 
In the Effective date field, type or select the earliest date to include in the first Positive Pay 

file. This is how far back the system searches for checks that have never been marked as 

sent. 

Scheduling Positive Pay Files 

In the Schedule section, set a schedule for generating the Positive Pay files: 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select a starting date for the schedule. 

---

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

2. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select when the schedule should end: 

• 
Never: Select this option to continue auto-generating files indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Select this option to specify the number of times to generate 

files. 

• 
End date: Select this option to stop generating files after a particular date. 

3. 
In the Email success results to and Email failure results to fields, type the email address to 

notify when the file successfully generates or fails to generate, respectively. 

Selecting Bank Accounts 

In the Accounts section, select the bank account(s) to which the configuration applies: 

1. 
Select the Select check box next to each bank account.  

2. 
When finished, click Save to save the configuration. 

Overriding Bank Layout Specifications for Positive Pay CSV Files 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > 
 Positive Pay Configuration`


You can override certain bank layout specifications for any Positive Pay files saved in a CSV or 

delimited format. 

1. 
While you are adding a Positive Pay configuration (on page 603), click the Override Layout 

Specifications button. 

Make sure you’ve selected a bank’s layout specifications from the Layout drop-down list 
first. 

2. 
In the Define layout overrides box, update the specifications that you want to override: 

• 
Date format: This is the date format used in the Positive Pay file, including the order of 

the month, day, and year and any separators between them. 

• 
Normal check indicator: This is a specific value in the Positive Pay file that indicates a 

check is legitimate and authorized for payment, as opposed to an exception or 

potential fraud item. Common values include “I” for “Issued” and “P” for “Payment”. 

• 
Void check indicator: This is a specific value in the Positive Pay file that marks a check 

as voided or canceled to notify the bank not to honor it. Common values include “V”, 

“VOID,” or “-1”.  

• 
End of line character: This is an invisible code that tells a program where to start a 

new line, also known as a newline character. The type of character used depends on 

the operating system where the Positive Pay file was created: 

• 
Windows (CR/LF): The standard newline character for Windows and DOS 

systems. It is a two-character sequence with a carriage return and line feed, \R\N.

Updating a Check Signature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > Check Update`


To update a check signature: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the 

Setup tab. 

2. 
In the More section, click the Check update menu option. 

The Check update page opens. 

3. 
Select the Signature update radio button in the Checking accounts section. 

4. 
Optionally, filter the list of checking accounts by entity: 

a) 
Click the Filters section to expand it. 

b) 
Select a specific entity from the Entity drop-down list or select the Show entity-level 

accounts check box to include all entity-level bank accounts. 

c) 
Select the Show inactive accounts check box if you want include checking accounts 

whose status has been set to Inactive. 

d) 
Click the Apply filters button. The list of checking accounts refreshes with the selected 

filters. 

5. 
In the Checking accounts section, select the check box next to each account that you want to 

update. To select all accounts, select the check box in the column header. 

6. 
In the Signatures section, click the Choose file button, browse to the new signature file on 

your local drive, and then click the Open button.  

A preview of the signature appears. The signature should fill the box, leaving little white 

space. If your signature does not fill the box, it will appear distorted on your printed checks.  

The signature file must be in JPG or GIF format. The file size must be 3.0 inches (width) x 
0.36 inches (height) or less. The file cannot exceed 10,000 bytes.

7. 
Click Save. 

A confirmation box opens. 

8. 
Click OK to update the signature files.

##### Adding an Owner Distribution
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 638*

More 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an Owner Distribution 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > 
 Owner Distribution`


To add an owner distribution: 

1. 
In the Property ID drop-down list, select the property for which you have previously defined 

owners and their owner percentages. 

2. 
In the Bank account drop-down list, select the bank account from which you want to make 

the distribution. 

3. 
In Bank acct balance, the system automatically displays the fund amount available in the 

selected bank account. 

4. 
In Reserve amount, the system displays the default reserve defined during the entity setup.  

5. 
In AP invoice number, enter a reference number for the owner’s A/P invoice. 

6. 
In AP invoice date, enter or select a date that you want to set as the A/P invoice date. All 

owner A/P invoices from this distribution will have this date. 

7. 
In GL posting date, enter or select the date when you want the transaction to post to the 

General Ledger. You can enable this option on the Configure Accounts Payable page.  

8. 
In Due date, enter the payment due date. 

9. 
Select the Allow available amt to be > bank balance check box if you want to make a 

distribution that is greater than the fund amount currently available in the bank account.  

10. 
In Available amount, the system displays the fund amount in the selected bank account 

minus the reserve amount. This amount is divided among the owners according to their 

percentages of ownership. 

11. 
In the Items section, the system automatically populates the owner details as line items 

when you select previously defined entities with ownership percentages in the Property ID 

field. 

• 
In Owner ID/name, the system displays all owners created for a stand-alone enterprise 

company. For multi-entity shared companies, owners are also created as vendors, but 

they are assigned to the specific entity in the Ownership information tab of the Entity 

Information page. 

• 
In the Default account drop-down list,  

• 
In Ownership %, the system displays the previous default owner percentage. However, 

you can override the default here.  

• 
In Amount to distribute, the system displays the amount of the A/P invoice created 

for this owner. The system initially proposes an amount based on the ownership 

percentage multiplied by the available amount. You can override this amount here.

#### Holdbacks

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Holdbacks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > Holdbacks`


Use the Holdbacks list to add and manage holdbacks. Holdbacks identify cash designated to pay 

future or anticipated expenses such as employee payroll. They are used to calculate or forecast a 

location or location group’s available cash. You can generate an available cash report on the 

Available cash location or Available cash location group page, respectively. 

You can base the holdback on an actual, budgeted, or manually specified amount: 

• 
Actual: The system calculates available cash based on G/L account balances. 

• 
Budget: The system calculates available cash based on the budget amounts in the default 

budget. 

• 
Manual entry: The system calculates available cash based on a manually entered holdback 

amount. 

---

user’s permissions. 

Adding a Holdback 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > 
 Holdbacks`


Holdbacks are used to calculate a location’s available cash. A holdback is an anticipated expense 

that cannot be calculated automatically. 

To add a holdback record: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
In the More section of the menu, click the 
 Add button next to Holdbacks. 

4. 
In the Holdback based on drop-down list, select one of the following: 

• 
Actual: The system uses G/L account balances when calculating the cash available 

cash. 

• 
Budget: The system uses information from the default budget when calculating the 

cash available. 

• 
Manual entry: The system uses a manually entered amount when calculating the cash 

available. 

5. 
If you are adding a holdback based on an Actual or Budget, then select the account group 

or account from the Account group/Account drop-down list.  

---


<!-- Page 649 -->
Chapter 8: More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

• 
Select the Summarize accounts check box if you want to summarize account groups 

into one line on the Available cash location page. Clear the check box if you want to 

show each account on a separate line. 

• 
Select the Include opening balance check box if you want to show the ending balance 

for balance sheet accounts on the Available cash location page, including the opening 

balance. 

6. 
Type a name for the holdback in the Name field. 

7. 
Optionally, if you are adding a holdback based on a Manual entry, you can select a category 

to assign to the holdback from the Holdback category drop-down list. You can also add a 

new category by clicking the Add link in the drop-down list, and then typing the new 

category name. 

8. 
If the holdback is based on an Actual or Budget, then use the Calculation method 

drop-down list to select the span of time for which you are calculating: 

• 
Current month  

• 
Prior month 

• 
3 month average 

• 
6 month average 

• 
9 month average 

The Current month option is used only with the Budget holdback option. 

9. 
If the holdback is based on a Manual entry, then enter the Amount. You can also leave this 

field blank and enter an amount after calculating the available cash for a location.  

10. 
If the holdback is based on an Actual or Budget, then type the percentage to hold back in 

the Partial percent field. For example, type “10” for 10%. You can also type a value greater 

than 100 to accommodate anticipated increases. 

11. 
In the Sequence field, type the order number in which you want the holdback to appear on 

the Available cash location page.

##### Viewing and Editing Holdbacks
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 651*

Chapter 8: More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Viewing and Editing Holdbacks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > Holdbacks > View/Edit`


Holdbacks are used to calculate available cash. A holdback is an anticipated expense that cannot 

be calculated automatically. 

Viewing a Holdback 

To view a holdback record: 

1. 
In the Holdbacks list, click the View link next to the holdback record. 

The Holdback page opens in View mode. While viewing the record, you can: 

• 
Print the record. 

• 
Edit the record. 

• 
Duplicate the record to create a new holdback of the same kind. 

• 
View the audit trail of the holdback record. 

2. 
Click Done to close the record. 

Editing a Holdback 

To edit a holdback record: 

1. 
In the Holdbacks list, click the Edit link next to the holdback record. 

The Holdback page opens in Edit mode. 

2. 
Edit the fields as needed, and then click Save.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

A/P batch 

A group of A/P transactions—such as invoices or 

credits—entered and posted together. 

A/P configuration 

The collection of settings that define how A/P 

functions behave, including approval rules, 

numbering formats, tolerances, and posting 

options. 

A/P workflow 

The routing and approval structure that 

determines how invoices move through review 

and approval before posting. 

A/R Batch 

A group of A/R transactions—such as charges, 

receipts, or adjustments—entered and posted 

together. 

Account balance 

The total amount recorded in a G/L account for a 

given period, including beginning balance, 

activity, and ending balance. 

Account grouping 

A structure used in financial reports to organize 

G/L accounts into meaningful categories such as 

assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. 

Predefined or custom groupings of G/L accounts 

used for reporting, dashboards, and financial 

analysis. 

Account type 

A classification that determines how an account 

behaves in financial statements (Asset, Liability, 

Equity, Revenue, Expense). 

Accounting period 

Transactions are recorded and separated into 

different reporting periods such as months, 

quarters, and years. The use of reporting periods 

lets you compare past and present performance. 

Accounting reviewer 

A designated role responsible for reviewing and 

approving accounting-related transactions 

before they are posted. 

Accounts 

An account keeps track of what your company 

owns, owes, spends, or receives. Separate 

accounts let you keep separate records for each 

type of asset, liability, equity, revenue, and 

expense. 

Each account can contain several subaccounts, 

which helps organize and manage your finances. 

Each account tracks the activity of its category. 

For example, the Receivables account tracks 

money coming in and the Payables account 

tracks money going out. Each of these accounts 

typically has many subaccounts. For example, the 

Receivables account may have a subaccount for 

each property: 

1201.001 - Accounts Receivable - Fair Haven 

1201.002 - Accounts Receivable - Coconut Grove 

Glossary of Terms

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Each account has a beginning balance. You 

record the increases and decreases for a period, 

and at the end of the period, you have the 

resulting ending balance. 

Accrual accounting 

The accrual method of accounting recognizes 

income in the period earned, and expenses in 

the period incurred. The accrual method is a 

better measure of profit and loss. 

Accrued Expenses report 

A report showing expenses that have been 

incurred but not yet paid, used during close to 

validate balances. 

Accumulated depreciation account 

The G/L account credited when depreciation is 

posted. It offsets the asset’s cost on the balance 

sheet. 

Action card 

A dashboard component that provides quick 

access buttons for common tasks or navigation 

shortcuts. 

Actuals 

Financial results of activity in the general ledger 

and used as the baseline for forecasts and 

budgets. 

Adjustment 

A manual increase or decrease to a customer’s or 

vendor’s balance, used to correct errors or apply 

special credits/charges. 

Adjustment codes 

Predefined codes used to categorize manual 

increases or decreases to a customer’s balance. 

Aging buckets 

Time based categories (e.g., 0–30, 31–60 days) 

used to group outstanding receivables or 

payables for reporting. 

Aging report 

A report that groups outstanding balances (A/P 

or A/R) by how long they have been unpaid (e.g., 

0–30, 31–60 days). 

Allocation 

A process that distributes amounts from one 

account or entity to others based on predefined 

rules or percentages. 

Allocation (Expense Reports) 

A method of distributing an expense across 

multiple projects, tasks, or locations. 

Approval levels 

The hierarchy of users or roles authorized to 

approve invoices based on amount, vendor, or 

other criteria.  

The number of approvers required for a role 

(1–4) when that role is assigned to an approval 

policy. 

Approval policy 

A rule that determines which users or roles are 

authorized to approve a transaction based on 

criteria such as amount, vendor, G/L account, 

job, or payment method.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Approval policy manager 

The page in the Company application used to 

create, edit, and organize approval policies. 

Approval queue 

The list of transactions awaiting approval, 

displayed in the Approval Workbench. 

Approval workbench 

An approval workbench is where users review, 

approve, and decline pending transactions. 

Approval workflow 

The routing process that determines who must 

review and approve a transaction before it can 

be posted or paid. A collection of approval 

policies are applied to specific transaction types 

and properties. 

Approver 

An approver is a person responsible for deciding 

to approve or decline a transaction. There are 

three types of approvers: 

• 
General approvers can approve or decline 

only transactions assigned to them or their 

role. 

• 
Unrestricted approvers can approve or 

decline any transaction. 

• 
Delegate approvers can approve or decline 

transactions assigned to another approver. 

Approver permissions 

The system permissions required to create 

approval policies or approve transactions. 

Asset account 

The G/L account representing the asset’s cost. 

Used when posting depreciation and disposal 

entries. 

Asset Activity report 

A report showing additions, disposals, transfers, 

and depreciation activity for selected assets. 

Asset class 

A category of assets that share the same 

depreciation rules and G/L account structure. 

Determines how depreciation is calculated and 

posted. 

Asset Disposal report 

A report showing assets that have been disposed 

of, including gain/loss calculations. 

Asset List report 

A report showing basic asset details such as cost, 

location, class, and placed in service date. 

Asset Reconciliation report 

A report comparing fixed asset balances to G/L 

balances to identify discrepancies. 

Assets 

The tangible and intangible items used in the 

operation of a business. Tangible assets include 

buildings, equipment, and vehicles. Intangible 

assets include the company’s bank account 

balance and A/R invoices representing future 

income from customers. Assets are tracked 

through acquisition, depreciation, transfer, and 

disposal.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Assumptions 

User defined variables—such as inflation rates, 

occupancy targets, or expense growth—that 

drive forecast calculations. 

Attachments 

An attachment is a bundle of one or more 

supporting documents, such as spreadsheets, 

scanned images, or word processor documents. 

Audit trail 

A system record showing changes made to 

transactions or records, including who made the 

change and when. 

Bank account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the bank account used. 

Bank accounts 

Financial accounts set up in the system for 

issuing payments, recording deposits, 

withdrawals, and performing reconciliations. 

Bank feed 

An automated connection that imports bank 

transactions into reconciliation for matching and 

reconciliation. 

Bank reconciliation 

The process of matching bank activity to general 

ledger transactions to ensure the bank balance 

and book balance agree. 

Bank register 

A chronological list of all transactions recorded 

in a bank account within the system. 

Baseline forecast 

The initial forecast generated from actuals and 

default assumptions before adjustments or 

scenario modeling. 

Batch 

A group of journal entries entered and posted 

together as a single unit. 

Batch report 

A report that displays all transactions included in 

a specific batch, such as A/P invoices or journal 

entries. 

Beginning balance 

The starting balance of a G/L account at the 

beginning of a fiscal period. 

Billable time 

Hours worked on a project that can be invoiced 

to a customer. The Billable Time page allows 

users to generate invoices for approved billable 

hours. 

Book balance 

The balance of a bank account according to the 

general ledger. It can also be the balance from 

the general ledger of a default general ledger 

account set on the bank account. 

Bookmarks / favorites 

User-defined shortcuts to frequently accessed 

pages or modules. 

Books closed 

The state indicating that the accounting period 

has been finalized for a property.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Budget 

A financial plan for a future period that outlines 

expected revenue, expenses, and cash flow. In 

Job Cost, a budget is an estimate of expected 

costs for a job. 

Budget version 

A saved iteration of a budget or forecast, 

allowing comparison between drafts, scenarios, 

or approval stages. 

BVA 

Budget Variance Analysis is an analysis of the 

difference between the amount that you 

budgeted for and the actual amount that you 

spent. 

Calculation model 

The logic used to compute forecasted values, 

such as percentage growth, fixed amounts, or 

driver based formulas. 

Cash accounting 

The cash method of accounting recognizes 

revenue in the same reporting period as the cash 

is received, and expenses in the period in which 

cash payments are made. 

Cash flow forecast 

A projection of expected cash inflows and 

outflows over a defined period. 

Certification / skill 

A credential, license, or skill tracked for an 

employee. Users can add, edit, or delete 

certifications and skills in their profile. 

Charge 

A receivable posted to a customer or tenant 

account for rent, fees, utilities, or other billable 

items. 

Charge schedule 

A configuration that defines when recurring 

charges generate, such as monthly rent cycles. 

Chart of accounts (COA) 

The structured list of G/L accounts used to 

categorize financial transactions. 

Check layout 

The format and design used when printing 

checks, including alignment, fields, and MICR line 

settings. 

Check run 

A batch process that selects, reviews, and prints 

multiple vendor payments at once. 

Child location 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, properties are 

called locations. Subproperties are called child 

locations. 

An entity represents the corporate office of one 

or more locations, responsible for locations’ 

taxes. Every location is associated with an entity. 

An entity can be responsible for one location or 

a large group of locations and child locations.  

A company can be composed of one entity or 

multiple entities. See also Multi-entity companies 

(on page 655).

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cleared transaction 

A payment or deposit that has been matched to 

bank activity during reconciliation. 

Cloned dashboard 

A duplicate of an existing dashboard that can be 

edited independently. 

Close account 

A close account is a G/L account used to track 

job completion. 

Close checklist 

A list of tasks required to complete the financial 

close for a period. Can be generated 

automatically or manually. 

Close console 

A centralized page for managing close activities, 

including generating checklists, opening/closing 

books, and viewing charts. 

Close workbench 

A workspace that displays close tasks, checklists, 

and work paper actions for selected properties. 

Closing period 

The process of finalizing a fiscal period so no 

additional transactions can be posted. 

Coding 

Assigning G/L accounts, properties, entities, and 

other classifications to an invoice or credit. 

Commitment 

A commitment, or purchase order, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount. 

Component 

An individual element displayed on a dashboard, 

such as a chart, list, report, performance card, 

calendar, or smartlink. 

Component controls 

The actions available on each dashboard 

component, such as edit, delete, expand, 

collapse, or move. 

Component group 

A collection of dashboard components grouped 

together for organization or layout purposes. 

Component permissions 

Permissions required to view the underlying data 

of a dashboard component. Users must have 

access to the data source (e.g., A/P invoices, G/L 

accounts) to see the component. 

Concession 

A concession is a negative charge awarded to 

the customer as a short-term incentive. Examples 

of concessions include waived fees, reduced rent, 

nuisance discounts, and renovation credits.  

Console page 

A dashboard style page showing close status, 

charts, and tools for generating checklists and 

managing books.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Consolidation 

Combining financial data from multiple entities 

into a single set of financial statements. 

Contra accounts 

A contra account is an account which offsets and 

reduces or offsets the balance of another 

account. You can have contra accounts for both 

assets and liabilities. 

A contra asset account has a credit balance and 

offsets and decreases the debit balance of the 

related asset account. An example of a 

contra-asset account is Accumulated 

Depreciation Autos & Vehicles account, which 

reduces the Automobiles & Vehicles account to 

arrive at the net value. 

A contra-liability account has a debit balance 

and offsets and decreases the credit balance of 

the related liability account. 

Cost code 

A cost code is a way to track a specific cost 

based on nature or function. 

Cost code policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific cost code. 

Cost coding 

Cost coding is a method of grouping individual 

costs based on their nature, function, or work 

phase. 

Credit memo 

A credit memo increases the overall amount you 

owe a vendor. It is typically a vendor-issued 

document that reduces the amount owed on an 

invoice. 

Custom field 

A user-defined field added to records or 

transactions to capture additional data not 

included in standard RealPage fields. 

Custom field wizard 

The guided tool used to create new custom 

fields, define field types, and configure visibility. 

Custom report 

A user built report that pulls data from Financial 

Suite records, transactions, and custom fields, 

allowing flexible filtering, grouping, and 

calculations. 

Custom report wizard 

A step-by-step tool for building custom reports, 

including selecting data sources, defining 

columns, adding filters, grouping, and setting 

prompts. 

Custom view 

A personalized list view that displays selected 

columns, filters, and sorting for any application’s 

list pages. 

Customer / tenant ledger 

A detailed record of all charges, payments, 

adjustments, and balances for a specific 

customer or tenant. 

Dashboard 

A workspace where users can pin frequently 

used reports for quick access, and display

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

business insights using components such as 

charts, KPIs, lists, and reports. 

Dashboard library 

A collection of prebuilt dashboards available for 

installation, typically provided when a company 

is created using a QuickStart template. 

Data import wizard 

A tool used to import data such as vendors, 

customers, G/L accounts, or transactions into the 

Financial Suite. 

Data mapping 

The process of aligning fields in your import file 

with the corresponding fields in the Financial 

Suite so the system knows where each value 

belongs. 

Data source (primary data source) 

The record or transaction type selected as the 

foundation for a report (e.g., Customer, A/P 

Invoice Detail, G/L entry). 

Data template 

A predefined spreadsheet or CSV layout 

provided by RealPage that specifies the required 

columns and formatting for a successful import. 

Debit memo 

A debit memo decreases the overall amount you 

owe that vendor. 

For example, if you receive a credit memo from a 

vendor, enter it as a debit memo to reduce the 

amount you owe that vendor. 

Debits and credits 

In common use, credit generally has positive 

associations; in accounting, credit is associated 

with decreases in asset, expense, and equity 

accounts. 

Debits increase balances in asset and expense 

accounts and decrease balances in liability 

accounts, revenue accounts, and capital 

accounts. 

Credits increase balances in liability, revenue, 

and capital accounts, and decrease balances in 

asset and expense accounts. 

Debit accounts are asset and expense accounts 

that usually have debit balances; the total debits 

usually exceed the total credits in each debit 

account. 

Credit accounts are revenue (income, gains) 

accounts and liability accounts that usually have 

credit balances. 

Declining balance (100/150/200) 

A depreciation method that accelerates 

depreciation by applying a percentage to the 

asset’s remaining book value. 

Default dashboard 

The dashboard automatically displayed when a 

user logs in. 

Default settings 

Predefined values that automatically populate 

fields when creating records, such as default G/L 

accounts or payment terms (A/P), or default 

charge codes or payment application rules (A/R).

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Delegate 

The approver who assumes your responsibility 

for approving transactions while you are out of 

the office. Any approvals that have been 

delegated while you are out of the office remain 

with your delegate, even if you turn off the 

out-of-office notification before the delegate has 

approved or declined the transaction. 

Deposit 

Funds received and recorded in a bank account, 

often grouped into a deposit batch for posting. 

Deposit batch 

A group of deposits entered and posted 

together. 

Depreciation batch 

A batch of depreciation journal entries generated 

for a period. Can be posted, viewed, or deleted. 

Depreciation expense account 

The G/L account debited when depreciation is 

posted. 

Depreciation journal entry 

The G/L entry created when depreciation is 

posted, debiting expense and crediting 

accumulated depreciation. 

Depreciation schedule 

The system generated schedule showing 

depreciation amounts for each period over the 

asset’s useful life. 

Depreciation schedules (financial vs. 
tax) 

Separate schedules that allow different 

depreciation rules for GAAP and tax reporting. 

Detail data source 

A data source option that includes both header 

and line item information for transactions (e.g., 

A/P Invoice Detail). 

Detail ledger 

A record showing all transactions posted to a 

specific G/L account. 

Detail report 

A report that includes line item or transaction 

level information rather than summarized totals. 

Dimension report structures 

Dimension report structures are named 

structures that you can create for the purpose of 

adding custom analysis to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. You can add dimension 

structures for any dimension that you have in 

your company. 

Disbursement 

Any outgoing cash transaction, such as checks, 

ACH payments, or manual payments. 

Document template 

A customizable Word-based template used for 

printed documents such as invoices, statements, 

sales orders, and purchase orders.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Document type 

The category of document associated with a 

report, such as invoices, statements, or purchase 

orders. 

Draft asset 

An asset imported from an external system that 

has not yet been activated. 

Draft expense report 

An expense report that has been created but not 

yet submitted for approval. 

Draw 

In Job Cost & Reserves, a draw summarizes 

invoiced costs by combining job activity into 

predetermined categories. After it’s summarized, 

you can provide the draw to the funding sources 

of the job. 

Draw model 

A draw model is an agreement between a lender 

and your company that lists the budgeted items 

approved for funds. 

Driver 

A variable that influences forecasted values (e.g., 

occupancy, rent growth, utility usage). 

Due date 

The date by which a vendor invoice must be 

paid. 

eInvoice 

A system-generated A/P invoice created by 

Spend Management Storefront. 

Entity 

An entity record contains a property’s or 

location’s accounting and legal details, such as 

the business name and address as they should 

appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and tax 

forms. An entity contains the accounting 

information of a location/property or property 

management company. 

In a multi-entity environment, entities are 

distinct—but nearly identical—companies or 

business units that are fully owned by a 

corporate or headquarters entity. Entities can 

represent divisions managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized 

payables and receivables and a common chart of 

accounts. 

Exception 

A transaction that does not match bank activity 

during reconciliation and requires review or 

correction. 

Expense report 

A form used to record reimbursable expenses. 

Users can add receipts, allocate expenses, and 

submit for approval. 

FAS 

A final account statement (FAS) is a document 

that provides a detailed record of a transaction’s 

activity. 

Filter 

Criteria applied to limit which records appear in 

a report.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Final work paper package 

The completed, approved set of work papers for 

a period, locked after approval. 

Fiscal calendar 

The structure of accounting periods and fiscal 

years used for reporting and posting. 

Forecast 

A forward looking projection of financial 

performance based on actuals, assumptions, and 

drivers. 

Forecast cycle 

The defined period for creating, reviewing, and 

finalizing forecasts (monthly, quarterly, annually). 

Funding source 

A funding source is a lender for a job. 

G/L account (general ledger account) 

A financial account used to categorize 

transactions for reporting and posting. A G/L 

account is associated with each charge or 

payment. 

G/L account group 

A predefined group of G/L accounts that can be 

selected instead of individual account ranges. 

G/L account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific G/L account or 

account range. 

G/L group 

A collection of G/L accounts grouped for 

reporting, allocations, or approval routing. 

Global (top level) setup 

Configuration performed at the top level that 

applies to all entities in the portfolio. 

Home page 

The landing page provides quick access to 

dashboards, tasks, and frequently used modules. 

Import log 

A system-generated record that shows which 

rows were imported successfully and which 

failed, including error messages. 

Initial posting date 

Revaluation reports help you manage 

unrecognized gains and losses from the 

fluctuation in exchange rates. Set the initial 

posting date on this report as the end of the 

month. 

Injection (smart rules / smart events) 

A dynamic value inserted into a rule or event 

action, such as a field value, date, or user 

information. 

Interim financing 

Interim financing, or construction loan, is a 

deployment of capital for short-term 

development, such as the acquisition and 

renovation of properties. This capital is typically 

provided by a lender.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

When the project is complete, owners pay the 

construction loan and replace it with permanent 

financing. 

In-transit item 

A transaction recorded in the system but not yet 

reflected on the bank statement (e.g., 

outstanding checks, deposits in transit). 

Invoice (A/P) 

A vendor’s bill for goods or services received. 

Invoice (A/R) 

A document generated to bill a customer for 

charges owed. In A/R, invoices may be created 

manually or automatically. 

Invoice entry 

The process of entering vendor invoices into the 

A/P module for approval and posting. 

Invoice matching 

The process of comparing an invoice to purchase 

orders, receipts, or expected amounts before 

approval. 

Invoice numbering rules 

Settings that determine how invoice numbers are 

validated, formatted, or restricted. 

Job 

A job is a method of tracking the work and 

expenses related to construction at a property. 

Jobs are used for job costing and approval 

routing. 

Job policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific job. 

Job type 

A classification of jobs used for approval policies 

and reporting. 

Job type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a job type. 

Journal entry 

A journal entry documents the movement of 

money. When you add a journal entry, you enter 

an accounting transaction into the records. Every 

journal entry must include at least two equal and 

offsetting entries. This is because every 

transaction involves a change in at least two 

places in the accounting records, and the total of 

all debits and credits must balance. 

Key performance indicator (KPI) 

A measurable metric used to evaluate financial 

or operational performance (e.g., NOI, occupancy 

rate). KPIs can be displayed on performance 

cards on a dashboard to show financial or 

operational performance. 

Late fee 

A charge applied when a customer fails to pay by 

the due date, based on configured rules. 

Late fee rules 

Configuration that determines when late fees 

apply, how they are calculated, and which charge 

codes they use.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Ledger 

The complete set of financial accounts used to 

record all transactions for an entity or portfolio. 

Line item 

An individual revenue or expense entry within a 

transaction such as an invoice, purchase order, 

budget or forecast. 

Loan schedule 

A loan schedule is a list of all payments 

previously paid (historical purposes only) or due 

to the lender for the loan. 

Lookup values 

Reference lists—such as vendors, charge codes, 

or account types—that must exist in the system 

before certain imports can succeed. 

Manual entry 

A bank transaction entered directly into the 

system rather than imported through a bank 

feed or processed by AI. 

Manual journal entry 

A journal entry created directly by a user rather 

than generated by a subsystem such as A/P or 

A/R. 

Matching 

The process of pairing bank activity with 

corresponding G/L transactions during 

reconciliation.  

M-console 

The M-console is the management console used 

by administrators to create and manage multiple 

RealPage Accounting Suite environments. 

M-console access is different from RealPage 

Accounting Suite system access. To access the 

M-console, you must have a separate account in 

the M-console. 

Most implementations of RealPage Accounting 

Suite do not need the M-console. 

Memorized report 

A saved version of a report with preset filters, 

parameters, and formatting for quick reuse. 

Merge field 

A placeholder inserted into a Word document 

template that pulls data from the Financial Suite 

when the document is generated. 

Monthly checklist 

A checklist used for monthly close activities. 

Multi year forecast 

A projection that spans multiple fiscal years, 

often used for long term planning. 

Multi-entity companies 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, a parent property 

is called a location, and a subproperty is called a 

child location. A location must have an entity 

associated with it. The entity handles the 

accounting and tax activities for its location and 

any child locations. 

In a multi-entity shared corporation, entities 

represent a separate tax identification or a 

separately secured, fully balancing set of books. 

Entities typically represent properties, or 

locations, which are managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Performance card 

A dashboard component that displays KPIs, 

trends, or financial metrics in a compact visual 

format. 

Period activity 

The total debits and credits posted to an account 

within a specific accounting period. 

Period close 

The workflow used to review, adjust, and finalize 

financial activity before closing an accounting 

period. 

Periodic tasks 

Recurring A/P activities performed on a regular 

schedule, such as check runs, recurring invoice 

generation, or reconciliation. 

Permission 

The rights required to view and work with data 

and access pages. 

A permission allows you to access a single 

function. When RealPage adds a new feature to a 

product, the feature often comes with new 

permissions that you must enable before users 

can use the new feature. The word “Right” and 

the word “Permission” refer to the same thing. 

When you use the Unified Platform, they are 

referred to as rights. When you set up access to 

functions in the Financial Suite, they are referred 

to as permissions.  

Permit 

A permit is a category that organizes job 

attachments by type or function. 

Placed in service date 

The date the asset begins being used. 

Depreciation starts based on this date. 

PO 

An abbreviation for purchase order (on page 

658). 

Policy type 

The category of rule used to determine approval 

routing (User, Amount, Tiered Amount, Vendor, 

Vendor Type, G/L Account, Job, Job Type, Cost 

Code, Accounting Reviewer, Journal Type, 

Payment Method, Bank Account). 

Positive Pay 

Positive pay is an automated service that the 

bank offers to help detect fraud by matching a 

company’s check with the check presented for 

payment.  

You can use the RealPage Financial Suite Positive 

Pay feature to generate a Positive Pay file and 

transmit the list of checks to the bank for review. 

The bank compares the amount, check number, 

and account number to ensure that they match. 

Non-matching checks are flagged and sent back 

to the check issuer for review. 

You can also configure the system to submit 

Positive Pay files on a schedule. When a schedule 

is configured, the system generates the Positive 

Pay files containing a list of checks on the 

scheduled dates and automatically sends them 

to the bank. 

Posting 

The action that finalizes a transaction and 

records it in the general ledger.

When you post a transaction, you are

posted to the general ledger, including batch 

behavior and posting dates.

formatting or data issues before the actual 

import runs.

Project

entries and expenses. Projects must be created 

before they can be used in timesheets. 

Project type 

A classification used to group projects for 

reporting and setup. 

Prompts 

User input fields added to a custom report to 

allow filtering at runtime. 

Properties (entities) 

Individual business units or properties whose 

financial activity is tracked separately. 

PTO (paid time off) 

Time away from work that can be requested and 

approved through the Time & Resources 

application. 

PTO approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline PTO requests. 

PTO request 

A request submitted by an employee for paid 

time off. 

PTO types 

Administrator-defined categories of PTO, such as 

vacation, sick leave, or personal time. 

Punchout vendor 

Punchout refers to a digital system in which a 

vendor allows customers to browse his product 

catalogs online and then purchase goods or 

services within the client’s e-procurement 

system. 

Purchase order 

A purchase order, or commitment, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount.

Financial Suite, “receipt” and “payment” are often 

used interchangeably. 

Reclassification (asset) 

Changing the G/L account or asset class 

associated with an asset. 

Reconciliation date 

The date through which the bank account is 

being reconciled. 

Reconciliation workbench 

The tool used to match bank activity with G/L 

transactions and complete bank reconciliations. 

You can match, review, and clear bank 

transactions during the reconciliation process. 

Record 

Any data object in the Financial Suite, such as 

Customer, Vendor, G/L Account, or Invoice. 

Recurring charge (property 
management) 

A charge that is automatically generated on a 

schedule (e.g., monthly rent or recurring fees). 

Also called recurring invoice. 

Recurring invoice (accounting) 

An invoice template that automatically generates 

new invoices on a set schedule. 

Recurring journal entry 

A journal entry template that automatically 

generates entries on a defined schedule. 

Refresh 

The action that reloads a page’s data to reflect 

the most recent system updates. 

REIT 

Real Estate Investment Trust 

REMIC 

Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit 

Report audience 

A report audience is an audience assigned to a 

report in order to designate who the report is 

intended to be viewed by or addressed to. By 

assigning a report audience to a report, you can 

filter the list of reports by audience type later. 

Report center 

The central hub where users browse, run, create, 

and manage reports. 

Report column 

A vertical section in a report that displays one 

specific type of information, such as dates, 

amounts, or statuses.

Revaluate 

An adjustment to a country’s official exchange

Revenue account 

The G/L account associated with a charge code, 

used to classify revenue in financial reporting. 

Reversal 

A journal entry created to negate a previous

Rights 

A right allows you to access a single function. 

When RealPage adds a new feature to a product, 

the feature often comes with new rights that you 

must enable before users can use the new 

feature. The word “Right” and the word 

“Permission” refer to the same thing. When you 

use the Unified Platform, they are referred to as 

rights. When you set up access to functions in 

the Financial Suite, they are referred to as 

permissions.  

Role 

A group of users who share permissions and 

responsibilities; roles can be assigned as 

approvers. Roles are assigned to users to control 

access to modules and actions. 

RPA 

An abbreviation for RealPage Accounting. 

Segments 

A component used to categorize financial data 

(e.g., entity, department, account). 

You can use segments to organize, sort, and 

report on your company information in 

meaningful ways. It is a type of tag with a set of 

values, which you can associate with transactions 

and G/L entries. 

Sequences 

Document sequences refer to the system’s 

automatic document numbering feature used to 

assign unique identifiers to new records. This 

helps ensure consistency and avoids duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document 

sequencing, is available only for select 

transactions and records in RealPage 

Accounting. Document sequencing uses 

pre-defined numbering plans to assign 

sequential identifiers to new records or 

transactions, such as customer records or A/R 

invoices. Document sequencing is a two-step 

process. First, you configure the numbering 

scheme, then you assign the scheme to the type 

of record or transaction.  

Service charge 

A bank fee recorded during reconciliation to 

adjust the book balance. 

Setup 

The Setup tab appears at the top of most menu 

panes. Click it to display the menu items 

available to you based on your subscriptions, 

user permissions, and admin privileges. If the

Site Experience 

The Site Experience is a scaled-down version of 

Spend Management in a simplified interface. 

While the Spend Management application in the 

RealPage Financial Suite offers more robust 

functionality, most users can accomplish their 

procurement-to-payment processes from the 

Site Experience. 

The Site View option opens Site Experience. The 

Site View menu option is available in the Spend 

Management, General Ledger, and Accounts 

Payable application menus. 

Smart event 

An automation that triggers an action—such as 

sending an email, making an API call, or posting 

an HTTP request—when conditions are met. 

Smart rule 

A rule that triggers warnings or errors to guide 

user behavior when certain conditions are met. 

Smartlink 

A dashboard component that provides a 

clickable link to another page, report, or 

application. 

Source entity 

The paying entity. The entity that is the source of 

the money in a transaction between two or more 

entities. 

Splits 

A line within a transaction that records the 

account and amount of money involved is called 

a split. 

Spread method (budgeting) 

The rule used to distribute annual amounts 

across months (e.g., evenly, seasonally, 

driver-based). 

Staff expenses 

Expense reports created on behalf of staff 

members by administrators or managers. 

Staff timesheets 

Timesheets created or managed by supervisors 

for their staff. 

Standard report 

A pre-built Financial Suite report that cannot be 

modified but can be exported or memorized. 

Statement 

A statement, or Statement of Account, is 

essentially a report. It’s a snapshot that includes 

all open and unapplied transactions at the time 

the snapshot was taken—usually at the end of a 

period. 

Statement balance 

The ending balance shown on the bank 

statement for the reconciliation period. 

Straight line depreciation 

A depreciation method that spreads the asset’s 

cost evenly over its useful life.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Subledger 

A subledger is a ledger containing all of one kind 

of transaction. For example, a subledger may 

contain all accounts receivable transactions, or 

accounts payable transactions, or fixed asset 

transactions. All transactions in all subledgers roll 

up into the general ledger. 

Submitted (timesheet status) 

Indicates that a timesheet has been submitted 

and is awaiting approval. 

Sum of years digits (SYD) 

An accelerated depreciation method that applies 

a decreasing fraction of the asset’s cost each 

year. 

Summary 

Summaries are collections of the same type of 

transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, 

no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either open or closed. When 

summaries are open in Accounts Receivable, you 

can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits. In 

designing an accounts receivable process, the 

system administrator can give access to the 

pages involved with managing invoices but not 

opening or closing summaries. 

Summary report 

A high level report that aggregates data without 

showing line item detail. 

Suspense account 

A temporary account used to hold transactions 

that require review or correction. 

System journal 

A system journal is a journal that is used by the 

system. Users can designate a journal as a 

system journal. Users cannot add journal entries 

to system journals, and system journals are 

excluded from appearing in manual journals 

drop-down lists. 

Target (budgeting) 

A predefined financial goal used to guide 

budgeting or forecasting (e.g., NOI target, 

expense cap). 

Task (Financial Close Management) 

An individual close activity, such as reconciling a 

subledger or reviewing a report. 

Task (Time & Resources application) 

A specific activity within a project. Tasks must be 

created before they can be selected on 

timesheets. 

Template version (importing) 

The specific RealPage-approved layout for an 

import file. Using an outdated version can cause 

errors. 

Tenant / customer 

The individual or organization responsible for 

paying charges recorded in A/R. 

Three-way tie 

A reconciliation requirement ensuring that the 

bank balance, book balance, and cleared balance 

all match.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Cash Management User Guide 

Tiered amount policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions 

through multiple approval tiers based on 

increasing amount ranges. 

TIH 

Trust Interest Holder 

Time approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline submitted timesheets. 

Timesheet 

A weekly record of hours worked on projects and 

tasks. Users can add comments, submit for 

approval, and track status. 

Timesheet periods 

Defined weekly or biweekly periods used for 

time entry. Administrators open and close 

periods as needed. 

Tolerance percentage 

The allowable variance between an invoice and 

the expected amount before manual approval is 

required. 

Transaction date 

The date the A/R activity occurred, which 

determines how it appears in aging and 

reporting. 

Transaction detail 

Line-level information associated with a 

transaction, such as invoice items or journal 

entry lines. 

Transaction type 

The category of transaction, such as invoices, 

journal entries, or payments. 

Transactions 

A transaction represents money flowing from 

one account to another. Whenever you spend or 

receive money, or transfer money from one 

account to another, it is represented as a 

transaction. 

In double-entry accounting, transactions always 

involve at least two accounts—a source account 

and a destination account. 

Transfer 

A movement of funds between two bank 

accounts within the system. 

Transfer (asset transfer) 

Moving an asset from one location, entity, or 

department to another. 

Trial balance 

A report showing all G/L accounts with 

beginning balances, period activity, and ending 

balances. 

Unapplied payment 

A payment that has been received but not yet 

applied to specific charges. 

Unapplied payment handling 

Rules that determine how payments are stored 

when they cannot be matched to specific 

charges.

Unapproving (Expense report)

Uncleared transaction

Unit

Unposted batch

development. 

Work paper

reconciles all subaccounts of an accounting 

category for auditing purposes. Work papers can 

also be used for preparing financial statements. 

Work paper package 

A compiled set of work papers, attachments, and 

supporting documents for a period.
