About Cash Management

Use the Cash Management application to manage corporate
cash accounts—including checking, savings, and credit card
accounts—from a central location. As a cloud-based
application, users can work cooperatively regardless of their
geographic location. For example, even if your headquarters
are in the East, regional offices in other global areas can enter
their own credit card transactions and reconcile them.

Adding a Bank Account

Enter details about your bank account, map journals and other
accounts, and define how you want to print checks and pay
your vendors.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Bank accounts.
3. On the Details tab, fill in the required bank and account details.
4. On the Check printing tab, choose how you want to print
checks.
5. Optionally, on the ACH setup tab (or the Electronic payments
setup tab), enable ACH or electronic payments for the account.

The Electronic payments setup tab appears only if your
company has enabled foreign electronic payments on the
Configure Cash Management page.

6. If enabled, set up your ACH or electronic payments and
payment numbering sequences.
7. Click Save.

Adding a Credit Card Account

Create a credit card account to enter credit card or debit card
information.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Credit card.
3. Fill in the credit card details and account preferences.
4. Click Save.

Adding a Deposit

Create a deposit after receiving payments into an undeposited
funds account to reflect the transfer of funds.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Deposits.
3. Select Filters to display undeposited funds.
4. Click Continue.
5. Fill in the Deposit details.
6. Select the transactions you want to create deposit slips for.
7. Click Save.

Transferring Funds

Move funds from one bank account to another.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Funds transfer.
3. Select a From account (source account) and To account
(receiving account).
4. Type or select the Date to transfer funds.
5. Type the Amount to transfer.
6. In the Reference number field, type the transaction number.
7. Type a Description for the funds transfer.
8. Select an Attachment.
9. Select a Department and Location to associate with the
transfer.
10. Click Save.

Reversing a Deposit or Transfer

Correct a deposit or transfer by reversing it.

1. In Cash Management, in the Reports section of the menu,
select Registers, and then select Bank.
2. Select the report's parameters, and then click View.
3. Find the deposit or transfer you want to reverse, and then click
Reverse.
4. Type the date and explanation.
5. Click Submit.

Adding a Manual Payment

Use the manual payment option to quickly add a bill and record
the payment at the same time.

1. In Cash Management, select the All tab.

2. Select 
 Manual payment.
3. Select the Payment method.
4. Select the Bank or Credit card account from which you will
draw the payment.
5. Type or select the payment Date.
6. Select the Vendor receiving the payment.
7. Type the Transaction amount.
8. Type the Check # or Document number.
9. Select the Pay to vendor or recipient.
10. Type the A/P invoice number.
11. Optionally, type a Memo and select an Attachment.
12. In the Entries section, fill in the payment line items.

You must specify at least an Account and Amount.

13. Click Save & confirm to post the payment.

Generating a Payment File

Generate the ACH or electronic payment file that contains the
payments you want to make.

1. In Accounts Payable or Cash Management, click the All tab.
2. In the ACH or Electronic payments section, select ACH file
generation or File generation.
3. Select the payment requests you want to send to the bank for
processing.
4. Click Generate file to generate a payment file for the selected
payments (one file per bank).
5. Send each payment file to its corresponding bank in their
preferred format.
6. After the bank receives the file and sends it to the vendor, click
Confirm.

Adding a Receipt

Miscellaneous revenue is revenue that cannot be booked in
Leasing & Rents. Other receipts are receipts that aren't
associated with either a customer or invoice.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Other receipts.
3. Type or select the Receipt date.
4. Type the name of the Payer.
5. Select the Payment method.
6. Type or select the Transaction date.
7. Type the Transaction number, such as the check number.
8. Type a Description for the receipt.
9. Select an Attachment.
10. Select whether to deposit the payment into a Bank account or
into Undeposited funds.

▪
For bank accounts, select the Account into which you want
to deposit the payment, and then select the Bank G/L
account and Deposit date.
▪
For undeposited funds, select the Account into which you
want to hold funds temporarily until you deposit them.

11. If the receipt is for a multi-currency transaction, fill in the
currency and exchange rate details.
12. In the Entries section, enter the line items for the receipt.
13. Click Save.

Adding a Credit Card Transaction

Record charges against your credit and debit cards.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Credit card transactions.
3. Select the Credit card account.
4. Type or select the Date of the transaction.
5. Type the Reference number from your statement.
6. Type the name of the Payee.
7. Type a Description of the transaction.
8. Select an Attachment.
9. In the Entries section, fill in each line item.

You must specify at least an Account and Amount.

10. Click Save.

Adding a Charge Payoff

Identify the charges that you want to pay before paying the
invoice in Accounts Payable.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Charge payoffs.
3. Select the Credit card account.
4. Click Continue.
5. Type or select the payoff Date.
6. Select an Attachment.
7. Select the transactions that you want to pay in full or enter an
Amount to pay partially.
8. Click Save.

Customizing and Running a Register Report

Make modifications to standard register reports by setting filters
and selecting formatting options.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.
2. In the Reports section, select Registers, and then select a
report option.
3. If applicable, select Reporting accounts.
4. Specify a Time period.
5. Set Filters.
6. Select Format settings.
7. Type Titles.
8. Click View.

Adding Bank Interest and Charges

Enter transaction charges and fees directly from the Cash
Management menu.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Bank interest and charges.
3. Select a Bank account.
4. Type or select the transaction Date.
5. Select a Transaction type:

▪
Service charge: Records the monthly charge.
▪
Interest earned: Records the interest.

6. Type the Reference number from your statement.
7. Type a Description of the transaction.
8. Select an Attachment.
9. For multi-currency transactions, fill in the currency and
exchange rate details.
10. In the Entries section, fill in each line item.

You must specify at least an Account and Amount.

11. Click Save.

Adding Credit Card Charges and Fees

Enter monthly interest charges or record credit card fees and
charges for late payments.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Credit card charges and fees.
3. Select a Credit card account.
4. Type or select the transaction Date.
5. Select a Transaction type:

▪
Finance charge: Records monthly interest charges.
▪
Other fees: Records a credit card fee or late payment
charge.

6. Type the Reference number from your statement.
7. Type a Description of the transaction.
8. Select an Attachment.
9. For multi-currency transactions, fill in the currency and
exchange rate details.
10. In the Entries section, fill in each line item.

You must specify at least an Account and Amount.

11. Click Save.

Reconciling a Bank Account

Make sure the monthly bank statement matches the accounting
system.

1. In Cash Management, select Bank in the Reconciliation
section.
2. Select the Account to reconcile.
3. Type or select the Statement ending date.
4. Type or select the Statement ending balance.
5. Select an Attachment.
6. Click Import.
7. Apply filters to narrow the list of transactions.
8. Select the items you want to match.
9. Click Match transactions.
10. When the Amount to reconcile is zero, click Reconcile.

If the Amount to reconcile is not zero, then you can create
adjusting entries.

Reconciling a Credit Card

Enter miscellaneous charges from your credit card statement
and check off cleared items to balance your account.

1. In Cash Management, click the All tab.
2. In the Reconciliation section, select Credit card.
3. Select the Credit card account to reconcile.
4. In the Beginning balance cut off date field, type or select the
date to begin reconciliation.

This is typically the day before the first day of the statement
period.

5. Type or select the Statement ending date.
6. In the Sort by drop-down list, select how you want to sort the
columns in the reconciliation list.
7. Select Charges and credits to group all of the charges together
and the credits together. Otherwise, select None.
8. Click Initial open items to add in-transit items or items that
were open as of the last reconciliation.
9. Import the initial open items from a CSV file.
10. Type the Ending credit card balance.
11. Rearrange the Book transaction columns as needed.
12. Select an Attachment.
13. Click Continue.
14. If you imported initial open items, clear the Compensating
initial open items entry check box.
15. Click Add charges and other fees to add any interest and
bank charges.
16. Select transactions to clear until Amount to reconcile equals 0.
17. Click Reconcile.

### Creating Reconciliation Rules
*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management QS.pdf`, Page 3*

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management QS.pdf`, Page 3*

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management QS.pdf`, Page 3*

*Source: `RP Accounting Cash Management QS.pdf`, Page 3*

Creating Reconciliation Rules

Set up reconciliation rules and pair them with rule sets to auto-
match transactions in RealPage Accounting to bank
transactions.
To add a rule:

1. On the Setup tab, under Reconciliation rules, select 
 Rule.
2. Enter basic details: Rule ID, Rule name, Description, Status.
3. Filter which transactions to apply the rule to:

▪
Select the transaction Data source, either RealPage or
Bank.
▪
Select the Field to filter transactions by.
▪
Select an Operator for the filter criteria.
▪
Type the Value to filter by.

4. Add additional filters as needed.
5. Select whether to group transactions by Document number or
Posting date.
6. Define the condition(s) that must be met to auto-match the
transactions:

▪
Select the Bank transaction field on which to base the
condition.
▪
Select an Operator for the matching condition.
▪
Type a Value to complete the expression.

7. Save the rule.

To add a rule to a rule set:

1. On the Setup tab, under Reconciliation rules, select 
 Rule
sets.
2. Enter basic details: ID, Name, Description, Status.
3. Select each Rule to include in the rule set, ordered by priority.
4. Select one or more bank accounts for the rule(s) to apply to.
5. Save the rule set.

Escheating Invoices

If a vendor or resident does not collect your payment, you can
initiate the escheatment process:

1. Select an Aged payable account on the Configure cash
management page to hold unclaimed funds.
2. Mark the invoice as an aged payable in the Escheatment
workbench. The system:

▪
Voids the original payment (if the invoice was paid).
▪
Creates a journal entry in the APJE journal to record the
transfer of funds to your Aged payable account.
▪
Changes the invoice status to Aged payable.

3. After you've transferred the funds to the state, mark the aged
payable as an escheated invoice.

Scheduling Positive Pay Files

Set up Positive Pay to generate or schedule positive pay files
and protect your company against fraudulent bank activity.

1. On the Setup tab, select 
 Positive pay configuration.
2. Define the required bank and file details:

▪
Type a Configuration name.
▪
Select a predefined bank Layout.
▪
In Effective date, type or select the earliest date to include
in the positive pay file.

3. Schedule the positive pay files:

▪
Type or select a Start date.
▪
Select an Ending on option.
▪
Type the Email to notify when a file generates.

4. Select the bank accounts to which Positive Pay applies.
5. Save the configuration.

Calculating a Location's Available Cash

Calculate and view a report of a location's available cash after
adjusting for any holdback amounts (future or anticipated
expenses).

1. Define the Available cash settings on the Configure cash
management page:

▪
Transfer requirements: Select the account you want to
transfer holdback amounts into and the journal in which to
record the transfer.
▪
Name captions: Define up to three custom text fields for
available cash locations.
▪
Summary options: Select whether to summarize cash,
A/P, and A/R accounts into a single line in the available
cash report.

2. Add one or more holdbacks based on actual, budgeted, or
manual amounts.
3. Add the location to the Available cash locations list:

▪
Select the Location.
▪
Fill in any custom fields (Name captions).
▪
Select the Cash, A/P, and A/R accounts or account groups
to use in the calculation.

4. View or Edit the available cash location to view a report of its
available cash.

▪
Edit manual holdback Amounts or Current reductions as
needed.
▪
Refresh the report data as needed.
▪
Print or Export the report as needed.

Bank Reconciliation Quick Help 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Bank Reconciliations 

If your bank reconciliation Amount to Reconcile is not zero, follow the steps below in order. Each 

step helps verify a common cause and explains what to do if something does not match. 

Step 1: Confirm the Beginning Balance 

Start by confirming that the Beginning Balance in the bank reconciliation matches the balance 

from the last completed reconciliation. 

If the beginning balance does not match, this usually means a transaction was posted to the bank 

GL account in a prior, already reconciled period. 

How to Resolve It 

• 
Reopen the bank reconciliation for the period where the entry was made. 

• 
Reconcile that period again so the beginning balance rolls forward correctly. 

How to Prevent This Going Forward 

• 
Make sure G/L books and subledger books are closed after completing a reconciliation to 

prevent changes in finalized periods. 

Step 2: Confirm the Statement Ending Date and Ending Balance 

Verify that the statement details match your bank statement. 

• 
Confirm the Statement Date in RealPage Accounting matches the statement date from your 

bank 

• 
Confirm the Ending Balance in RealPage Accounting matches the ending balance on the 

bank statement 

If either the date or ending balance does not match, the reconciliation will not zero out. 

Step 3: Compare the Book Balance to the G/L Balance 

Run a general ledger or trial balance report to ensure the Book Balance shown in the 

reconciliation matches the balance of the bank G/L account. 

How to Resolve It 

• 
If the balances do not match, then enter a support ticket as the Book balance shown in the 

reconciliation should always match the G/L account balance  

Step 4: Identify Missing Transactions 

Review both your bank statement and the reconciliation to ensure all transactions are accounted 

for. Every transaction on the bank statement should either appear in RealPage Accounting or be 

intentionally handled as a reconciling item. 

Every transaction in the reconciliation should either appear on the bank statement or remain 

unmatched appropriately. 

---



### FAQs
*Source: `Bank Reconciliation Quick Help.pdf`, Page 3*



### Summary
*Source: `Bank Reconciliation Quick Help.pdf`, Page 3*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Bank Reconciliation Quick Help 

If a transaction appears on the bank statement but will post to the GL in a future period (for 

example, due to a month-end cutoff), then  

• 
Open the reconciliation and navigate to More actions > Add bank transaction. 

• 
Enter the transactions details and save. 

• 
The transactions will appear in the Bank section at the bottom of the reconciliation page. 

• 
On that transaction, click Actions > Reconciling. 

Marking the transaction as reconciling indicates it will post to the G/L later and will reduce the 

Amount to Reconcile. 

If a transaction appears on the bank reconciliation but not in your statement, then that 

transaction should be left as unmatched. 

FAQs 

1. 
Where do the Difference and Uncleared amounts come from? 

The Uncleared Amount represents the total of all G/L transactions in the reconciliation that 

have not yet been matched to a bank transaction. The Difference is calculated as the 

difference between the Book Balance and the Ending Balance after reconciling items are 

applied. Together, these values determine the Amount to Reconcile, which should be zero 

when all balances and transactions are accounted for correctly. 

2. 
What is the AUTO ENTRY for? 

The AUTO ENTRY appears only on the first bank reconciliation. It represents the beginning 

balance of the G/L account based on the beginning balance cutoff date. This entry is not an 

additional posting to the G/L; it is simply a placeholder the system uses to establish the 

starting balance. Because the system assumes the reconciliation starts at zero, the AUTO 

ENTRY must be cleared on the first reconciliation to bring the Amount to Reconcile down. 

3. 
What is the AUTO CONTRA entry? 

The AUTO CONTRA entry also appears on the first reconciliation and represents the net 

debits and credits created as initial open items when the account is first set up for 

reconciliation. This entry should always be matched during the first reconciliation and 

should not remain uncleared. 

Summary 

If your Amount to Reconcile is not zero: 

• 
Confirm the beginning balance 

• 
Verify the statement date and ending balance 

• 
Ensure the book balance matches the G/L balance 

• 
Review for missing, unmatched, or timing-related transactions
